ap-book-open.formula: CO_ADJ_OPEN, read off any single row. Broadcast company total = SUM(B0..B6) OVER (). Equals CO_RAW_OPEN - SUM(CREDIT_APPLIED) and equals ap-trade-open + ap-group-open.
ap-book-open.label: Whole-book credit-adjusted payable (trade + group)
section_traps: CO_* columns are BROADCAST company totals repeated identically on every row (verified across all 644/88/164 rows). Summing CO_ADJ_OPEN_TRADE down Oil's table gives Rs 14,604 Cr instead of Rs 22.68 Cr. Read any CO_* off a single row; never aggregate it.

Summing ADJ_OPEN over ALL rows gives Oil Rs 102.51 Cr, not Rs 22.68 Cr. 78% of Oil's aged book, 95% of Mart's and 36% of Bev's is JIVO's own branch and intercompany cards. The filter ACCT_KIND == 'TRADE' (or IS_EXCLUDED == 0) is mandatory on every trade figure.

Row count is not party count. Oil has 635 TRADE cards but only 256 owe anything; 170 hold an advance and 154 rows of the whole book are nil on both sides. v1's KPI subtitle counts rows and overstates exposure ~2.5x - the SQL header says so at lines 11-13 and the renderer ignores it.

RAW_OPEN is not a payable. On Oil's trade book it is Rs 223.92 Cr against Rs 22.68 Cr = 9.87x. The '~3x' figure quoted in README.md and in the SQL header is the WHOLE-BOOK ratio (Oil 3.03x, Mart 7.52x, Bev 1.63x) and understates the distortion on the number the board actually shows.

UNAPPLIED_PAY (OVPM.OpenBal) and OPEN_CN (open ORPC) are diagnostics and are ALREADY inside the ledger balance. Subtracting either double-counts. Oil's CO_UNAPPLIED_PAY is Rs 2,017.71 Cr against a Rs 103.20 Cr real payable, and 8,355 of Oil's 9,038 uncancelled supplier payments carry a non-zero OpenBal - at JIVO 'OpenBal' means never internally reconciled, not money still unspent.

DAYS_OLDEST and OLDEST_DUE are PRE-CREDIT: the oldest open bill on the card, before the ledger credit was consumed against it. 226 Oil trade cards report a DAYS_OLDEST while owing Rs 0, and Oil's 3,189-day maximum (VENDA001047 BLESSING ADVERTISING) has its surviving Rs 26.26 L bucketed at 61-90 and 91-180 days, not 365+. 16 Oil cards worth Rs 0.31 Cr and 3 Mart cards worth Rs 1.05 Cr have DAYS_OLDEST over 365 with B6_365PLUS = 0.
ADJ_OVERDUE_60PLUS is B3+B4+B5+B6, i.e. 61 days and over - the name rounds to 60 and is wrong. Label it '61 d +'. It was deliberately not renamed because v1's hero hardcodes the key.

There is no STAFF class in this section, unlike open-item-list. 82 Oil / 24 Mart / 22 Bev employee imprest cards (VENDOR_GROUP = 'STAFF VENDOR', CARD_CODE prefix ORGV) are scored TRADE here and STAFF there - 18/6/5 direct disagreements on the cards both sections carry. The money is small (Oil Rs 0.011 Cr ADJ_OPEN and Rs 0.227 Cr of advances, Bev Rs 0.047 Cr) but two ORGV cards sit inside Bev's top 10 payables, so a 'top external suppliers' chart will print employee names unless it filters VENDOR_GROUP != 'STAFF VENDOR'. This matters beyond the charts: CONTRACT.md §2 defines data/parties.<company>.json with kind in TRADE|BRANCH|INTERCO|STAFF, so the party index must NOT take a vendor's kind from this section's ACCT_KIND - it would emit zero STAFF vendors. Take it from open-item-list.ACCT_KIND, or re-derive STAFF from VENDOR_GROUP == 'STAFF VENDOR'.

ACCT_KIND is a name-and-group heuristic, not a register: '%BRANCH%' in the group name, or JIVO / AKAL ROZGAR / AKAL INFO in the card name. A new group entity named otherwise scores TRADE. Groups 146/144 'COMPANY UNIT VENDOR' hold 0 cards today and would be caught by neither test. C-0005's 23 named intercompany CardCodes are all CUSTA (customer-side) codes and do NOT cover the vendor side, so this section cannot be validated against that list.

MIGRATED_OPEN is hardcoded to DocDate = 2024-09-30 (Oil's go-live). Returning 0 for Mart and Bev is the TRUE answer - Mart's OPCH starts 2025-01-01, Bev's 2024-10-01, and neither carried its A/P openings in as invoices. Generalising it to MIN(DocDate) per schema would relabel Bev's first ordinary trading day as a migration.

Oldest-due-bill-first is an assumption. The ledger proves the total credit; WHICH bills it settled is inferred. The total is right in every case; where a genuinely-unpaid old bill sits behind newer settled ones, the bucket split shifts newer than reality. Unfalsifiable without the OITR/ITR1 reconciliation history.

On any --as-of that is not today the bucket split is approximate: OPCH.PaidToDate is a right-now field and cannot be rewound, so the total is correct but the bill side is today's and the unexplained part lands in UNBACKED_CREDIT (Oil: Rs 0.48 Cr at as-of=today, Rs 6.51 Cr at 2026-06-30, Rs 23.83 Cr at 2025-12-31). Read UNBACKED_CREDIT before trusting any past-dated bucket chart.

PAYABLE and VENDOR_ADVANCE are mutually exclusive per card (0 cards carry both) and must never be netted into one 'position' across cards - that would let one supplier's advance cancel another's overdue bill.

OCRD_BALANCE does not come from OCRD.Balance. It is the JDT1-derived as-of ledger balance (they agree to the rupee at as-of = today, on all 5,174 vendor cards). Its sign is SAP's, so NEGATIVE means JIVO owes - rendering it raw without saying so reads exactly backwards.

This section has no detail slice: vendor-ageing-detail.sql does not exist and data.json's detail object is {} for all three companies. Bill-level drill-down must come from open-item-list DOCTYPE='AP_INV', which is capped per document type - only 21 of Oil's 256 owed trade cards, 1 of Mart's 31 and 56 of Bev's 75 have ALL their bills present there. A document list rendered from it without saying so implies a vendor has fewer bills than it does.

Group totals are not eliminated. Adding oil + mart + bev double counts JIVO's inter-book trading - Mart's Rs 20.93 Cr owed to VENDA000001 JIVO WELLNESS is the mirror of an Oil receivable. Per-company is the figure that means something.

A card can be in scope with zero open bills (155 Oil / 25 Mart / 31 Bev rows) purely because of a ledger balance, an unapplied payment or an open credit note. OLDEST_DUE and DAYS_OLDEST are NULL on exactly those rows - the only two nullable columns in the section. Sorting or charting on them must handle NULL, not coerce it to 0 (which would place them at 'due today').

sql.text:
ROUND(SUM(TOTOPEN)  OVER (), 2)           AS CO_RAW_OPEN,
  ROUND(SUM(PAYABLE)  OVER (), 2)           AS CO_PAYABLE,
  ROUND(SUM(B0+B1+B2+B3+B4+B5+B6) OVER (), 2) AS CO_ADJ_OPEN,
  ROUND(SUM(UNBACKED) OVER (), 2)           AS CO_UNBACKED_CREDIT,
  ROUND(SUM(UNAPP)    OVER (), 2)           AS CO_UNAPPLIED_PAY,
  ROUND(SUM(OPENCN)   OVER (), 2)           AS CO_OPEN_CN,
  ROUND(SUM(ADVANCE)  OVER (), 2)           AS CO_VENDOR_ADVANCE,
  ROUND(SUM(MIGEFF)   OVER (), 2)           AS CO_MIGRATED_OPEN,
  ROUND(SUM(BACKEFF)  OVER (), 2)           AS CO_BACKDATED_DUE_OPEN,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN ACCT_KIND='TRADE' THEN B0+B1+B2+B3+B4+B5+B6 ELSE 0 END) OVER (), 2) AS CO_ADJ_OPEN_TRADE,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN ACCT_KIND='TRADE' THEN B3+B4+B5+B6 ELSE 0 END) OVER (), 2)          AS CO_ADJ_OVERDUE_60PLUS_TRADE

bal AS (
  SELECT "ShortName"                                                       AS CC,
         ROUND(SUM(CAST("Debit" AS DOUBLE) - CAST("Credit" AS DOUBLE)), 2) AS BAL
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.JDT1
  WHERE "RefDate" <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'
  GROUP BY "ShortName"
),

caveats.right: There are 23 related-party customer cards across the three companies (Oil 9, Mart 8, Beverages 6). All of them are group entities, so all of them are intercompany. Exclude the whole set, not one card, and name which cards were excluded.
caveats.rule: Intercompany is 23 group CardCodes, not just CUSTA000606: Oil CUSTA000001/2/3/4/606/827/906/1099/1113, Mart CUSTA000001/827/874/875/876/877/878/926, Bev CUSTA000001/2/3/4/606/827. Exclude all; name them.
caveats.title: Intercompany is 23 group cards, not just CUSTA000606
caveats.wrong: Split external vs intercompany by excluding only CUSTA000606 (JIVO MART PVT LTD), per C-0002. That leaves every other group card counted as an outside customer — JIVO WELLNESS DL/HR/PB/HP, JIVO MART HR/DL/PB/KR/RJ/UP/ISD, JIVO BEVERAGES-CUST. June-2026 olive: Mart 'external' came out Rs 10.47 Cr excluding only CUSTA000606, against Rs 9.53 Cr excluding all eight of Mart's group cards — a Rs 1.53 Cr overstatement of outside business.

caveats.right: On the vendor side several intercompany accounts sit in ordinary trading groups, so a group-only test silently counts JIVO's own money as external trade payable. Measured live 2026-08-21: Mart VENDA000001 'JIVO WELLNESS PVT LTD' is in group PURCHASE at -20.93 Cr and is Mart's single largest payable; Mart VENDA000004 'JIVO WELLNESS PVT LTD - DL' also in PURCHASE; Oil VENDA000483 'JIVO MART PVT LTD' is in group E-COMMERCE at -2.25 Cr. Together 23.19 Cr is missed. The remaining group entities do sit in BRANCH VENDOR, so the group test is necessary but not sufficient. Correction C-0005 lists 23 intercompany CardCodes but they are all CUSTA* — it covers no vendor codes at all. Test the group AND the CardName (JIVO / AKAL), and flag the rows rather than dropping them.
caveats.rule: Intercompany vendors hide outside BRANCH groups: Mart VENDA000001 'JIVO WELLNESS' is in group PURCHASE (-20.93 Cr), Oil VENDA000483 in E-COMMERCE. Match OCRD.CardName too, never group alone.
caveats.title: Intercompany vendors hide outside the BRANCH groups — match on name too
caveats.wrong: Identified JIVO's own intercompany and branch accounts by joining OCRD to OCRG and testing GroupName LIKE '%BRANCH%', assuming that catches every group entity.

sql.text:
vend AS (
  SELECT c."CardCode"                        AS CC,
         c."CardName"                        AS CNAME,
         IFNULL(g."GroupName", '(no group)') AS GRPNAME,
         IFNULL(b.BAL, 0)                    AS BAL,
         CASE
           WHEN g."GroupName" LIKE '%BRANCH%' THEN 'BRANCH'
           WHEN UPPER(c."CardName") LIKE '%JIVO%'
             OR UPPER(c."CardName") LIKE '%AKAL ROZGAR%'
             OR UPPER(c."CardName") LIKE '%AKAL INFO%'
           THEN 'INTERCO'
           ELSE 'TRADE'
         END                                 AS ACCT_KIND
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.OCRD c
  LEFT JOIN {{SCHEMA}}.OCRG g
         ON g."GroupCode" = c."GroupCode"
        AND g."GroupType" = c."CardType"
  LEFT JOIN bal b ON b.CC = c."CardCode"
  WHERE c."CardType" = 'S'
),

  SELECT v.CC,
         IFNULL(t.TOTOPEN, 0)                                        AS TOTOPEN,
         GREATEST(0, -v.BAL)                                         AS PAYABLE,

sql.text:
SELECT
  CC                                        AS CARD_CODE,
  CNAME                                     AS CARD_NAME,
  GRPNAME                                   AS VENDOR_GROUP,
  ACCT_KIND                                 AS ACCT_KIND,
  CASE WHEN ACCT_KIND = 'TRADE' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS IS_EXCLUDED,
  ROUND(BAL, 2)                             AS OCRD_BALANCE,
  ROUND(PAYABLE, 2)                         AS PAYABLE,
  ROUND(ADVANCE, 2)                         AS VENDOR_ADVANCE,
  NBILL                                     AS N_OPEN_BILLS,
  ROUND(TOTOPEN, 2)                         AS RAW_OPEN,
  ROUND(CREDIT, 2)                          AS CREDIT_APPLIED,
  ROUND(B0+B1+B2+B3+B4+B5+B6, 2)            AS ADJ_OPEN,
  ROUND(UNBACKED, 2)                        AS UNBACKED_CREDIT,
  ROUND(MIGEFF, 2)                          AS MIGRATED_OPEN,
  ROUND(BACKEFF, 2)                         AS BACKDATED_DUE_OPEN,
  OLDESTDUE                                 AS OLDEST_DUE,
  CASE WHEN OLDESTDUE IS NULL THEN NULL
       ELSE DAYS_BETWEEN(OLDESTDUE, DATE'{{ASOF}}') END AS DAYS_OLDEST,
  ROUND(B0, 2) AS B0_NOTDUE,
  ROUND(B1, 2) AS B1_1_30,
  ROUND(B2, 2) AS B2_31_60,
  ROUND(B3, 2) AS B3_61_90,
  ROUND(B4, 2) AS B4_91_180,
  ROUND(B5, 2) AS B5_181_365,
  ROUND(B6, 2) AS B6_365PLUS,
  ROUND(B3+B4+B5+B6, 2)                     AS ADJ_OVERDUE_60PLUS,
  NPAY                                      AS N_UNAPPLIED_PAY,
  ROUND(UNAPP, 2)                           AS UNAPPLIED_PAY,
  NCN                                       AS N_OPEN_CN,
  ROUND(OPENCN, 2)                          AS OPEN_CN,
  ROUND(SUM(TOTOPEN)  OVER (), 2)           AS CO_RAW_OPEN,
  ROUND(SUM(PAYABLE)  OVER (), 2)           AS CO_PAYABLE,

check.method: reproduces the figure measured independently from the SQL when the section was catalogued

ap-trade-overdue-61p.formula: SUM over TRADE cards of ADJ_OVERDUE_60PLUS = B3_61_90 + B4_91_180 + B5_181_365 + B6_365PLUS. The column name says 60 but the boundary is DAYS_BETWEEN(DocDueDate, as-of) >= 61 - label it '61 d +'.
ap-trade-overdue-61p.label: Overdue to pay, 61 days and over
section_traps: CO_* columns are BROADCAST company totals repeated identically on every row (verified across all 644/88/164 rows). Summing CO_ADJ_OPEN_TRADE down Oil's table gives Rs 14,604 Cr instead of Rs 22.68 Cr. Read any CO_* off a single row; never aggregate it.

Summing ADJ_OPEN over ALL rows gives Oil Rs 102.51 Cr, not Rs 22.68 Cr. 78% of Oil's aged book, 95% of Mart's and 36% of Bev's is JIVO's own branch and intercompany cards. The filter ACCT_KIND == 'TRADE' (or IS_EXCLUDED == 0) is mandatory on every trade figure.

Row count is not party count. Oil has 635 TRADE cards but only 256 owe anything; 170 hold an advance and 154 rows of the whole book are nil on both sides. v1's KPI subtitle counts rows and overstates exposure ~2.5x - the SQL header says so at lines 11-13 and the renderer ignores it.

RAW_OPEN is not a payable. On Oil's trade book it is Rs 223.92 Cr against Rs 22.68 Cr = 9.87x. The '~3x' figure quoted in README.md and in the SQL header is the WHOLE-BOOK ratio (Oil 3.03x, Mart 7.52x, Bev 1.63x) and understates the distortion on the number the board actually shows.

UNAPPLIED_PAY (OVPM.OpenBal) and OPEN_CN (open ORPC) are diagnostics and are ALREADY inside the ledger balance. Subtracting either double-counts. Oil's CO_UNAPPLIED_PAY is Rs 2,017.71 Cr against a Rs 103.20 Cr real payable, and 8,355 of Oil's 9,038 uncancelled supplier payments carry a non-zero OpenBal - at JIVO 'OpenBal' means never internally reconciled, not money still unspent.

DAYS_OLDEST and OLDEST_DUE are PRE-CREDIT: the oldest open bill on the card, before the ledger credit was consumed against it. 226 Oil trade cards report a DAYS_OLDEST while owing Rs 0, and Oil's 3,189-day maximum (VENDA001047 BLESSING ADVERTISING) has its surviving Rs 26.26 L bucketed at 61-90 and 91-180 days, not 365+. 16 Oil cards worth Rs 0.31 Cr and 3 Mart cards worth Rs 1.05 Cr have DAYS_OLDEST over 365 with B6_365PLUS = 0.
ADJ_OVERDUE_60PLUS is B3+B4+B5+B6, i.e. 61 days and over - the name rounds to 60 and is wrong. Label it '61 d +'. It was deliberately not renamed because v1's hero hardcodes the key.

There is no STAFF class in this section, unlike open-item-list. 82 Oil / 24 Mart / 22 Bev employee imprest cards (VENDOR_GROUP = 'STAFF VENDOR', CARD_CODE prefix ORGV) are scored TRADE here and STAFF there - 18/6/5 direct disagreements on the cards both sections carry. The money is small (Oil Rs 0.011 Cr ADJ_OPEN and Rs 0.227 Cr of advances, Bev Rs 0.047 Cr) but two ORGV cards sit inside Bev's top 10 payables, so a 'top external suppliers' chart will print employee names unless it filters VENDOR_GROUP != 'STAFF VENDOR'. This matters beyond the charts: CONTRACT.md §2 defines data/parties.<company>.json with kind in TRADE|BRANCH|INTERCO|STAFF, so the party index must NOT take a vendor's kind from this section's ACCT_KIND - it would emit zero STAFF vendors. Take it from open-item-list.ACCT_KIND, or re-derive STAFF from VENDOR_GROUP == 'STAFF VENDOR'.

ACCT_KIND is a name-and-group heuristic, not a register: '%BRANCH%' in the group name, or JIVO / AKAL ROZGAR / AKAL INFO in the card name. A new group entity named otherwise scores TRADE. Groups 146/144 'COMPANY UNIT VENDOR' hold 0 cards today and would be caught by neither test. C-0005's 23 named intercompany CardCodes are all CUSTA (customer-side) codes and do NOT cover the vendor side, so this section cannot be validated against that list.

MIGRATED_OPEN is hardcoded to DocDate = 2024-09-30 (Oil's go-live). Returning 0 for Mart and Bev is the TRUE answer - Mart's OPCH starts 2025-01-01, Bev's 2024-10-01, and neither carried its A/P openings in as invoices. Generalising it to MIN(DocDate) per schema would relabel Bev's first ordinary trading day as a migration.

Oldest-due-bill-first is an assumption. The ledger proves the total credit; WHICH bills it settled is inferred. The total is right in every case; where a genuinely-unpaid old bill sits behind newer settled ones, the bucket split shifts newer than reality. Unfalsifiable without the OITR/ITR1 reconciliation history.

On any --as-of that is not today the bucket split is approximate: OPCH.PaidToDate is a right-now field and cannot be rewound, so the total is correct but the bill side is today's and the unexplained part lands in UNBACKED_CREDIT (Oil: Rs 0.48 Cr at as-of=today, Rs 6.51 Cr at 2026-06-30, Rs 23.83 Cr at 2025-12-31). Read UNBACKED_CREDIT before trusting any past-dated bucket chart.

PAYABLE and VENDOR_ADVANCE are mutually exclusive per card (0 cards carry both) and must never be netted into one 'position' across cards - that would let one supplier's advance cancel another's overdue bill.

OCRD_BALANCE does not come from OCRD.Balance. It is the JDT1-derived as-of ledger balance (they agree to the rupee at as-of = today, on all 5,174 vendor cards). Its sign is SAP's, so NEGATIVE means JIVO owes - rendering it raw without saying so reads exactly backwards.

This section has no detail slice: vendor-ageing-detail.sql does not exist and data.json's detail object is {} for all three companies. Bill-level drill-down must come from open-item-list DOCTYPE='AP_INV', which is capped per document type - only 21 of Oil's 256 owed trade cards, 1 of Mart's 31 and 56 of Bev's 75 have ALL their bills present there. A document list rendered from it without saying so implies a vendor has fewer bills than it does.

Group totals are not eliminated. Adding oil + mart + bev double counts JIVO's inter-book trading - Mart's Rs 20.93 Cr owed to VENDA000001 JIVO WELLNESS is the mirror of an Oil receivable. Per-company is the figure that means something.

A card can be in scope with zero open bills (155 Oil / 25 Mart / 31 Bev rows) purely because of a ledger balance, an unapplied payment or an open credit note. OLDEST_DUE and DAYS_OLDEST are NULL on exactly those rows - the only two nullable columns in the section. Sorting or charting on them must handle NULL, not coerce it to 0 (which would place them at 'due today').

sql.text:
agg AS (
  SELECT CC,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(DUEDT, DATE'{{ASOF}}') <=   0 THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS B0,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(DUEDT, DATE'{{ASOF}}') BETWEEN   1 AND  30 THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS B1,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(DUEDT, DATE'{{ASOF}}') BETWEEN  31 AND  60 THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS B2,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(DUEDT, DATE'{{ASOF}}') BETWEEN  61 AND  90 THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS B3,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(DUEDT, DATE'{{ASOF}}') BETWEEN  91 AND 180 THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS B4,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(DUEDT, DATE'{{ASOF}}') BETWEEN 181 AND 365 THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS B5,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(DUEDT, DATE'{{ASOF}}') >  365 THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS B6,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DOCDT = DATE'2024-09-30' THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END)                      AS MIGEFF,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DUEDT < DOCDT           THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END)                       AS BACKEFF
  FROM eff GROUP BY CC
),

Note the Service Layer differs: it exposes only Cancelled 'tYES'/'tNO', so the documented OData filter Cancelled eq 'tNO' is already correct and is not affected.

UNAPPLIED_PAY (OVPM.OpenBal) and OPEN_CN (open ORPC) are diagnostics and are ALREADY inside the ledger balance. Subtracting either double-counts. Oil's CO_UNAPPLIED_PAY is Rs 2,017.71 Cr against a Rs 103.20 Cr real payable, and 8,355 of Oil's 9,038 uncancelled supplier payments carry a non-zero OpenBal - at JIVO 'OpenBal' means never internally reconciled, not money still unspent.

DAYS_OLDEST and OLDEST_DUE are PRE-CREDIT: the oldest open bill on the card, before the ledger credit was consumed against it. 226 Oil trade cards report a DAYS_OLDEST while owing Rs 0, and Oil's 3,189-day maximum (VENDA001047 BLESSING ADVERTISING) has its surviving Rs 26.26 L bucketed at 61-90 and 91-180 days, not 365+. 16 Oil cards worth Rs 0.31 Cr and 3 Mart cards worth Rs 1.05 Cr have DAYS_OLDEST over 365 with B6_365PLUS = 0.
ADJ_OVERDUE_60PLUS is B3+B4+B5+B6, i.e. 61 days and over - the name rounds to 60 and is wrong. Label it '61 d +'. It was deliberately not renamed because v1's hero hardcodes the key.

There is no STAFF class in this section, unlike open-item-list. 82 Oil / 24 Mart / 22 Bev employee imprest cards (VENDOR_GROUP = 'STAFF VENDOR', CARD_CODE prefix ORGV) are scored TRADE here and STAFF there - 18/6/5 direct disagreements on the cards both sections carry. The money is small (Oil Rs 0.011 Cr ADJ_OPEN and Rs 0.227 Cr of advances, Bev Rs 0.047 Cr) but two ORGV cards sit inside Bev's top 10 payables, so a 'top external suppliers' chart will print employee names unless it filters VENDOR_GROUP != 'STAFF VENDOR'. This matters beyond the charts: CONTRACT.md §2 defines data/parties.<company>.json with kind in TRADE|BRANCH|INTERCO|STAFF, so the party index must NOT take a vendor's kind from this section's ACCT_KIND - it would emit zero STAFF vendors. Take it from open-item-list.ACCT_KIND, or re-derive STAFF from VENDOR_GROUP == 'STAFF VENDOR'.

ACCT_KIND is a name-and-group heuristic, not a register: '%BRANCH%' in the group name, or JIVO / AKAL ROZGAR / AKAL INFO in the card name. A new group entity named otherwise scores TRADE. Groups 146/144 'COMPANY UNIT VENDOR' hold 0 cards today and would be caught by neither test. C-0005's 23 named intercompany CardCodes are all CUSTA (customer-side) codes and do NOT cover the vendor side, so this section cannot be validated against that list.

MIGRATED_OPEN is hardcoded to DocDate = 2024-09-30 (Oil's go-live). Returning 0 for Mart and Bev is the TRUE answer - Mart's OPCH starts 2025-01-01, Bev's 2024-10-01, and neither carried its A/P openings in as invoices. Generalising it to MIN(DocDate) per schema would relabel Bev's first ordinary trading day as a migration.

Oldest-due-bill-first is an assumption. The ledger proves the total credit; WHICH bills it settled is inferred. The total is right in every case; where a genuinely-unpaid old bill sits behind newer settled ones, the bucket split shifts newer than reality. Unfalsifiable without the OITR/ITR1 reconciliation history.

On any --as-of that is not today the bucket split is approximate: OPCH.PaidToDate is a right-now field and cannot be rewound, so the total is correct but the bill side is today's and the unexplained part lands in UNBACKED_CREDIT (Oil: Rs 0.48 Cr at as-of=today, Rs 6.51 Cr at 2026-06-30, Rs 23.83 Cr at 2025-12-31). Read UNBACKED_CREDIT before trusting any past-dated bucket chart.

PAYABLE and VENDOR_ADVANCE are mutually exclusive per card (0 cards carry both) and must never be netted into one 'position' across cards - that would let one supplier's advance cancel another's overdue bill.

This section has no detail slice: vendor-ageing-detail.sql does not exist and data.json's detail object is {} for all three companies. Bill-level drill-down must come from open-item-list DOCTYPE='AP_INV', which is capped per document type - only 21 of Oil's 256 owed trade cards, 1 of Mart's 31 and 56 of Bev's 75 have ALL their bills present there. A document list rendered from it without saying so implies a vendor has fewer bills than it does.

Group totals are not eliminated. Adding oil + mart + bev double counts JIVO's inter-book trading - Mart's Rs 20.93 Cr owed to VENDA000001 JIVO WELLNESS is the mirror of an Oil receivable. Per-company is the figure that means something.

A card can be in scope with zero open bills (155 Oil / 25 Mart / 31 Bev rows) purely because of a ledger balance, an unapplied payment or an open credit note. OLDEST_DUE and DAYS_OLDEST are NULL on exactly those rows - the only two nullable columns in the section. sql.text:
WITH bill AS (
  SELECT p."CardCode"                                   AS CC,
         p."DocEntry"                                   AS DE,
         p."DocDueDate"                                 AS DUEDT,
         p."DocDate"                                    AS DOCDT,
         CAST(p."DocTotal" - p."PaidToDate" AS DOUBLE)  AS OPENAMT
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.OPCH p
  WHERE p."DocStatus" = 'O'
    AND p."CANCELED"  = 'N'
    AND p."DocDate"  <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'
    AND CAST(p."DocTotal" - p."PaidToDate" AS DOUBLE) > 0
),

sql.text:
base AS (
  SELECT v.CC, v.CNAME, v.GRPNAME, v.ACCT_KIND, v.BAL,
         c.PAYABLE, c.CREDIT, c.TOTOPEN,
         IFNULL(t.NBILL,0)     AS NBILL,
         t.OLDESTDUE           AS OLDESTDUE,
         IFNULL(a.B0,0) B0, IFNULL(a.B1,0) B1, IFNULL(a.B2,0) B2,
         IFNULL(a.B3,0) B3, IFNULL(a.B4,0) B4, IFNULL(a.B5,0) B5,
         IFNULL(a.B6,0) B6,
         IFNULL(a.MIGEFF,0)    AS MIGEFF,
         IFNULL(a.BACKEFF,0)   AS BACKEFF,
         IFNULL(p.NPAY,0)      AS NPAY,
         IFNULL(p.UNAPP,0)     AS UNAPP,
         IFNULL(n.NCN,0)       AS NCN,
         IFNULL(n.OPENCN,0)    AS OPENCN,
         GREATEST(0, v.BAL)                              AS ADVANCE,
         GREATEST(0, GREATEST(0,-v.BAL) - IFNULL(t.TOTOPEN,0)) AS UNBACKED
  FROM vend v
  JOIN cr   c ON c.CC = v.CC
  LEFT JOIN tot t ON t.CC = v.CC
  LEFT JOIN agg a ON a.CC = v.CC
  LEFT JOIN vpm p ON p.CC = v.CC
  LEFT JOIN cn  n ON n.CC = v.CC
  WHERE IFNULL(t.NBILL,0) > 0
     OR v.BAL <> 0
     OR IFNULL(p.UNAPP,0) <> 0
     OR IFNULL(n.OPENCN,0) <> 0
)

caveats.right: In the HANA tables the flag has THREE values: 'N' = live, 'Y' = the cancelled original, and 'C' = the system-generated cancellation mirror SAP posts to reverse it. Y and C always appear as exact matching pairs carrying the same value, so a <>'Y' test keeps every mirror and double-counts. Measured live on Oil 2026-08-21: OINV 30,387 'N' (1045.62 Cr) plus 320 'Y' and 320 'C' at 37.27 Cr each; OPCH 16,101 'N' plus 113+113 at 15.96 Cr each; OPDN 10,640 'N' plus 473+473 at 94.63 Cr each; ORDN 1,817 'N' plus 107+107 at 0.49 Cr each. Same pattern in Mart and Beverages. Always test CANCELED='N' positively. Note the Service Layer differs: it exposes only Cancelled 'tYES'/'tNO', so the documented OData filter Cancelled eq 'tNO' is already correct and is not affected.
caveats.rule: HANA "CANCELED" is three-valued: 'N' live, 'Y' cancelled original, 'C' its system mirror. Always filter CANCELED='N' - a <>'Y' test keeps the mirrors and double-counts (Oil OPDN +94.63 Cr).
caveats.title: HANA CANCELED is three-valued — filter ='N', never <>'Y'
caveats.wrong: Excluded cancelled documents in HANA SQL by writing "CANCELED" <> 'Y' (or omitting the filter), assuming the flag is a two-valued Y/N.

         SUM(CAST(IFNULL("OpenBal",0) AS DOUBLE)) AS UNAPP

terms.label: Unmatched supplier payments
terms.note: Oil: 802 payments across 277 cards; Rs 1,835.66 Cr of it sits on one card, VENDA000724 AL GHURAIR RESOURCES OILS, on 16 payments. Mart: Rs 181.32 Cr of Rs 185.61 Cr is on the interco card VENDA000001.

caveats.right: At JIVO a document stays DocStatus='O' long after the money moved, because settlements are posted as manual journal entries (JDT1.TransType=30) and as on-account ORCT/OVPM receipts and payments that are never internally reconciled to the document. OCRD.Balance is the only ground truth for what a party owes or is owed. Measured live 2026-08-21, open documents vs OCRD balances: Oil A/R 180.69 vs 109.51 Cr and A/P 309.20 vs 102.63 Cr; Mart A/R 128.12 vs 23.35 Cr and A/P 219.60 vs 29.22 Cr; Bev A/R 6.34 vs 4.83 Cr and A/P 3.56 vs 2.24 Cr. Overstatement 1.3x to 7.5x, worst on Mart payables. Correct method: take the party balance as the real exposure, derive unapplied credit as sum(open docs) - balance, consume it oldest-due-first, then bucket the remainder.
caveats.rule: SAP DocStatus='O' is unreliable at JIVO: documents settled by manual JE or unapplied on-account payment stay open. Age from OCRD.Balance, not open documents - naive ageing overstates 1.3-7.5x.
caveats.title: DocStatus='O' is unreliable — age from OCRD.Balance, not open documents
caveats.wrong: Built an ageing by summing open documents (OINV/OPCH DocStatus='O', DocTotal-PaidToDate) and bucketing on DocDueDate, treating 'open' as 'unpaid'.

caveats.right: The business-partner sub-ledger is JDT1 (JOIN OCRD ON CardCode = ShortName). A document-based extract silently omits every journal entry posted against a party, plus pre-cutover postings, cancelled documents with their reversals, and payments booked under the other side's DocType. Re-verified live 2026-08-22 in JIVO_OIL_HANADB since the migration: A/R invoice 30,956 / A/P invoice 16,330 / incoming payment 13,021 / outgoing payment 10,640 / JOURNAL ENTRY 7,478 (Rs 3,043.6 cr) / A/R credit note 6,431 / A/P credit note 1,587 / manual reconciliation 48. On CUSTA000578 RELIANCE RETAIL the document-based ledger showed 324 of the 620 postings SAP holds. It still footed to the correct closing balance only because the builder plugged the difference into a fabricated opening-balance row - so the omission was invisible from the total. Treat any figure that ties only because of a plug as unverified.
caveats.rule: Build a party ledger from JDT1 (OCRD.CardCode = JDT1.ShortName), never from document extracts - they miss every journal entry (7,478 in Oil, Rs 3,043 cr), cancellations and pre-cutover postings.
caveats.title: A party ledger comes from JDT1, not from document extracts
caveats.wrong: Built the vendor/customer Ledger from the ageing extract (Invoices + CreditNotes + Payments) and treated it as a statement of account.

check.method: 1.0% from the figure measured when the section was catalogued — consistent with movement in a live book, not corroborated

ap-unbacked-credit.closure_note: Terms describe how the query built this figure; they are not addends over a row set, so no arithmetic closure is asserted.
ap-unbacked-credit.formula: CO_UNBACKED_CREDIT = SUM over cards of GREATEST(0, PAYABLE - RAW_OPEN). The residual that closes the section's structural identity SUM(buckets) + UNBACKED_CREDIT = PAYABLE. Small at as-of=today; it is the parking place for the error on any past as-of, because OPCH.PaidToDate cannot be rewound.
ap-unbacked-credit.label: Owed per the ledger with no open bill to explain it
section_traps: CO_* columns are BROADCAST company totals repeated identically on every row (verified across all 644/88/164 rows). Summing CO_ADJ_OPEN_TRADE down Oil's table gives Rs 14,604 Cr instead of Rs 22.68 Cr. Read any CO_* off a single row; never aggregate it.

Summing ADJ_OPEN over ALL rows gives Oil Rs 102.51 Cr, not Rs 22.68 Cr. 78% of Oil's aged book, 95% of Mart's and 36% of Bev's is JIVO's own branch and intercompany cards. The filter ACCT_KIND == 'TRADE' (or IS_EXCLUDED == 0) is mandatory on every trade figure.

Row count is not party count. Oil has 635 TRADE cards but only 256 owe anything; 170 hold an advance and 154 rows of the whole book are nil on both sides. v1's KPI subtitle counts rows and overstates exposure ~2.5x - the SQL header says so at lines 11-13 and the renderer ignores it.

RAW_OPEN is not a payable. On Oil's trade book it is Rs 223.92 Cr against Rs 22.68 Cr = 9.87x. The '~3x' figure quoted in README.md and in the SQL header is the WHOLE-BOOK ratio (Oil 3.03x, Mart 7.52x, Bev 1.63x) and understates the distortion on the number the board actually shows.

UNAPPLIED_PAY (OVPM.OpenBal) and OPEN_CN (open ORPC) are diagnostics and are ALREADY inside the ledger balance. Subtracting either double-counts. Oil's CO_UNAPPLIED_PAY is Rs 2,017.71 Cr against a Rs 103.20 Cr real payable, and 8,355 of Oil's 9,038 uncancelled supplier payments carry a non-zero OpenBal - at JIVO 'OpenBal' means never internally reconciled, not money still unspent.

DAYS_OLDEST and OLDEST_DUE are PRE-CREDIT: the oldest open bill on the card, before the ledger credit was consumed against it. 226 Oil trade cards report a DAYS_OLDEST while owing Rs 0, and Oil's 3,189-day maximum (VENDA001047 BLESSING ADVERTISING) has its surviving Rs 26.26 L bucketed at 61-90 and 91-180 days, not 365+. 16 Oil cards worth Rs 0.31 Cr and 3 Mart cards worth Rs 1.05 Cr have DAYS_OLDEST over 365 with B6_365PLUS = 0.
ADJ_OVERDUE_60PLUS is B3+B4+B5+B6, i.e. 61 days and over - the name rounds to 60 and is wrong. Label it '61 d +'. It was deliberately not renamed because v1's hero hardcodes the key.

There is no STAFF class in this section, unlike open-item-list. 82 Oil / 24 Mart / 22 Bev employee imprest cards (VENDOR_GROUP = 'STAFF VENDOR', CARD_CODE prefix ORGV) are scored TRADE here and STAFF there - 18/6/5 direct disagreements on the cards both sections carry. The money is small (Oil Rs 0.011 Cr ADJ_OPEN and Rs 0.227 Cr of advances, Bev Rs 0.047 Cr) but two ORGV cards sit inside Bev's top 10 payables, so a 'top external suppliers' chart will print employee names unless it filters VENDOR_GROUP != 'STAFF VENDOR'. This matters beyond the charts: CONTRACT.md §2 defines data/parties.<company>.json with kind in TRADE|BRANCH|INTERCO|STAFF, so the party index must NOT take a vendor's kind from this section's ACCT_KIND - it would emit zero STAFF vendors. Take it from open-item-list.ACCT_KIND, or re-derive STAFF from VENDOR_GROUP == 'STAFF VENDOR'.

ACCT_KIND is a name-and-group heuristic, not a register: '%BRANCH%' in the group name, or JIVO / AKAL ROZGAR / AKAL INFO in the card name. A new group entity named otherwise scores TRADE. Groups 146/144 'COMPANY UNIT VENDOR' hold 0 cards today and would be caught by neither test. C-0005's 23 named intercompany CardCodes are all CUSTA (customer-side) codes and do NOT cover the vendor side, so this section cannot be validated against that list.

MIGRATED_OPEN is hardcoded to DocDate = 2024-09-30 (Oil's go-live). Returning 0 for Mart and Bev is the TRUE answer - Mart's OPCH starts 2025-01-01, Bev's 2024-10-01, and neither carried its A/P openings in as invoices. Generalising it to MIN(DocDate) per schema would relabel Bev's first ordinary trading day as a migration.

Oldest-due-bill-first is an assumption. The ledger proves the total credit; WHICH bills it settled is inferred. The total is right in every case; where a genuinely-unpaid old bill sits behind newer settled ones, the bucket split shifts newer than reality. Unfalsifiable without the OITR/ITR1 reconciliation history.

On any --as-of that is not today the bucket split is approximate: OPCH.PaidToDate is a right-now field and cannot be rewound, so the total is correct but the bill side is today's and the unexplained part lands in UNBACKED_CREDIT (Oil: Rs 0.48 Cr at as-of=today, Rs 6.51 Cr at 2026-06-30, Rs 23.83 Cr at 2025-12-31). Read UNBACKED_CREDIT before trusting any past-dated bucket chart.

PAYABLE and VENDOR_ADVANCE are mutually exclusive per card (0 cards carry both) and must never be netted into one 'position' across cards - that would let one supplier's advance cancel another's overdue bill.

OCRD_BALANCE does not come from OCRD.Balance. It is the JDT1-derived as-of ledger balance (they agree to the rupee at as-of = today, on all 5,174 vendor cards). Its sign is SAP's, so NEGATIVE means JIVO owes - rendering it raw without saying so reads exactly backwards.

This section has no detail slice: vendor-ageing-detail.sql does not exist and data.json's detail object is {} for all three companies. Bill-level drill-down must come from open-item-list DOCTYPE='AP_INV', which is capped per document type - only 21 of Oil's 256 owed trade cards, 1 of Mart's 31 and 56 of Bev's 75 have ALL their bills present there. A document list rendered from it without saying so implies a vendor has fewer bills than it does.

Group totals are not eliminated. Adding oil + mart + bev double counts JIVO's inter-book trading - Mart's Rs 20.93 Cr owed to VENDA000001 JIVO WELLNESS is the mirror of an Oil receivable. Per-company is the figure that means something.

A card can be in scope with zero open bills (155 Oil / 25 Mart / 31 Bev rows) purely because of a ledger balance, an unapplied payment or an open credit note. OLDEST_DUE and DAYS_OLDEST are NULL on exactly those rows - the only two nullable columns in the section. Sorting or charting on them must handle NULL, not coerce it to 0 (which would place them at 'due today').

sql.text: GREATEST(0, GREATEST(0,-v.BAL) - IFNULL(t.TOTOPEN,0)) AS UNBACKED

Un-bill-backed payable

caveats.right: There are 23 related-party customer cards across the three companies (Oil 9, Mart 8, Beverages 6). All of them are group entities, so all of them are intercompany. Exclude the whole set, not one card, and name which cards were excluded.
caveats.rule: Intercompany is 23 group CardCodes, not just CUSTA000606: Oil CUSTA000001/2/3/4/606/827/906/1099/1113, Mart CUSTA000001/827/874/875/876/877/878/926, Bev CUSTA000001/2/3/4/606/827. Exclude all; name them.
caveats.title: Intercompany is 23 group cards, not just CUSTA000606
caveats.wrong: Split external vs intercompany by excluding only CUSTA000606 (JIVO MART PVT LTD), per C-0002. That leaves every other group card counted as an outside customer — JIVO WELLNESS DL/HR/PB/HP, JIVO MART HR/DL/PB/KR/RJ/UP/ISD, JIVO BEVERAGES-CUST. June-2026 olive: Mart 'external' came out Rs 10.47 Cr excluding only CUSTA000606, against Rs 9.53 Cr excluding all eight of Mart's group cards — a Rs 1.53 Cr overstatement of outside business.

caveats.right: At JIVO a document stays DocStatus='O' long after the money moved, because settlements are posted as manual journal entries (JDT1.TransType=30) and as on-account ORCT/OVPM receipts and payments that are never internally reconciled to the document. OCRD.Balance is the only ground truth for what a party owes or is owed. Measured live 2026-08-21, open documents vs OCRD balances: Oil A/R 180.69 vs 109.51 Cr and A/P 309.20 vs 102.63 Cr; Mart A/R 128.12 vs 23.35 Cr and A/P 219.60 vs 29.22 Cr; Bev A/R 6.34 vs 4.83 Cr and A/P 3.56 vs 2.24 Cr. Overstatement 1.3x to 7.5x, worst on Mart payables. Correct method: take the party balance as the real exposure, derive unapplied credit as sum(open docs) - balance, consume it oldest-due-first, then bucket the remainder.
caveats.rule: SAP DocStatus='O' is unreliable at JIVO: documents settled by manual JE or unapplied on-account payment stay open. Age from OCRD.Balance, not open documents - naive ageing overstates 1.3-7.5x.
caveats.title: DocStatus='O' is unreliable — age from OCRD.Balance, not open documents
caveats.wrong: Built an ageing by summing open documents (OINV/OPCH DocStatus='O', DocTotal-PaidToDate) and bucketing on DocDueDate, treating 'open' as 'unpaid'.

ar-book-open-total.closure_note: Terms describe how the query built this figure; they are not addends over a row set, so no arithmetic closure is asserted.
ar-book-open-total.formula: the GROUPING SETS () roll-up of EFF_OPEN_INR over every CardType='C' card
ar-book-open-total.label: Whole customer book, JIVO's own accounts included
section_traps: ZZ_TOTAL is a FIFTH ROW in the same array as BRANCH/INTERCO/STAFF/TRADE (GROUPING SETS, column KIND, literal value 'ZZ_TOTAL'). Summing any money column across all rows returns exactly 2x the truth. The TOTAL row is KIND=='ZZ_TOTAL'; every other consumer must filter by KIND. This is the section's live landmine and v1's renderer only just avoids it.

DocStatus='O' is not solvency at JIVO (C-0019). Raw open vs credit-adjusted on the TRADE book: Oil ₹75.86 Cr → ₹7.35 Cr (10.3x), Mart ₹113.84 Cr → ₹10.30 Cr (11.1x), Bev ₹5.00 Cr → ₹3.84 Cr (1.3x). Anything that reads RAW_OPEN_INR and calls it a receivable is wrong by an order of magnitude on two of the three books.

N_CUSTOMERS and N_OPEN_INV are SAP's UNCORRECTED counts. Pairing them with EFF_OPEN_INR re-commits the very error the section corrects: ₹7.35 Cr ÷ 11,499 invoices = ₹6,396 each, against the truth of ₹55,509 across 1,325. Use N_EFF_CUSTOMERS and N_EFF_INV; show the SAP count struck through if at all.

The bucket split is an ASSUMPTION, the total is a measurement. EFF_OPEN_INR is identical to the paisa whether credit is consumed oldest-first or newest-first; the BUCKETS are not. Mart's 60-day-plus figure moves from ₹30.14 L (shipped, FIFO) to ₹8.46 Cr (newest-first) — 28x. Oil 1.18x, Bev 1.01x. Every overdue figure on this page is a LOWER BOUND and must say so, Mart loudest.

Never subtract UNAPPLIED_RECEIPTS_INR or OPEN_CREDIT_NOTES_INR from the receivable. They are already inside OCRD.Balance, which is what EFF_OPEN_INR is capped at. Subtracting Oil's ₹66.2 Cr of unapplied receipts from its ₹7.35 Cr trade book would produce a large negative receivable out of correct data.

EFF_OPEN_INR is capped at the ledger debit, so BAL_NOT_IN_INV_INR of trade debit is carried by no open invoice and is never aged: Oil ₹65.07 L (8.13% of the trade ledger debit), Mart ₹13.09 L (1.26%), Bev ₹45,378 (0.12%). The headline is a disclosed understatement of the debit book. Show OCRD_DEBIT_INR beside it, never instead of it.

OCRD_CREDIT_INR is stored NEGATIVE (JIVO sign convention: −ve = JIVO owes the party). Adding it to OCRD_DEBIT_INR silently nets customers in advance against customers in arrears and produces a 'net receivable' that means nothing. The detail twin CUSTOMER_ADVANCE stores the same money POSITIVE — mixing the two flips a sign.

MIGRATED_OPEN_INR: Oil's 365-day-plus TRADE bucket is 96.6% migrated pre-SAP openings (invoices dated exactly at go-live 2024-09-30, carrying true original due dates back to 2017). Calling it 'debt that rotted since go-live' is wrong. The 0.00 in Mart and Bev is a TRUE zero — their first invoices are 2024-10-03 and 2024-10-04 and neither book has an opening batch — but the date is HARD-CODED and Oil-specific, so a fourth company book would need its own go-live checked.

OLDEST_OPEN_DUE / OLDEST_DUE is the oldest date that still carries money AFTER credit application, not the oldest open document. It jumps forward when a receipt is matched, and it deliberately means something different here than in vendor-ageing.sql, which reports the raw oldest bill. Do not compare the two sections' oldest dates.

The detail row count is NOT N_CUSTOMERS and must never be asserted equal. The detail keeps cards that exist only as an unapplied receipt or an open credit note (642 Oil rows vs 379 counted), and 25 Oil / 3 Mart / 9 Bev cards carry sub-paise dust balances that are <>0 in SQL but round to 0.00 at 2 dp. N_EFF_CUSTOMERS for Oil TRADE is 89 while detail rows with ADJ_OPEN>0 number 85 — same dust. Assert the money, never the headcount.

Classification divergences that are real and deliberately unfixed: Oil CUSTA000242 AKAL INFORMATION SYSTEMS LTD (group DEBTORS, ₹10,000) reads TRADE here and INTERCO in both vendor-ageing.sql and open-item-list.sql — verified live 2026-08-22, the one ACCT_KIND mismatch across 229 shared Oil cards. And 8-9 employee imprest cards filed in a STATE group instead of 'STAFF CUSTOMER' read TRADE (Oil ₹3,555 · Mart ₹1,957 · Bev ₹11,562 incl. CUSTA000902 NAVNEET SINGH, which has no 'IMPREST' in its name). Fixing either in one file without the other breaks the summary↔detail tie.

CUSTA000356 'FREE SAMPLE' is classified TRADE in all three books and carries a real ageing (Oil ₹91,239 with ₹85,509 over 60 days; Bev ₹57,809). Nothing in OCRG or the card name marks it internal. It is almost certainly not collectable and it has never been checked with Accounts — do not put it on a collection list without a footnote.

UNAPPLIED_RCPT can be NEGATIVE by a rounding paisa (Oil CUSTA000482 METRO CASH & CARRY = −0.01). Any treemap, log scale or sqrt-area chart over that column must clamp, and a 'top unmatched receipts' sort must not assume the column is non-negative.

Cross-section: open-item-list's CARD_OPEN_GROSS is NOT this section's RAW_OPEN — it folds unapplied receipts into 'gross open'. Oil CUSTA000844 ILAHI CO. reads ₹44.71 L there and ₹24.71 L here, a ₹20 L AR receipt. Its CARD_BALANCE, however, IS the same OCRD.Balance and matched on 229/21/220 shared cards with zero mismatches — that column is a valid cross-file check, CARD_OPEN_GROSS is not.

A back-dated {{ASOF}} is not a point-in-time A/R. OCRD.Balance and PaidToDate are the CURRENT snapshot — SAP keeps no per-date history — so a past as-of ages today's open items against an older calendar. Measured on Oil: --as-of 2026-03-31 gives ₹80.34 Cr adjusted against ₹108.86 Cr today, and ₹2.87 Cr of trade against ₹7.43 Cr. The cut-off is on DocDate only, so an invoice cancelled yesterday vanishes from a last-month run.

Group totals are NOT intercompany-eliminated. Oil, Mart and Bev trade with each other and each book carries the other as a customer; adding the three EFF_OPEN_INR figures double-counts JIVO's own money. Per-company is the only figure that means anything, and the INTERCO row names the amount in each book.

A KIND row with NOTDUE_INR = 0 and EFF_OPEN_INR > 0 is REAL, not a missing bucket: Oil BRANCH, Mart BRANCH/INTERCO/STAFF and Bev BRANCH/INTERCO are 100% overdue. Rendering that as an empty bar or 'no data' misreports a book that is entirely past due.

Every CO_* column in the detail (CO_RAW_OPEN … CO_ADJ_OVERDUE_60PLUS_TRADE) is a company-level total repeated on EVERY row by SUM() OVER (). Read one row. Summing the column multiplies it by 642 / 100 / 451.

data.json is being rewritten under readers roughly every 2 minutes by the VPS refresh loop. A consumer that reads the file twice in one pass can mix two builds — I hit exactly this and briefly saw ZZ_TOTAL disagree with the sum of its KIND rows by ₹40.32 L. Load once into memory, and stamp every derived figure with the generated_at it came from.

sql.text:
SELECT
  CASE WHEN GROUPING(KIND) = 1 THEN 'ZZ_TOTAL' ELSE KIND END AS KIND,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN EFF_OPEN > 0 OR BAL <> 0 THEN 1 END)        AS N_CUSTOMERS,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN EFF_OPEN > 0 THEN 1 END)                    AS N_EFF_CUSTOMERS,
  SUM(NINV)                                                   AS N_OPEN_INV,
  SUM(NEFFINV)                                                AS N_EFF_INV,
  ROUND(SUM(RAW_OPEN),2)                                      AS RAW_OPEN_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(UNAPPLIED),2)                                     AS UNAPPLIED_CREDIT_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(EFF_OPEN),2)                                      AS EFF_OPEN_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(NOTDUE),2)                                        AS NOTDUE_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D1_30),2)                                         AS D1_30_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D31_60),2)                                        AS D31_60_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D61_90),2)                                        AS D61_90_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D91_180),2)                                       AS D91_180_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D181_365),2)                                      AS D181_365_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D365P),2)                                         AS D365P_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(OVERDUE),2)                                       AS OVERDUE_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(OD60P),2)                                         AS OD60P_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(MIGRATED),2)                                      AS MIGRATED_OPEN_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(BAL_NOT_IN_INV),2)                                AS BAL_NOT_IN_INV_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(BAL_DR),2)                                        AS OCRD_DEBIT_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(BAL_CR),2)                                        AS OCRD_CREDIT_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(UNAPPLIED_RCPT),2)                                AS UNAPPLIED_RECEIPTS_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(OPEN_CN),2)                                       AS OPEN_CREDIT_NOTES_INR,
  MIN(OLDEST_OPEN_DUE)                                        AS OLDEST_OPEN_DUE
FROM cust
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((KIND), ())

sql.text:
-- migrated openings: DocDate = SAP go-live. Their DocDueDate is the TRUE
    -- original date (back to 2017), so the bucket is right, but a 3,000-day
    -- overdue is inherited history, not rot since go-live. Oil only.
    SUM(CASE WHEN DOCDATE = DATE'2024-09-30'        THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS MIGRATED,
    -- invoices left carrying something after the credit netting (see header)
    SUM(CASE WHEN EFFOPEN > 0                       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  AS NEFFINV,
    MIN(CASE WHEN EFFOPEN > 0 THEN DUEDATE END)                         AS OLDEST_OPEN_DUE
  FROM eff GROUP BY CARDCODE
),
rc AS (  -- unapplied customer receipts: cash banked, never knocked off an invoice
  SELECT "CardCode" AS CARDCODE,
         SUM(CAST(IFNULL("OpenBal",0) AS DOUBLE)) AS UNAPPLIED_RCPT
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.ORCT
  WHERE "DocType" = 'C' AND "Canceled" = 'N'        -- ORCT spells it "Canceled"
    AND CAST("DocDate" AS DATE) <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'
  GROUP BY "CardCode"
),
cn AS (  -- unapplied sales credit notes
  SELECT "CardCode" AS CARDCODE,
         SUM(CAST("DocTotal" - "PaidToDate" AS DOUBLE)) AS OPEN_CN
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.ORIN
  WHERE "DocStatus" = 'O' AND "CANCELED" = 'N'
    AND CAST("DocDate" AS DATE) <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'
  GROUP BY "CardCode"
),
cust AS (  -- one row per customer card, nothing dropped
  SELECT b.CARDCODE, b.KIND, b.BAL,
         IFNULL(c.TOTOPEN,0)    AS RAW_OPEN,
         IFNULL(c.NINV,0)       AS NINV,
         IFNULL(c.UNAPPLIED,0)  AS UNAPPLIED,
         IFNULL(a.EFF_OPEN,0)   AS EFF_OPEN,
         IFNULL(a.NOTDUE,0)     AS NOTDUE,
         IFNULL(a.D1_30,0)      AS D1_30,
         IFNULL(a.D31_60,0)     AS D31_60,
         IFNULL(a.D61_90,0)     AS D61_90,
         IFNULL(a.D91_180,0)    AS D91_180,
         IFNULL(a.D181_365,0)   AS D181_365,
         IFNULL(a.D365P,0)      AS D365P,
         IFNULL(a.OVERDUE,0)    AS OVERDUE,
         IFNULL(a.OD60P,0)      AS OD60P,
         IFNULL(a.MIGRATED,0)   AS MIGRATED,
         IFNULL(a.NEFFINV,0)    AS NEFFINV,
         a.OLDEST_OPEN_DUE      AS OLDEST_OPEN_DUE,
         -- debit sitting in the ledger but carried by no open invoice
         GREATEST(0, b.BAL) - IFNULL(a.EFF_OPEN,0) AS BAL_NOT_IN_INV,
         GREATEST(0, b.BAL)     AS BAL_DR,
         LEAST(0, b.BAL)        AS BAL_CR,
         IFNULL(r.UNAPPLIED_RCPT,0) AS UNAPPLIED_RCPT,
         IFNULL(n.OPEN_CN,0)        AS OPEN_CN
  FROM bp b
  LEFT JOIN cr  c ON c.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
  LEFT JOIN ag  a ON a.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
  LEFT JOIN rc  r ON r.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
  LEFT JOIN cn  n ON n.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN GROUPING(KIND) = 1 THEN 'ZZ_TOTAL' ELSE KIND END AS KIND,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN EFF_OPEN > 0 OR BAL <> 0 THEN 1 END)        AS N_CUSTOMERS,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN EFF_OPEN > 0 THEN 1 END)                    AS N_EFF_CUSTOMERS,
  SUM(NINV)                                                   AS N_OPEN_INV,
  SUM(NEFFINV)                                                AS N_EFF_INV,
  ROUND(SUM(RAW_OPEN),2)                                      AS RAW_OPEN_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(UNAPPLIED),2)                                     AS UNAPPLIED_CREDIT_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(EFF_OPEN),2)                                      AS EFF_OPEN_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(NOTDUE),2)                                        AS NOTDUE_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D1_30),2)                                         AS D1_30_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D31_60),2)                                        AS D31_60_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D61_90),2)                                        AS D61_90_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D91_180),2)                                       AS D91_180_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D181_365),2)                                      AS D181_365_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D365P),2)                                         AS D365P_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(OVERDUE),2)                                       AS OVERDUE_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(OD60P),2)                                         AS OD60P_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(MIGRATED),2)                                      AS MIGRATED_OPEN_INR,

check.method: reproduces the figure measured independently from the SQL when the section was catalogued

excludes.label: ZZ_TOTAL — the GROUPING SETS roll-up row
excludes.why: Not an exclusion of money but of a ROW: ZZ_TOTAL sits in the same array as the four KIND rows, so any consumer that sums the column without filtering gets exactly 2x.

ar-nontrade-open.label: JIVO's own accounts sitting in 'debtors' (branch + intercompany + staff)
section_traps: ZZ_TOTAL is a FIFTH ROW in the same array as BRANCH/INTERCO/STAFF/TRADE (GROUPING SETS, column KIND, literal value 'ZZ_TOTAL'). Summing any money column across all rows returns exactly 2x the truth. The TOTAL row is KIND=='ZZ_TOTAL'; every other consumer must filter by KIND. This is the section's live landmine and v1's renderer only just avoids it.

DocStatus='O' is not solvency at JIVO (C-0019). Raw open vs credit-adjusted on the TRADE book: Oil ₹75.86 Cr → ₹7.35 Cr (10.3x), Mart ₹113.84 Cr → ₹10.30 Cr (11.1x), Bev ₹5.00 Cr → ₹3.84 Cr (1.3x). Anything that reads RAW_OPEN_INR and calls it a receivable is wrong by an order of magnitude on two of the three books.

N_CUSTOMERS and N_OPEN_INV are SAP's UNCORRECTED counts. Pairing them with EFF_OPEN_INR re-commits the very error the section corrects: ₹7.35 Cr ÷ 11,499 invoices = ₹6,396 each, against the truth of ₹55,509 across 1,325. The bucket split is an ASSUMPTION, the total is a measurement. EFF_OPEN_INR is identical to the paisa whether credit is consumed oldest-first or newest-first; the BUCKETS are not. Mart's 60-day-plus figure moves from ₹30.14 L (shipped, FIFO) to ₹8.46 Cr (newest-first) — 28x. Oil 1.18x, Bev 1.01x. Never subtract UNAPPLIED_RECEIPTS_INR or OPEN_CREDIT_NOTES_INR from the receivable. They are already inside OCRD.Balance, which is what EFF_OPEN_INR is capped at. Subtracting Oil's ₹66.2 Cr of unapplied receipts from its ₹7.35 Cr trade book would produce a large negative receivable out of correct data.

EFF_OPEN_INR is capped at the ledger debit, so BAL_NOT_IN_INV_INR of trade debit is carried by no open invoice and is never aged: Oil ₹65.07 L (8.13% of the trade ledger debit), Mart ₹13.09 L (1.26%), Bev ₹45,378 (0.12%). The headline is a disclosed understatement of the debit book. Show OCRD_DEBIT_INR beside it, never instead of it.

OCRD_CREDIT_INR is stored NEGATIVE (JIVO sign convention: −ve = JIVO owes the party). Adding it to OCRD_DEBIT_INR silently nets customers in advance against customers in arrears and produces a 'net receivable' that means nothing. The detail twin CUSTOMER_ADVANCE stores the same money POSITIVE — mixing the two flips a sign.

Calling it 'debt that rotted since go-live' is wrong. The 0.00 in Mart and Bev is a TRUE zero — their first invoices are 2024-10-03 and 2024-10-04 and neither book has an opening batch — but the date is HARD-CODED and Oil-specific, so a fourth company book would need its own go-live checked.

OLDEST_OPEN_DUE / OLDEST_DUE is the oldest date that still carries money AFTER credit application, not the oldest open document. It jumps forward when a receipt is matched, and it deliberately means something different here than in vendor-ageing.sql, which reports the raw oldest bill. Do not compare the two sections' oldest dates.

sql.text:
CASE
           -- (a) JIVO's own state GST registrations: ~116 Cr of fake "debtors"
           WHEN IFNULL(g."GroupName",'') LIKE '%BRANCH%' THEN 'BRANCH'
           -- (b) the other JIVO entities/units. The C-0005 CardCode list is
           --     company-specific and the SAME code is a real shop in another
           --     book (CUSTA000874 = "JIVO MART PVT LTD - DL" in Mart but
           --     "RAKESH BROTHER" in Oil), so the code list is AND-ed with a
           --     name test. Verified live: 'JIVO%' matches every intra-group
           --     card in all 3 books and no external customer.
           WHEN UPPER(c."CardName") LIKE 'JIVO%'
             OR UPPER(c."CardName") LIKE '%A U O JWPL%'
             OR IFNULL(g."GroupName",'') IN ('PARENT COMPANY','COMPANY UNIT CUSTOMER')
             OR ( c."CardCode" IN ('CUSTA000001','CUSTA000002','CUSTA000003','CUSTA000004',
                                   'CUSTA000606','CUSTA000827','CUSTA000874','CUSTA000875',
                                   'CUSTA000876','CUSTA000877','CUSTA000878','CUSTA000906',
                                   'CUSTA000926','CUSTA001099','CUSTA001113')
                  AND UPPER(c."CardName") LIKE 'JIVO%' )
             THEN 'INTERCO'
           WHEN IFNULL(g."GroupName",'') = 'STAFF CUSTOMER' THEN 'STAFF'
           ELSE 'TRADE'
         END AS KIND
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.OCRD c
  LEFT JOIN {{SCHEMA}}.OCRG g
         ON g."GroupCode" = c."GroupCode" AND g."GroupType" = c."CardType"
  WHERE c."CardType" = 'C'
),
-- Open A/R invoices. "CANCELED" (ONE l) has 3 values here: N, Y (was cancelled)
-- and C (IS the cancelling document); only 'N' is live.
inv AS (
  SELECT "CardCode"                                 AS CARDCODE,
         "DocEntry"                                 AS DOCENTRY,
         CAST("DocDate"    AS DATE)                 AS DOCDATE,
         CAST("DocDueDate" AS DATE)                 AS DUEDATE,
         CAST("DocTotal" - "PaidToDate" AS DOUBLE)  AS OPENAMT
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.OINV
  WHERE "DocStatus" = 'O'
    AND "CANCELED"  = 'N'
    AND ("DocTotal" - "PaidToDate") > 0
    AND CAST("DocDate" AS DATE) <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'
),
tot AS (SELECT CARDCODE, SUM(OPENAMT) AS TOTOPEN, COUNT(*) AS NINV FROM inv GROUP BY CARDCODE),
cr AS (
  SELECT t.CARDCODE, t.TOTOPEN, t.NINV,
         GREATEST(0, t.TOTOPEN - GREATEST(0, IFNULL(b.BAL, t.TOTOPEN))) AS UNAPPLIED
  FROM tot t LEFT JOIN bp b ON b.CARDCODE = t.CARDCODE
),
-- oldest-first running total, so unapplied credit clears the oldest invoice first
run AS (
  SELECT i.CARDCODE, i.DOCDATE, i.DUEDATE, i.OPENAMT, c.UNAPPLIED,
         SUM(i.OPENAMT) OVER (PARTITION BY i.CARDCODE
                              ORDER BY i.DUEDATE, i.DOCENTRY
                              ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS CUM
  FROM inv i JOIN cr c ON c.CARDCODE = i.CARDCODE
),
eff AS (
  SELECT CARDCODE, DOCDATE, DUEDATE,
         DAYS_BETWEEN(DUEDATE, DATE'{{ASOF}}')       AS DAYS_OD,
         GREATEST(0, LEAST(OPENAMT, CUM - UNAPPLIED)) AS EFFOPEN
  FROM run
),
ag AS (
  SELECT CARDCODE,
    SUM(EFFOPEN)                                                        AS EFF_OPEN,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_OD <=   0                    THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS NOTDUE,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_OD BETWEEN   1 AND  30       THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS D1_30,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_OD BETWEEN  31 AND  60       THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS D31_60,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_OD BETWEEN  61 AND  90       THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS D61_90,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_OD BETWEEN  91 AND 180       THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS D91_180,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_OD BETWEEN 181 AND 365       THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS D181_365,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_OD > 365                     THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS D365P,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_OD >   0                     THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS OVERDUE,
    SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_OD >  60                     THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS OD60P,
    -- migrated openings: DocDate = SAP go-live. Their DocDueDate is the TRUE
    -- original date (back to 2017), so the bucket is right, but a 3,000-day
    -- overdue is inherited history, not rot since go-live. Oil only.
    SUM(CASE WHEN DOCDATE = DATE'2024-09-30'        THEN EFFOPEN ELSE 0 END) AS MIGRATED,
    -- invoices left carrying something after the credit netting (see header)
    SUM(CASE WHEN EFFOPEN > 0                       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  AS NEFFINV,
    MIN(CASE WHEN EFFOPEN > 0 THEN DUEDATE END)                         AS OLDEST_OPEN_DUE
  FROM eff GROUP BY CARDCODE
),
rc AS (  -- unapplied customer receipts: cash banked, never knocked off an invoice
  SELECT "CardCode" AS CARDCODE,
         SUM(CAST(IFNULL("OpenBal",0) AS DOUBLE)) AS UNAPPLIED_RCPT
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.ORCT
  WHERE "DocType" = 'C' AND "Canceled" = 'N'        -- ORCT spells it "Canceled"
    AND CAST("DocDate" AS DATE) <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'
  GROUP BY "CardCode"
),
cn AS (  -- unapplied sales credit notes
  SELECT "CardCode" AS CARDCODE,
         SUM(CAST("DocTotal" - "PaidToDate" AS DOUBLE)) AS OPEN_CN
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.ORIN
  WHERE "DocStatus" = 'O' AND "CANCELED" = 'N'
    AND CAST("DocDate" AS DATE) <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'
  GROUP BY "CardCode"
),
cust AS (  -- one row per customer card, nothing dropped
  SELECT b.CARDCODE, b.KIND, b.BAL,
         IFNULL(c.TOTOPEN,0)    AS RAW_OPEN,
         IFNULL(c.NINV,0)       AS NINV,
         IFNULL(c.UNAPPLIED,0)  AS UNAPPLIED,
         IFNULL(a.EFF_OPEN,0)   AS EFF_OPEN,
         IFNULL(a.NOTDUE,0)     AS NOTDUE,
         IFNULL(a.D1_30,0)      AS D1_30,
         IFNULL(a.D31_60,0)     AS D31_60,
         IFNULL(a.D61_90,0)     AS D61_90,
         IFNULL(a.D91_180,0)    AS D91_180,
         IFNULL(a.D181_365,0)   AS D181_365,
         IFNULL(a.D365P,0)      AS D365P,
         IFNULL(a.OVERDUE,0)    AS OVERDUE,
         IFNULL(a.OD60P,0)      AS OD60P,
         IFNULL(a.MIGRATED,0)   AS MIGRATED,
         IFNULL(a.NEFFINV,0)    AS NEFFINV,
         a.OLDEST_OPEN_DUE      AS OLDEST_OPEN_DUE,
         -- debit sitting in the ledger but carried by no open invoice
         GREATEST(0, b.BAL) - IFNULL(a.EFF_OPEN,0) AS BAL_NOT_IN_INV,
         GREATEST(0, b.BAL)     AS BAL_DR,
         LEAST(0, b.BAL)        AS BAL_CR,
         IFNULL(r.UNAPPLIED_RCPT,0) AS UNAPPLIED_RCPT,
         IFNULL(n.OPEN_CN,0)        AS OPEN_CN
  FROM bp b
  LEFT JOIN cr  c ON c.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
  LEFT JOIN ag  a ON a.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
  LEFT JOIN rc  r ON r.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
  LEFT JOIN cn  n ON n.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
)

  CASE WHEN GROUPING(KIND) = 1 THEN 'ZZ_TOTAL' ELSE KIND END AS KIND,

caveats.right: At JIVO a document stays DocStatus='O' long after the money moved, because settlements are posted as manual journal entries (JDT1.TransType=30) and as on-account ORCT/OVPM receipts and payments that are never internally reconciled to the document. OCRD.Balance is the only ground truth for what a party owes or is owed. Measured live 2026-08-21, open documents vs OCRD balances: Oil A/R 180.69 vs 109.51 Cr and A/P 309.20 vs 102.63 Cr; Mart A/R 128.12 vs 23.35 Cr and A/P 219.60 vs 29.22 Cr; Bev A/R 6.34 vs 4.83 Cr and A/P 3.56 vs 2.24 Cr. Overstatement 1.3x to 7.5x, worst on Mart payables. Correct method: take the party balance as the real exposure, derive unapplied credit as sum(open docs) - balance, consume it oldest-due-first, then bucket the remainder.
caveats.rule: SAP DocStatus='O' is unreliable at JIVO: documents settled by manual JE or unapplied on-account payment stay open. Age from OCRD.Balance, not open documents - naive ageing overstates 1.3-7.5x.
caveats.title: DocStatus='O' is unreliable — age from OCRD.Balance, not open documents
caveats.wrong: Built an ageing by summing open documents (OINV/OPCH DocStatus='O', DocTotal-PaidToDate) and bucketing on DocDueDate, treating 'open' as 'unpaid'.

ar-oldest-item-days.formula: as_of − MIN(DocDueDate where EFFOPEN > 0), in days
ar-oldest-item-days.label: Age of the oldest item still carrying money
ar-oldest-item-days.method: age in days: newest from OLDEST_OPEN_DUE to the as-of date
section_traps: ZZ_TOTAL is a FIFTH ROW in the same array as BRANCH/INTERCO/STAFF/TRADE (GROUPING SETS, column KIND, literal value 'ZZ_TOTAL'). Summing any money column across all rows returns exactly 2x the truth. The TOTAL row is KIND=='ZZ_TOTAL'; every other consumer must filter by KIND. This is the section's live landmine and v1's renderer only just avoids it.

DocStatus='O' is not solvency at JIVO (C-0019). Raw open vs credit-adjusted on the TRADE book: Oil ₹75.86 Cr → ₹7.35 Cr (10.3x), Mart ₹113.84 Cr → ₹10.30 Cr (11.1x), Bev ₹5.00 Cr → ₹3.84 Cr (1.3x). Anything that reads RAW_OPEN_INR and calls it a receivable is wrong by an order of magnitude on two of the three books.

N_CUSTOMERS and N_OPEN_INV are SAP's UNCORRECTED counts. Pairing them with EFF_OPEN_INR re-commits the very error the section corrects: ₹7.35 Cr ÷ 11,499 invoices = ₹6,396 each, against the truth of ₹55,509 across 1,325. Use N_EFF_CUSTOMERS and N_EFF_INV; show the SAP count struck through if at all.

The bucket split is an ASSUMPTION, the total is a measurement. EFF_OPEN_INR is identical to the paisa whether credit is consumed oldest-first or newest-first; the BUCKETS are not. Mart's 60-day-plus figure moves from ₹30.14 L (shipped, FIFO) to ₹8.46 Cr (newest-first) — 28x. Oil 1.18x, Bev 1.01x. Every overdue figure on this page is a LOWER BOUND and must say so, Mart loudest.

Never subtract UNAPPLIED_RECEIPTS_INR or OPEN_CREDIT_NOTES_INR from the receivable. They are already inside OCRD.Balance, which is what EFF_OPEN_INR is capped at. Subtracting Oil's ₹66.2 Cr of unapplied receipts from its ₹7.35 Cr trade book would produce a large negative receivable out of correct data.

EFF_OPEN_INR is capped at the ledger debit, so BAL_NOT_IN_INV_INR of trade debit is carried by no open invoice and is never aged: Oil ₹65.07 L (8.13% of the trade ledger debit), Mart ₹13.09 L (1.26%), Bev ₹45,378 (0.12%). The headline is a disclosed understatement of the debit book. Show OCRD_DEBIT_INR beside it, never instead of it.

OCRD_CREDIT_INR is stored NEGATIVE (JIVO sign convention: −ve = JIVO owes the party). Adding it to OCRD_DEBIT_INR silently nets customers in advance against customers in arrears and produces a 'net receivable' that means nothing. The detail twin CUSTOMER_ADVANCE stores the same money POSITIVE — mixing the two flips a sign.

MIGRATED_OPEN_INR: Oil's 365-day-plus TRADE bucket is 96.6% migrated pre-SAP openings (invoices dated exactly at go-live 2024-09-30, carrying true original due dates back to 2017). Calling it 'debt that rotted since go-live' is wrong. The 0.00 in Mart and Bev is a TRUE zero — their first invoices are 2024-10-03 and 2024-10-04 and neither book has an opening batch — but the date is HARD-CODED and Oil-specific, so a fourth company book would need its own go-live checked.

OLDEST_OPEN_DUE / OLDEST_DUE is the oldest date that still carries money AFTER credit application, not the oldest open document. It jumps forward when a receipt is matched, and it deliberately means something different here than in vendor-ageing.sql, which reports the raw oldest bill. Do not compare the two sections' oldest dates.

The detail row count is NOT N_CUSTOMERS and must never be asserted equal. The detail keeps cards that exist only as an unapplied receipt or an open credit note (642 Oil rows vs 379 counted), and 25 Oil / 3 Mart / 9 Bev cards carry sub-paise dust balances that are <>0 in SQL but round to 0.00 at 2 dp. N_EFF_CUSTOMERS for Oil TRADE is 89 while detail rows with ADJ_OPEN>0 number 85 — same dust. Assert the money, never the headcount.

Classification divergences that are real and deliberately unfixed: Oil CUSTA000242 AKAL INFORMATION SYSTEMS LTD (group DEBTORS, ₹10,000) reads TRADE here and INTERCO in both vendor-ageing.sql and open-item-list.sql — verified live 2026-08-22, the one ACCT_KIND mismatch across 229 shared Oil cards. And 8-9 employee imprest cards filed in a STATE group instead of 'STAFF CUSTOMER' read TRADE (Oil ₹3,555 · Mart ₹1,957 · Bev ₹11,562 incl. CUSTA000902 NAVNEET SINGH, which has no 'IMPREST' in its name). Fixing either in one file without the other breaks the summary↔detail tie.

CUSTA000356 'FREE SAMPLE' is classified TRADE in all three books and carries a real ageing (Oil ₹91,239 with ₹85,509 over 60 days; Bev ₹57,809). Nothing in OCRG or the card name marks it internal. It is almost certainly not collectable and it has never been checked with Accounts — do not put it on a collection list without a footnote.

UNAPPLIED_RCPT can be NEGATIVE by a rounding paisa (Oil CUSTA000482 METRO CASH & CARRY = −0.01). Any treemap, log scale or sqrt-area chart over that column must clamp, and a 'top unmatched receipts' sort must not assume the column is non-negative.

Cross-section: open-item-list's CARD_OPEN_GROSS is NOT this section's RAW_OPEN — it folds unapplied receipts into 'gross open'. Oil CUSTA000844 ILAHI CO. reads ₹44.71 L there and ₹24.71 L here, a ₹20 L AR receipt. Its CARD_BALANCE, however, IS the same OCRD.Balance and matched on 229/21/220 shared cards with zero mismatches — that column is a valid cross-file check, CARD_OPEN_GROSS is not.

A back-dated {{ASOF}} is not a point-in-time A/R. OCRD.Balance and PaidToDate are the CURRENT snapshot — SAP keeps no per-date history — so a past as-of ages today's open items against an older calendar. Measured on Oil: --as-of 2026-03-31 gives ₹80.34 Cr adjusted against ₹108.86 Cr today, and ₹2.87 Cr of trade against ₹7.43 Cr. The cut-off is on DocDate only, so an invoice cancelled yesterday vanishes from a last-month run.

Group totals are NOT intercompany-eliminated. Oil, Mart and Bev trade with each other and each book carries the other as a customer; adding the three EFF_OPEN_INR figures double-counts JIVO's own money. Per-company is the only figure that means anything, and the INTERCO row names the amount in each book.

A KIND row with NOTDUE_INR = 0 and EFF_OPEN_INR > 0 is REAL, not a missing bucket: Oil BRANCH, Mart BRANCH/INTERCO/STAFF and Bev BRANCH/INTERCO are 100% overdue. Rendering that as an empty bar or 'no data' misreports a book that is entirely past due.

Every CO_* column in the detail (CO_RAW_OPEN … CO_ADJ_OVERDUE_60PLUS_TRADE) is a company-level total repeated on EVERY row by SUM() OVER (). Read one row. Summing the column multiplies it by 642 / 100 / 451.

data.json is being rewritten under readers roughly every 2 minutes by the VPS refresh loop. A consumer that reads the file twice in one pass can mix two builds — I hit exactly this and briefly saw ZZ_TOTAL disagree with the sum of its KIND rows by ₹40.32 L. Load once into memory, and stamp every derived figure with the generated_at it came from.

sql.text:
MIN(CASE WHEN EFFOPEN > 0 THEN DUEDATE END)                         AS OLDEST_OPEN_DUE
  FROM eff GROUP BY CARDCODE
),
rc AS (  -- unapplied customer receipts: cash banked, never knocked off an invoice
  SELECT "CardCode" AS CARDCODE,
         SUM(CAST(IFNULL("OpenBal",0) AS DOUBLE)) AS UNAPPLIED_RCPT
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.ORCT
  WHERE "DocType" = 'C' AND "Canceled" = 'N'        -- ORCT spells it "Canceled"
    AND CAST("DocDate" AS DATE) <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'
  GROUP BY "CardCode"
),
cn AS (  -- unapplied sales credit notes
  SELECT "CardCode" AS CARDCODE,
         SUM(CAST("DocTotal" - "PaidToDate" AS DOUBLE)) AS OPEN_CN
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.ORIN
  WHERE "DocStatus" = 'O' AND "CANCELED" = 'N'
    AND CAST("DocDate" AS DATE) <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'
  GROUP BY "CardCode"
),
cust AS (  -- one row per customer card, nothing dropped
  SELECT b.CARDCODE, b.KIND, b.BAL,
         IFNULL(c.TOTOPEN,0)    AS RAW_OPEN,
         IFNULL(c.NINV,0)       AS NINV,
         IFNULL(c.UNAPPLIED,0)  AS UNAPPLIED,
         IFNULL(a.EFF_OPEN,0)   AS EFF_OPEN,
         IFNULL(a.NOTDUE,0)     AS NOTDUE,
         IFNULL(a.D1_30,0)      AS D1_30,
         IFNULL(a.D31_60,0)     AS D31_60,
         IFNULL(a.D61_90,0)     AS D61_90,
         IFNULL(a.D91_180,0)    AS D91_180,
         IFNULL(a.D181_365,0)   AS D181_365,
         IFNULL(a.D365P,0)      AS D365P,
         IFNULL(a.OVERDUE,0)    AS OVERDUE,
         IFNULL(a.OD60P,0)      AS OD60P,
         IFNULL(a.MIGRATED,0)   AS MIGRATED,
         IFNULL(a.NEFFINV,0)    AS NEFFINV,
         a.OLDEST_OPEN_DUE      AS OLDEST_OPEN_DUE,
         -- debit sitting in the ledger but carried by no open invoice
         GREATEST(0, b.BAL) - IFNULL(a.EFF_OPEN,0) AS BAL_NOT_IN_INV,
         GREATEST(0, b.BAL)     AS BAL_DR,
         LEAST(0, b.BAL)        AS BAL_CR,
         IFNULL(r.UNAPPLIED_RCPT,0) AS UNAPPLIED_RCPT,
         IFNULL(n.OPEN_CN,0)        AS OPEN_CN
  FROM bp b
  LEFT JOIN cr  c ON c.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
  LEFT JOIN ag  a ON a.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
  LEFT JOIN rc  r ON r.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
  LEFT JOIN cn  n ON n.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN GROUPING(KIND) = 1 THEN 'ZZ_TOTAL' ELSE KIND END AS KIND,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN EFF_OPEN > 0 OR BAL <> 0 THEN 1 END)        AS N_CUSTOMERS,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN EFF_OPEN > 0 THEN 1 END)                    AS N_EFF_CUSTOMERS,
  SUM(NINV)                                                   AS N_OPEN_INV,
  SUM(NEFFINV)                                                AS N_EFF_INV,
  ROUND(SUM(RAW_OPEN),2)                                      AS RAW_OPEN_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(UNAPPLIED),2)                                     AS UNAPPLIED_CREDIT_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(EFF_OPEN),2)                                      AS EFF_OPEN_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(NOTDUE),2)                                        AS NOTDUE_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D1_30),2)                                         AS D1_30_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D31_60),2)                                        AS D31_60_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D61_90),2)                                        AS D61_90_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D91_180),2)                                       AS D91_180_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D181_365),2)                                      AS D181_365_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D365P),2)                                         AS D365P_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(OVERDUE),2)                                       AS OVERDUE_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(OD60P),2)                                         AS OD60P_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(MIGRATED),2)                                      AS MIGRATED_OPEN_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(BAL_NOT_IN_INV),2)                                AS BAL_NOT_IN_INV_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(BAL_DR),2)                                        AS OCRD_DEBIT_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(BAL_CR),2)                                        AS OCRD_CREDIT_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(UNAPPLIED_RCPT),2)                                AS UNAPPLIED_RECEIPTS_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(OPEN_CN),2)                                       AS OPEN_CREDIT_NOTES_INR,
  MIN(OLDEST_OPEN_DUE)                                        AS OLDEST_OPEN_DUE

terms.label: Oldest effective due date
terms.note: AFTER credit application, so it moves when a receipt is matched. It is NOT the oldest open document — vendor-ageing.sql reports the raw oldest bill and the two files deliberately differ.

caveats.right: In the HANA tables the flag has THREE values: 'N' = live, 'Y' = the cancelled original, and 'C' = the system-generated cancellation mirror SAP posts to reverse it. Y and C always appear as exact matching pairs carrying the same value, so a <>'Y' test keeps every mirror and double-counts. Measured live on Oil 2026-08-21: OINV 30,387 'N' (1045.62 Cr) plus 320 'Y' and 320 'C' at 37.27 Cr each; OPCH 16,101 'N' plus 113+113 at 15.96 Cr each; OPDN 10,640 'N' plus 473+473 at 94.63 Cr each; ORDN 1,817 'N' plus 107+107 at 0.49 Cr each. Same pattern in Mart and Beverages. Always test CANCELED='N' positively. Note the Service Layer differs: it exposes only Cancelled 'tYES'/'tNO', so the documented OData filter Cancelled eq 'tNO' is already correct and is not affected.
caveats.rule: HANA "CANCELED" is three-valued: 'N' live, 'Y' cancelled original, 'C' its system mirror. Always filter CANCELED='N' - a <>'Y' test keeps the mirrors and double-counts (Oil OPDN +94.63 Cr).
caveats.title: HANA CANCELED is three-valued — filter ='N', never <>'Y'
caveats.wrong: Excluded cancelled documents in HANA SQL by writing "CANCELED" <> 'Y' (or omitting the filter), assuming the flag is a two-valued Y/N.

sql.text:
cn AS (  -- unapplied sales credit notes
  SELECT "CardCode" AS CARDCODE,
         SUM(CAST("DocTotal" - "PaidToDate" AS DOUBLE)) AS OPEN_CN
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.ORIN
  WHERE "DocStatus" = 'O' AND "CANCELED" = 'N'
    AND CAST("DocDate" AS DATE) <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'
  GROUP BY "CardCode"
),
cust AS (  -- one row per customer card, nothing dropped
  SELECT b.CARDCODE, b.KIND, b.BAL,
         IFNULL(c.TOTOPEN,0)    AS RAW_OPEN,
         IFNULL(c.NINV,0)       AS NINV,
         IFNULL(c.UNAPPLIED,0)  AS UNAPPLIED,
         IFNULL(a.EFF_OPEN,0)   AS EFF_OPEN,
         IFNULL(a.NOTDUE,0)     AS NOTDUE,
         IFNULL(a.D1_30,0)      AS D1_30,
         IFNULL(a.D31_60,0)     AS D31_60,
         IFNULL(a.D61_90,0)     AS D61_90,
         IFNULL(a.D91_180,0)    AS D91_180,
         IFNULL(a.D181_365,0)   AS D181_365,
         IFNULL(a.D365P,0)      AS D365P,
         IFNULL(a.OVERDUE,0)    AS OVERDUE,
         IFNULL(a.OD60P,0)      AS OD60P,
         IFNULL(a.MIGRATED,0)   AS MIGRATED,
         IFNULL(a.NEFFINV,0)    AS NEFFINV,
         a.OLDEST_OPEN_DUE      AS OLDEST_OPEN_DUE,
         -- debit sitting in the ledger but carried by no open invoice
         GREATEST(0, b.BAL) - IFNULL(a.EFF_OPEN,0) AS BAL_NOT_IN_INV,
         GREATEST(0, b.BAL)     AS BAL_DR,
         LEAST(0, b.BAL)        AS BAL_CR,
         IFNULL(r.UNAPPLIED_RCPT,0) AS UNAPPLIED_RCPT,
         IFNULL(n.OPEN_CN,0)        AS OPEN_CN
  FROM bp b
  LEFT JOIN cr  c ON c.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
  LEFT JOIN ag  a ON a.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
  LEFT JOIN rc  r ON r.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
  LEFT JOIN cn  n ON n.CARDCODE = b.CARDCODE
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN GROUPING(KIND) = 1 THEN 'ZZ_TOTAL' ELSE KIND END AS KIND,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN EFF_OPEN > 0 OR BAL <> 0 THEN 1 END)        AS N_CUSTOMERS,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN EFF_OPEN > 0 THEN 1 END)                    AS N_EFF_CUSTOMERS,
  SUM(NINV)                                                   AS N_OPEN_INV,
  SUM(NEFFINV)                                                AS N_EFF_INV,
  ROUND(SUM(RAW_OPEN),2)                                      AS RAW_OPEN_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(UNAPPLIED),2)                                     AS UNAPPLIED_CREDIT_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(EFF_OPEN),2)                                      AS EFF_OPEN_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(NOTDUE),2)                                        AS NOTDUE_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D1_30),2)                                         AS D1_30_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D31_60),2)                                        AS D31_60_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D61_90),2)                                        AS D61_90_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D91_180),2)                                       AS D91_180_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D181_365),2)                                      AS D181_365_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(D365P),2)                                         AS D365P_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(OVERDUE),2)                                       AS OVERDUE_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(OD60P),2)                                         AS OD60P_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(MIGRATED),2)                                      AS MIGRATED_OPEN_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(BAL_NOT_IN_INV),2)                                AS BAL_NOT_IN_INV_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(BAL_DR),2)                                        AS OCRD_DEBIT_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(BAL_CR),2)                                        AS OCRD_CREDIT_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(UNAPPLIED_RCPT),2)                                AS UNAPPLIED_RECEIPTS_INR,
  ROUND(SUM(OPEN_CN),2)                                       AS OPEN_CREDIT_NOTES_INR,
