rows.filter: r.get('DOCTYPE')=='AR_INV'  # read off the FIRST such row only

section_traps: CO_*, DT_* and CARD_* are BROADCAST AGGREGATES repeated on every row they describe. Summing CO_OPEN_ALL down the oil slice gives Rs 5,60,806 Cr instead of Rs 2,586.70 Cr — a 2,168x overstatement. Read CO_* off summary[0], DT_* off the first row of each DOCTYPE, CARD_* off the first row of each CARD_CODE. The only per-row money columns are DOC_TOTAL, APPLIED, OPEN_AMT, SIGNED_OPEN, OPEN_AMT_FC, ITEM_REAL_EST, OITR_RECON_AMT.

THE ROW SET IS CAPPED AND FLOORED, and nothing in the row data says so except CO_ITEMS_SHOWN vs CO_ITEMS_ALL. Only documents with OPEN_AMT >= Rs 10,000 that rank in the company's top 1,500 or their own doctype's top 400 are delivered — 2,168 of 23,240 (oil), 2,188 of 10,105 (mart), 1,096 of 2,212 (bev). Any KPI computed by summing the delivered rows is a SHOWN-SET figure and must be labelled as one. This is exactly the v1 bug the notes record: the doctype bar chart summed shown rows under an uncapped headline, drawing Rs 2,516 Cr of bars beneath a Rs 2,582 Cr number.

CO_OPEN_ALL IS NOT MONEY OWED, AND IS THE MOST DANGEROUS NUMBER ON THE BOARD. Oil shows Rs 2,586.70 Cr of open documents against Rs 12.89 Cr of actual ledger balance across the same parties — a 200x gap. Two causes, both measured: 76.6% is migration openings dated 2024-09-30, and the rest is DocStatus='O' being unreliable at JIVO because bills are settled by manual journal entry or unmatched on-account payments (C-0019). The receivable and payable figures come from customer-ageing / vendor-ageing, which anchor on OCRD.Balance. Every panel that shows CO_OPEN_ALL must carry that sentence.

DOCTYPE AND SIDE ARE DIFFERENT AXES. DOCTYPE names the SAP table; SIDE names the party's ledger side, derived from the payment's own DocType. Filtering by DOCTYPE='AR_RCT' when you meant 'customer receipts' pulls in ORCT rows with DocType='S' — cash received back FROM A VENDOR — worth Rs 2.25 Cr across 146 oil documents. Mirror image: 26 oil OVPM rows (Rs 25.86 L) are refunds paid TO A CUSTOMER and are SIDE='AR'. This was defect D1; after the fix SIDE agrees with OCRD.CardType on 100% of rows, so any disagreement is now a hard defect signal.

DAYS_OVERDUE AND AGE_DAYS DISAGREE BY YEARS ON MIGRATED ROWS, and both are correct. Oil's worst row is dated 2024-09-30 (691 days old) with a true original due date of 2020-02-19 (2,376 days overdue). AGE_BUCKET is cut on DAYS_OVERDUE, so 87.9% of Oil's shown value lands in 365+ largely because of pre-go-live due dates. Never write 'this document is N days old' from DAYS_OVERDUE, and never write 'N days overdue' from AGE_DAYS. On payments (AR_RCT/AP_PMT) DUE_DATE is the payment's own and means nothing as a deadline — AGE_DAYS is the honest field there.

ITEM_REAL_EST MUST BE SUMMED SIGNED OR NOT AT ALL. It is OPEN_AMT × CARD_REAL_PCT/100, and CARD_REAL_PCT is a ratio of NETS applied to GROSS amounts. A card whose large debits and credits offset gets 100% and every one of its rows is estimated at its full face value: Mart's VENDA000001 sums to Rs 347.86 Cr of 'really open' against a card balance of −Rs 20.93 Cr. Gross-summing it across Mart's shown rows yields Rs 505.88 Cr against a CO_OCRD_NET of −Rs 9.39 Cr, which is nonsense. 233 of 421 oil cards, 17 of 50 mart, 43 of 306 bev overstate this way. SUM(SGN × ITEM_REAL_EST) per card = sign(net) × min(|net|,|balance|) — verified on all 265 fully-contained cards — and that is the only defensible total. Recommendation: do NOT publish a company-level 'really open' KPI from this column; expose it per row and per card only.

OPEN_AMT_FC IS NOT RUPEES AND ITS COLUMN IS NOT ADDABLE. OPEN_AMT is always local INR; OPEN_AMT_FC is the same item in its own currency, so totalling the column adds USD to EUR to zero. 107 oil rows are non-INR and they are Rs 2,103.78 Cr of the Rs 2,519.74 Cr shown — 83% of the book is exchange-rate exposed. Worse, rows with a rotten DocRate are INVISIBLE: Oil OVPM 26317 books USD 44.34 L as Rs 443.40 (~87,000x too small) and sinks below the Rs 10,000 floor entirely. One such row was found; no systematic sweep was run.

OITR_RECON_AMT CAN EXCEED THE DOCUMENT'S OWN TOTAL AND THAT IS NOT A BUG. SAP writes account-level system reconciliations that stamp the reconciliation's whole total onto each participant line, so 87 oil / 14 mart / 1 bev documents legitimately carry more reconciliation than value. It is a DIAGNOSTIC, never a settlement figure, and it is never used to compute OPEN_AMT. It is also easy to break: the naive SUM over ITR1's signed lines double-counted settlements written on both IsCredit sides and fired FULL_PER_OITR on documents SAP had not reconciled (128 impossible rows and Rs 18.24 Cr of phantom excess in Oil before defect D2 was fixed). If the impossible-row count jumps back toward 128, the GREATEST(D,C) guard has been removed.

MART'S SHOWN LIST IS 67.2% INTERCOMPANY BY VALUE (Rs 356.62 Cr of Rs 530.98 Cr), 68.2% once its BRANCH cards are added (Rs 362.29 Cr = the IS_GROUP=1 figure) — and VENDA000001 'JIVO WELLNESS PVT LTD' alone is Rs 347.86 Cr across 1,070 documents. Any Mart headline read without ACCT_KIND in front of it is mostly JIVO trading with itself (C-0005). Oil is 6.8% group (BRANCH 5.1% + INTERCO 1.7%), Bev 11.6% (BRANCH 11.1% + INTERCO 0.5%). Group parties are flagged and kept here, never dropped — the board must let the reader subtract them consciously.

BPL_NAME IS INCONSISTENTLY CASED IN SAP. Oil carries both 'FACTORY' and 'Factory' and both 'DELHI' and 'Delhi'; Bev carries 'FACTORY'/'Factory', 'DELHI'/'Delhi' and 'Punjab'. Grouping without UPPER() splits one branch into two bars and understates the larger one.

EXT_REF IS NULL ON EVERY PAYMENT ROW and on many invoices — 1,344 of 2,168 oil rows, 909 of 2,188 mart, 883 of 1,096 bev. It is the ONLY nullable column in the 51. A naive String(v) prints the literal 'None'.

OBJ_TYPE AND DOC_ENTRY ARRIVE WITH MIXED JSON TYPES. The SQL declares OBJ_TYPE as a string but data.json holds it as an INTEGER (13, 14, 18, 19, 24, 46), while DOC_ENTRY — a numeric key in SAP — arrives as a STRING. Cast both before building a document URL or the link silently 404s.

AS_OF FILTERS DocDate ONLY. PaidToDate, OpenBal and OCRD.Balance are live values with no history in these tables, so a back-dated run gives 'documents that existed on that date, with today's settlement state' — not the open position as it stood. Measured on Oil: --as-of 2026-03-31 reports Rs 80.34 Cr adjusted receivable against Rs 108.86 Cr today. Never label a back-dated run as a closing position.

STAFF IS A GROUP-NAME TEST ONLY, so employee imprest cards filed under a geography group (ORGC000031 'ARVINDER SINGH IMPREST JWPL0115', group DELHI) come out as TRADE. Measured cost: 11 items / Rs 1.27 L (oil), 2 / Rs 1,957 (mart), 6 / Rs 11,562 (bev). Immaterial, deliberately left — but do not present the TRADE figure as 'purely external' without this footnote.

NEGATIVE OpenBal ROWS ARE SILENTLY DROPPED by the > 0 filter: 2 oil rows (−Rs 0.91), 2 mart (−Rs 1,025), 0 bev. Total Rs 1,025.91 across all three books. Immaterial, but it is why the ORCT/OVPM totals here differ by exactly that amount from a raw table scan.

data.json MOVES UNDER YOU. The VPS rebuilds it every 2 minutes. Between 18:58:48 and 19:05:02 on 2026-08-22 Oil's CO_OPEN_ALL moved +Rs 40.32 L on a single new A/R invoice — and CO_OCRD_NET moved by the identical amount, leaving CO_STALE_GAP unchanged, which is exactly the behaviour a correct pipeline should show. Any regression test must compare shape and identities, not frozen paise.

sql.text:
SELECT 'AR_INV' AS DOCTYPE, 'AR' AS SIDE, 1 AS SGN, '13' AS OBJ_TYPE,
         "DocEntry" AS DOC_ENTRY, "DocNum" AS DOC_NUM,
         CAST(IFNULL("NumAtCard",'') AS NVARCHAR(100)) AS EXT_REF,
         "CardCode" AS CARD_CODE, "BPLId" AS BPL_ID,
         CAST(IFNULL("BPLName",'') AS NVARCHAR(200)) AS BPL_NAME,
         CAST("DocDate" AS DATE) AS DOC_DATE, CAST("DocDueDate" AS DATE) AS DUE_DATE,
         CAST("DocTotal" AS DOUBLE) AS DOC_TOTAL,
         CAST("PaidToDate" AS DOUBLE) AS APPLIED,
         CAST("DocTotal" - "PaidToDate" AS DOUBLE) AS OPEN_AMT,
         CAST("DocCur" AS NVARCHAR(3)) AS CURRENCY,
         CAST(IFNULL("DocTotalFC",0) - IFNULL("PaidFC",0) AS DOUBLE) AS OPEN_AMT_FC
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.OINV
  WHERE "CANCELED" = 'N' AND "DocStatus" = 'O'
    AND CAST("DocTotal" - "PaidToDate" AS DOUBLE) > 0
    AND CAST("DocDate" AS DATE) <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'

OCRD.Balance is the only ground truth for what a party owes or is owed. Measured live 2026-08-21, open documents vs OCRD balances: Oil A/R 180.69 vs 109.51 Cr and A/P 309.20 vs 102.63 Cr; Mart A/R 128.12 vs 23.35 Cr and A/P 219.60 vs 29.22 Cr; Bev A/R 6.34 vs 4.83 Cr and A/P 3.56 vs 2.24 Cr. Overstatement 1.3x to 7.5x, worst on Mart payables. Correct method: take the party balance as the real exposure, derive unapplied credit as sum(open docs) - balance, consume it oldest-due-first, then bucket the remainder.

OCRD.Balance is the only ground truth for what a party owes or is owed. Measured live 2026-08-21, open documents vs OCRD balances: Oil A/R 180.69 vs 109.51 Cr and A/P 309.20 vs 102.63 Cr; Mart A/R 128.12 vs 23.35 Cr and A/P 219.60 vs 29.22 Cr; Bev A/R 6.34 vs 4.83 Cr and A/P 3.56 vs 2.24 Cr. Overstatement 1.3x to 7.5x, worst on Mart payables. Correct method: take the party balance as the real exposure, derive unapplied credit as sum(open docs) - balance, consume it oldest-due-first, then bucket the remainder.

caveats.wrong: Built an ageing by summing open documents (OINV/OPCH DocStatus='O', DocTotal-PaidToDate) and bucketing on DocDueDate, treating 'open' as 'unpaid'.

caveats.right: In the HANA tables the flag has THREE values: 'N' = live, 'Y' = the cancelled original, and 'C' = the system-generated cancellation mirror SAP posts to reverse it. Y and C always appear as exact matching pairs carrying the same value, so a <>'Y' test keeps every mirror and double-counts. Measured live on Oil 2026-08-21: OINV 30,387 'N' (1045.62 Cr) plus 320 'Y' and 320 'C' at 37.27 Cr each; OPCH 16,101 'N' plus 113+113 at 15.96 Cr each; OPDN 10,640 'N' plus 473+473 at 94.63 Cr each; ORDN 1,817 'N' plus 107+107 at 0.49 Cr each. Note the Service Layer differs: it exposes only Cancelled 'tYES'/'tNO', so the documented OData filter Cancelled eq 'tNO' is already correct and is not affected.

caveats.wrong: Excluded cancelled documents in HANA SQL by writing "CANCELED" <> 'Y' (or omitting the filter), assuming the flag is a two-valued Y/N.

caveats.right: There are 23 related-party customer cards across the three companies (Oil 9, Mart 8, Beverages 6). All of them are group entities, so all of them are intercompany. Exclude the whole set, not one card, and name which cards were excluded.
caveats.rule: Intercompany is 23 group CardCodes, not just CUSTA000606: Oil CUSTA000001/2/3/4/606/827/906/1099/1113, Mart CUSTA000001/827/874/875/876/877/878/926, Bev CUSTA000001/2/3/4/606/827. Exclude all; name them.
caveats.title: Intercompany is 23 group cards, not just CUSTA000606
caveats.wrong: Split external vs intercompany by excluding only CUSTA000606 (JIVO MART PVT LTD), per C-0002. That leaves every other group card counted as an outside customer — JIVO WELLNESS DL/HR/PB/HP, JIVO MART HR/DL/PB/KR/RJ/UP/ISD, JIVO BEVERAGES-CUST. June-2026 olive: Mart 'external' came out Rs 10.47 Cr excluding only CUSTA000606, against Rs 9.53 Cr excluding all eight of Mart's group cards — a Rs 1.53 Cr overstatement of outside business.

caveats.right: On the vendor side several intercompany accounts sit in ordinary trading groups, so a group-only test silently counts JIVO's own money as external trade payable. section_traps: CO_*, DT_* and CARD_* are BROADCAST AGGREGATES repeated on every row they describe. Summing CO_OPEN_ALL down the oil slice gives Rs 5,60,806 Cr instead of Rs 2,586.70 Cr — a 2,168x overstatement. Read CO_* off summary[0], DT_* off the first row of each DOCTYPE, CARD_* off the first row of each CARD_CODE. The only per-row money columns are DOC_TOTAL, APPLIED, OPEN_AMT, SIGNED_OPEN, OPEN_AMT_FC, ITEM_REAL_EST, OITR_RECON_AMT.

THE ROW SET IS CAPPED AND FLOORED, and nothing in the row data says so except CO_ITEMS_SHOWN vs CO_ITEMS_ALL. Only documents with OPEN_AMT >= Rs 10,000 that rank in the company's top 1,500 or their own doctype's top 400 are delivered — 2,168 of 23,240 (oil), 2,188 of 10,105 (mart), 1,096 of 2,212 (bev). Any KPI computed by summing the delivered rows is a SHOWN-SET figure and must be labelled as one. This is exactly the v1 bug the notes record: the doctype bar chart summed shown rows under an uncapped headline, drawing Rs 2,516 Cr of bars beneath a Rs 2,582 Cr number.

CO_OPEN_ALL IS NOT MONEY OWED, AND IS THE MOST DANGEROUS NUMBER ON THE BOARD. Oil shows Rs 2,586.70 Cr of open documents against Rs 12.89 Cr of actual ledger balance across the same parties — a 200x gap. Two causes, both measured: 76.6% is migration openings dated 2024-09-30, and the rest is DocStatus='O' being unreliable at JIVO because bills are settled by manual journal entry or unmatched on-account payments (C-0019). The receivable and payable figures come from customer-ageing / vendor-ageing, which anchor on OCRD.Balance. Every panel that shows CO_OPEN_ALL must carry that sentence.

DOCTYPE AND SIDE ARE DIFFERENT AXES. DOCTYPE names the SAP table; SIDE names the party's ledger side, derived from the payment's own DocType. Filtering by DOCTYPE='AR_RCT' when you meant 'customer receipts' pulls in ORCT rows with DocType='S' — cash received back FROM A VENDOR — worth Rs 2.25 Cr across 146 oil documents. Mirror image: 26 oil OVPM rows (Rs 25.86 L) are refunds paid TO A CUSTOMER and are SIDE='AR'. This was defect D1; after the fix SIDE agrees with OCRD.CardType on 100% of rows, so any disagreement is now a hard defect signal.

DAYS_OVERDUE AND AGE_DAYS DISAGREE BY YEARS ON MIGRATED ROWS, and both are correct. Oil's worst row is dated 2024-09-30 (691 days old) with a true original due date of 2020-02-19 (2,376 days overdue). ITEM_REAL_EST MUST BE SUMMED SIGNED OR NOT AT ALL. It is OPEN_AMT × CARD_REAL_PCT/100, and CARD_REAL_PCT is a ratio of NETS applied to GROSS amounts. A card whose large debits and credits offset gets 100% and every one of its rows is estimated at its full face value: Mart's VENDA000001 sums to Rs 347.86 Cr of 'really open' against a card balance of −Rs 20.93 Cr. Gross-summing it across Mart's shown rows yields Rs 505.88 Cr against a CO_OCRD_NET of −Rs 9.39 Cr, which is nonsense. 233 of 421 oil cards, 17 of 50 mart, 43 of 306 bev overstate this way. Recommendation: do NOT publish a company-level 'really open' KPI from this column; expose it per row and per card only.

OPEN_AMT_FC IS NOT RUPEES AND ITS COLUMN IS NOT ADDABLE. One such row was found; no systematic sweep was run.

SAP writes account-level system reconciliations that stamp the reconciliation's whole total onto each participant line, so 87 oil / 14 mart / 1 bev documents legitimately carry more reconciliation than value. It is a DIAGNOSTIC, never a settlement figure, and it is never used to compute OPEN_AMT. sql.text:
CASE
           WHEN IFNULL(g."GroupName",'') LIKE '%BRANCH%' THEN 'BRANCH'
           WHEN UPPER(c."CardName") LIKE 'JIVO%'
             OR UPPER(c."CardName") LIKE '%A U O JWPL%'
             OR UPPER(c."CardName") LIKE '%AKAL ROZGAR%'
             OR UPPER(c."CardName") LIKE '%AKAL INFO%'
             OR IFNULL(g."GroupName",'') IN ('PARENT COMPANY',
                                             'COMPANY UNIT CUSTOMER',
                                             'COMPANY UNIT VENDOR')
             THEN 'INTERCO'
           WHEN IFNULL(g."GroupName",'') LIKE '%STAFF%' THEN 'STAFF'
           ELSE 'TRADE'
         END                                 AS ACCT_KIND

terms.label: BRANCH — JIVO's own state GST registrations
terms.note: OCRG.GroupName LIKE '%BRANCH%'

terms.label: INTERCO — the other JIVO entities and Akal
terms.note: UPPER(CardName) LIKE 'JIVO%' OR AKAL ROZGAR/INFO OR group PARENT COMPANY / COMPANY UNIT CUSTOMER / COMPANY UNIT VENDOR. The NAME test does work the group test cannot — C-0020.

caveats.right: At JIVO a document stays DocStatus='O' long after the money moved, because settlements are posted as manual journal entries (JDT1.TransType=30) and as on-account ORCT/OVPM receipts and payments that are never internally reconciled to the document. OCRD.Balance is the only ground truth for what a party owes or is owed. Measured live 2026-08-21, open documents vs OCRD balances: Oil A/R 180.69 vs 109.51 Cr and A/P 309.20 vs 102.63 Cr; Mart A/R 128.12 vs 23.35 Cr and A/P 219.60 vs 29.22 Cr; Bev A/R 6.34 vs 4.83 Cr and A/P 3.56 vs 2.24 Cr. Overstatement 1.3x to 7.5x, worst on Mart payables. Correct method: take the party balance as the real exposure, derive unapplied credit as sum(open docs) - balance, consume it oldest-due-first, then bucket the remainder.
caveats.rule: SAP DocStatus='O' is unreliable at JIVO: documents settled by manual JE or unapplied on-account payment stay open. Age from OCRD.Balance, not open documents - naive ageing overstates 1.3-7.5x.
caveats.title: DocStatus='O' is unreliable — age from OCRD.Balance, not open documents
caveats.wrong: Built an ageing by summing open documents (OINV/OPCH DocStatus='O', DocTotal-PaidToDate) and bucketing on DocDueDate, treating 'open' as 'unpaid'.

caveats.right: The business-partner sub-ledger is JDT1 (JOIN OCRD ON CardCode = ShortName). A document-based extract silently omits every journal entry posted against a party, plus pre-cutover postings, cancelled documents with their reversals, and payments booked under the other side's DocType. Re-verified live 2026-08-22 in JIVO_OIL_HANADB since the migration: A/R invoice 30,956 / A/P invoice 16,330 / incoming payment 13,021 / outgoing payment 10,640 / JOURNAL ENTRY 7,478 (Rs 3,043.6 cr) / A/R credit note 6,431 / A/P credit note 1,587 / manual reconciliation 48. On CUSTA000578 RELIANCE RETAIL the document-based ledger showed 324 of the 620 postings SAP holds. It still footed to the correct closing balance only because the builder plugged the difference into a fabricated opening-balance row - so the omission was invisible from the total. Treat any figure that ties only because of a plug as unverified.
caveats.rule: Build a party ledger from JDT1 (OCRD.CardCode = JDT1.ShortName), never from document extracts - they miss every journal entry (7,478 in Oil, Rs 3,043 cr), cancellations and pre-cutover postings.
caveats.title: A party ledger comes from JDT1, not from document extracts
caveats.wrong: Built the vendor/customer Ledger from the ageing extract (Invoices + CreditNotes + Payments) and treated it as a statement of account.

ZERO HERE IS A VERIFIED TRUE ZERO, not a missed go-live date — render it as ₹0 with that sentence, never as empty().

oi-migrated-open.label: Still open from the go-live opening balances
section_traps: CO_*, DT_* and CARD_* are BROADCAST AGGREGATES repeated on every row they describe. Summing CO_OPEN_ALL down the oil slice gives Rs 5,60,806 Cr instead of Rs 2,586.70 Cr — a 2,168x overstatement. Read CO_* off summary[0], DT_* off the first row of each DOCTYPE, CARD_* off the first row of each CARD_CODE. The only per-row money columns are DOC_TOTAL, APPLIED, OPEN_AMT, SIGNED_OPEN, OPEN_AMT_FC, ITEM_REAL_EST, OITR_RECON_AMT.

THE ROW SET IS CAPPED AND FLOORED, and nothing in the row data says so except CO_ITEMS_SHOWN vs CO_ITEMS_ALL. Only documents with OPEN_AMT >= Rs 10,000 that rank in the company's top 1,500 or their own doctype's top 400 are delivered — 2,168 of 23,240 (oil), 2,188 of 10,105 (mart), 1,096 of 2,212 (bev). Any KPI computed by summing the delivered rows is a SHOWN-SET figure and must be labelled as one. This is exactly the v1 bug the notes record: the doctype bar chart summed shown rows under an uncapped headline, drawing Rs 2,516 Cr of bars beneath a Rs 2,582 Cr number.

CO_OPEN_ALL IS NOT MONEY OWED, AND IS THE MOST DANGEROUS NUMBER ON THE BOARD. Oil shows Rs 2,586.70 Cr of open documents against Rs 12.89 Cr of actual ledger balance across the same parties — a 200x gap. Two causes, both measured: 76.6% is migration openings dated 2024-09-30, and the rest is DocStatus='O' being unreliable at JIVO because bills are settled by manual journal entry or unmatched on-account payments (C-0019). The receivable and payable figures come from customer-ageing / vendor-ageing, which anchor on OCRD.Balance. Every panel that shows CO_OPEN_ALL must carry that sentence.

DOCTYPE AND SIDE ARE DIFFERENT AXES. DOCTYPE names the SAP table; SIDE names the party's ledger side, derived from the payment's own DocType. Filtering by DOCTYPE='AR_RCT' when you meant 'customer receipts' pulls in ORCT rows with DocType='S' — cash received back FROM A VENDOR — worth Rs 2.25 Cr across 146 oil documents. Mirror image: 26 oil OVPM rows (Rs 25.86 L) are refunds paid TO A CUSTOMER and are SIDE='AR'. This was defect D1; after the fix SIDE agrees with OCRD.CardType on 100% of rows, so any disagreement is now a hard defect signal.

DAYS_OVERDUE AND AGE_DAYS DISAGREE BY YEARS ON MIGRATED ROWS, and both are correct. Oil's worst row is dated 2024-09-30 (691 days old) with a true original due date of 2020-02-19 (2,376 days overdue). AGE_BUCKET is cut on DAYS_OVERDUE, so 87.9% of Oil's shown value lands in 365+ largely because of pre-go-live due dates. Never write 'this document is N days old' from DAYS_OVERDUE, and never write 'N days overdue' from AGE_DAYS. On payments (AR_RCT/AP_PMT) DUE_DATE is the payment's own and means nothing as a deadline — AGE_DAYS is the honest field there.

ITEM_REAL_EST MUST BE SUMMED SIGNED OR NOT AT ALL. It is OPEN_AMT × CARD_REAL_PCT/100, and CARD_REAL_PCT is a ratio of NETS applied to GROSS amounts. A card whose large debits and credits offset gets 100% and every one of its rows is estimated at its full face value: Mart's VENDA000001 sums to Rs 347.86 Cr of 'really open' against a card balance of −Rs 20.93 Cr. Gross-summing it across Mart's shown rows yields Rs 505.88 Cr against a CO_OCRD_NET of −Rs 9.39 Cr, which is nonsense. 233 of 421 oil cards, 17 of 50 mart, 43 of 306 bev overstate this way. SUM(SGN × ITEM_REAL_EST) per card = sign(net) × min(|net|,|balance|) — verified on all 265 fully-contained cards — and that is the only defensible total. Recommendation: do NOT publish a company-level 'really open' KPI from this column; expose it per row and per card only.

OPEN_AMT_FC IS NOT RUPEES AND ITS COLUMN IS NOT ADDABLE. OPEN_AMT is always local INR; OPEN_AMT_FC is the same item in its own currency, so totalling the column adds USD to EUR to zero. 107 oil rows are non-INR and they are Rs 2,103.78 Cr of the Rs 2,519.74 Cr shown — 83% of the book is exchange-rate exposed. Worse, rows with a rotten DocRate are INVISIBLE: Oil OVPM 26317 books USD 44.34 L as Rs 443.40 (~87,000x too small) and sinks below the Rs 10,000 floor entirely. One such row was found; no systematic sweep was run.

OITR_RECON_AMT CAN EXCEED THE DOCUMENT'S OWN TOTAL AND THAT IS NOT A BUG. SAP writes account-level system reconciliations that stamp the reconciliation's whole total onto each participant line, so 87 oil / 14 mart / 1 bev documents legitimately carry more reconciliation than value. It is a DIAGNOSTIC, never a settlement figure, and it is never used to compute OPEN_AMT. It is also easy to break: the naive SUM over ITR1's signed lines double-counted settlements written on both IsCredit sides and fired FULL_PER_OITR on documents SAP had not reconciled (128 impossible rows and Rs 18.24 Cr of phantom excess in Oil before defect D2 was fixed). If the impossible-row count jumps back toward 128, the GREATEST(D,C) guard has been removed.

MART'S SHOWN LIST IS 67.2% INTERCOMPANY BY VALUE (Rs 356.62 Cr of Rs 530.98 Cr), 68.2% once its BRANCH cards are added (Rs 362.29 Cr = the IS_GROUP=1 figure) — and VENDA000001 'JIVO WELLNESS PVT LTD' alone is Rs 347.86 Cr across 1,070 documents. Any Mart headline read without ACCT_KIND in front of it is mostly JIVO trading with itself (C-0005). Oil is 6.8% group (BRANCH 5.1% + INTERCO 1.7%), Bev 11.6% (BRANCH 11.1% + INTERCO 0.5%). Group parties are flagged and kept here, never dropped — the board must let the reader subtract them consciously.

BPL_NAME IS INCONSISTENTLY CASED IN SAP. Oil carries both 'FACTORY' and 'Factory' and both 'DELHI' and 'Delhi'; Bev carries 'FACTORY'/'Factory', 'DELHI'/'Delhi' and 'Punjab'. Grouping without UPPER() splits one branch into two bars and understates the larger one.

EXT_REF IS NULL ON EVERY PAYMENT ROW and on many invoices — 1,344 of 2,168 oil rows, 909 of 2,188 mart, 883 of 1,096 bev. It is the ONLY nullable column in the 51. A naive String(v) prints the literal 'None'.

OBJ_TYPE AND DOC_ENTRY ARRIVE WITH MIXED JSON TYPES. The SQL declares OBJ_TYPE as a string but data.json holds it as an INTEGER (13, 14, 18, 19, 24, 46), while DOC_ENTRY — a numeric key in SAP — arrives as a STRING. Cast both before building a document URL or the link silently 404s.

AS_OF FILTERS DocDate ONLY. PaidToDate, OpenBal and OCRD.Balance are live values with no history in these tables, so a back-dated run gives 'documents that existed on that date, with today's settlement state' — not the open position as it stood. Measured on Oil: --as-of 2026-03-31 reports Rs 80.34 Cr adjusted receivable against Rs 108.86 Cr today. Never label a back-dated run as a closing position.

STAFF IS A GROUP-NAME TEST ONLY, so employee imprest cards filed under a geography group (ORGC000031 'ARVINDER SINGH IMPREST JWPL0115', group DELHI) come out as TRADE. Measured cost: 11 items / Rs 1.27 L (oil), 2 / Rs 1,957 (mart), 6 / Rs 11,562 (bev). Immaterial, deliberately left — but do not present the TRADE figure as 'purely external' without this footnote.

NEGATIVE OpenBal ROWS ARE SILENTLY DROPPED by the > 0 filter: 2 oil rows (−Rs 0.91), 2 mart (−Rs 1,025), 0 bev. Total Rs 1,025.91 across all three books. Immaterial, but it is why the ORCT/OVPM totals here differ by exactly that amount from a raw table scan.

data.json MOVES UNDER YOU. The VPS rebuilds it every 2 minutes. Between 18:58:48 and 19:05:02 on 2026-08-22 Oil's CO_OPEN_ALL moved +Rs 40.32 L on a single new A/R invoice — and CO_OCRD_NET moved by the identical amount, leaving CO_STALE_GAP unchanged, which is exactly the behaviour a correct pipeline should show. Any regression test must compare shape and identities, not frozen paise.

sql.text:
CASE WHEN r.DOC_DATE = DATE'2024-09-30' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS IS_MIGRATED
  FROM raw r
),
-- card-level reality check, computed on the UNCAPPED set
card AS (
  SELECT CARD_CODE,
         SUM(SIGNED_OPEN) AS CARD_OPEN_NET,
         SUM(OPEN_AMT)    AS CARD_OPEN_GROSS
  FROM item GROUP BY CARD_CODE
),
-- uncapped per-DOCTYPE totals
dt AS (
  SELECT DOCTYPE, COUNT(*) AS DT_ITEMS_ALL, SUM(OPEN_AMT) AS DT_OPEN_ALL
  FROM item GROUP BY DOCTYPE
),
-- uncapped company totals ("of M" for the dashboard)
co AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*)          AS CO_ITEMS_ALL,
         SUM(i.OPEN_AMT)   AS CO_OPEN_ALL,
         SUM(i.SIGNED_OPEN) AS CO_OPEN_NET,
         SUM(CASE WHEN i.IS_MIGRATED = 1 THEN i.OPEN_AMT ELSE 0 END) AS CO_MIGRATED_OPEN

sql.text:
oitr AS (
  SELECT i."SrcObjTyp"                        AS OBJ_TYPE,
         i."SrcObjAbs"                        AS DOC_ENTRY,
         GREATEST(
           SUM(CASE WHEN i."IsCredit" = 'D' THEN CAST(i."ReconSum" AS DOUBLE) ELSE 0 END),
           SUM(CASE WHEN i."IsCredit" = 'C' THEN CAST(i."ReconSum" AS DOUBLE) ELSE 0 END)
         )                                    AS RECON_AMT,
         COUNT(*)                             AS RECON_LINES
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.ITR1 i
  JOIN {{SCHEMA}}.OITR o ON o."ReconNum" = i."ReconNum"
  WHERE o."Canceled" = 'N'
    AND i."SrcObjTyp" IN ('13','14','24','18','19','46')
    AND CAST(o."ReconDate" AS DATE) <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'
  GROUP BY i."SrcObjTyp", i."SrcObjAbs"
),

terms.note: RECON_AMT = GREATEST(SUM(D-side), SUM(C-side)) — never the sum of both; one settlement is written twice on opposite IsCredit sides

caveats.wrong: Built an ageing by summing open documents (OINV/OPCH DocStatus='O', DocTotal-PaidToDate) and bucketing on DocDueDate, treating 'open' as 'unpaid'.

caveats.right: In the HANA tables the flag has THREE values: 'N' = live, 'Y' = the cancelled original, and 'C' = the system-generated cancellation mirror SAP posts to reverse it. Y and C always appear as exact matching pairs carrying the same value, so a <>'Y' test keeps every mirror and double-counts. Measured live on Oil 2026-08-21: OINV 30,387 'N' (1045.62 Cr) plus 320 'Y' and 320 'C' at 37.27 Cr each; OPCH 16,101 'N' plus 113+113 at 15.96 Cr each; OPDN 10,640 'N' plus 473+473 at 94.63 Cr each; ORDN 1,817 'N' plus 107+107 at 0.49 Cr each. Same pattern in Mart and Beverages. Always test CANCELED='N' positively. Note the Service Layer differs: it exposes only Cancelled 'tYES'/'tNO', so the documented OData filter Cancelled eq 'tNO' is already correct and is not affected.
caveats.rule: HANA "CANCELED" is three-valued: 'N' live, 'Y' cancelled original, 'C' its system mirror. Always filter CANCELED='N' - a <>'Y' test keeps the mirrors and double-counts (Oil OPDN +94.63 Cr).
caveats.title: HANA CANCELED is three-valued — filter ='N', never <>'Y'
caveats.wrong: Excluded cancelled documents in HANA SQL by writing "CANCELED" <> 'Y' (or omitting the filter), assuming the flag is a two-valued Y/N.

Note the Service Layer differs: it exposes only Cancelled 'tYES'/'tNO', so the documented OData filter Cancelled eq 'tNO' is already correct and is not affected.

-- SIDE comes from the PAYMENT'S OWN "DocType", not from the table it sits in.
  -- ORCT is "money in", which is USUALLY a customer receipt - but 146 open Oil

  -- FROM A VENDOR.  Calling those AR put a vendor refund in the customer bucket.
  SELECT 'AR_RCT',
         CAST(CASE WHEN "DocType" = 'C' THEN 'AR' WHEN "DocType" = 'S' THEN 'AP'
                   ELSE 'AR' END AS NVARCHAR(2)), -1, '24',
         "DocEntry", "DocNum", CAST('' AS NVARCHAR(100)),
         "CardCode", "BPLId", CAST(IFNULL("BPLName",'') AS NVARCHAR(200)),
         CAST("DocDate" AS DATE), CAST("DocDueDate" AS DATE),
         CAST("DocTotal" AS DOUBLE),
         CAST("DocTotal" - "OpenBal" AS DOUBLE),
         CAST("OpenBal" AS DOUBLE),
         CAST("DocCurr" AS NVARCHAR(3)),
         CAST(IFNULL("OpenBalFc",0) AS DOUBLE)

caveats.right: At JIVO a document stays DocStatus='O' long after the money moved, because settlements are posted as manual journal entries (JDT1.TransType=30) and as on-account ORCT/OVPM receipts and payments that are never internally reconciled to the document. OCRD.Balance is the only ground truth for what a party owes or is owed. Measured live 2026-08-21, open documents vs OCRD balances: Oil A/R 180.69 vs 109.51 Cr and A/P 309.20 vs 102.63 Cr; Mart A/R 128.12 vs 23.35 Cr and A/P 219.60 vs 29.22 Cr; Bev A/R 6.34 vs 4.83 Cr and A/P 3.56 vs 2.24 Cr. Overstatement 1.3x to 7.5x, worst on Mart payables. Correct method: take the party balance as the real exposure, derive unapplied credit as sum(open docs) - balance, consume it oldest-due-first, then bucket the remainder.
caveats.rule: SAP DocStatus='O' is unreliable at JIVO: documents settled by manual JE or unapplied on-account payment stay open. Age from OCRD.Balance, not open documents - naive ageing overstates 1.3-7.5x.
caveats.title: DocStatus='O' is unreliable — age from OCRD.Balance, not open documents
caveats.wrong: Built an ageing by summing open documents (OINV/OPCH DocStatus='O', DocTotal-PaidToDate) and bucketing on DocDueDate, treating 'open' as 'unpaid'.

caveats.right: In the HANA tables the flag has THREE values: 'N' = live, 'Y' = the cancelled original, and 'C' = the system-generated cancellation mirror SAP posts to reverse it. Y and C always appear as exact matching pairs carrying the same value, so a <>'Y' test keeps every mirror and double-counts. Measured live on Oil 2026-08-21: OINV 30,387 'N' (1045.62 Cr) plus 320 'Y' and 320 'C' at 37.27 Cr each; OPCH 16,101 'N' plus 113+113 at 15.96 Cr each; OPDN 10,640 'N' plus 473+473 at 94.63 Cr each; ORDN 1,817 'N' plus 107+107 at 0.49 Cr each. Same pattern in Mart and Beverages. Always test CANCELED='N' positively. Note the Service Layer differs: it exposes only Cancelled 'tYES'/'tNO', so the documented OData filter Cancelled eq 'tNO' is already correct and is not affected.
caveats.rule: HANA "CANCELED" is three-valued: 'N' live, 'Y' cancelled original, 'C' its system mirror. Always filter CANCELED='N' - a <>'Y' test keeps the mirrors and double-counts (Oil OPDN +94.63 Cr).
caveats.title: HANA CANCELED is three-valued — filter ='N', never <>'Y'
caveats.wrong: Excluded cancelled documents in HANA SQL by writing "CANCELED" <> 'Y' (or omitting the filter), assuming the flag is a two-valued Y/N.

section_traps: CO_*, DT_* and CARD_* are BROADCAST AGGREGATES repeated on every row they describe. Summing CO_OPEN_ALL down the oil slice gives Rs 5,60,806 Cr instead of Rs 2,586.70 Cr — a 2,168x overstatement. Read CO_* off summary[0], DT_* off the first row of each DOCTYPE, CARD_* off the first row of each CARD_CODE. The only per-row money columns are DOC_TOTAL, APPLIED, OPEN_AMT, SIGNED_OPEN, OPEN_AMT_FC, ITEM_REAL_EST, OITR_RECON_AMT.

THE ROW SET IS CAPPED AND FLOORED, and nothing in the row data says so except CO_ITEMS_SHOWN vs CO_ITEMS_ALL. Only documents with OPEN_AMT >= Rs 10,000 that rank in the company's top 1,500 or their own doctype's top 400 are delivered — 2,168 of 23,240 (oil), 2,188 of 10,105 (mart), 1,096 of 2,212 (bev). Any KPI computed by summing the delivered rows is a SHOWN-SET figure and must be labelled as one. This is exactly the v1 bug the notes record: the doctype bar chart summed shown rows under an uncapped headline, drawing Rs 2,516 Cr of bars beneath a Rs 2,582 Cr number.

CO_OPEN_ALL IS NOT MONEY OWED, AND IS THE MOST DANGEROUS NUMBER ON THE BOARD. Oil shows Rs 2,586.70 Cr of open documents against Rs 12.89 Cr of actual ledger balance across the same parties — a 200x gap. Two causes, both measured: 76.6% is migration openings dated 2024-09-30, and the rest is DocStatus='O' being unreliable at JIVO because bills are settled by manual journal entry or unmatched on-account payments (C-0019). The receivable and payable figures come from customer-ageing / vendor-ageing, which anchor on OCRD.Balance. Every panel that shows CO_OPEN_ALL must carry that sentence.

DOCTYPE AND SIDE ARE DIFFERENT AXES. DOCTYPE names the SAP table; SIDE names the party's ledger side, derived from the payment's own DocType. Filtering by DOCTYPE='AR_RCT' when you meant 'customer receipts' pulls in ORCT rows with DocType='S' — cash received back FROM A VENDOR — worth Rs 2.25 Cr across 146 oil documents. Mirror image: 26 oil OVPM rows (Rs 25.86 L) are refunds paid TO A CUSTOMER and are SIDE='AR'. This was defect D1; after the fix SIDE agrees with OCRD.CardType on 100% of rows, so any disagreement is now a hard defect signal.

DAYS_OVERDUE AND AGE_DAYS DISAGREE BY YEARS ON MIGRATED ROWS, and both are correct. Oil's worst row is dated 2024-09-30 (691 days old) with a true original due date of 2020-02-19 (2,376 days overdue). AGE_BUCKET is cut on DAYS_OVERDUE, so 87.9% of Oil's shown value lands in 365+ largely because of pre-go-live due dates. Never write 'this document is N days old' from DAYS_OVERDUE, and never write 'N days overdue' from AGE_DAYS. On payments (AR_RCT/AP_PMT) DUE_DATE is the payment's own and means nothing as a deadline — AGE_DAYS is the honest field there.

ITEM_REAL_EST MUST BE SUMMED SIGNED OR NOT AT ALL. It is OPEN_AMT × CARD_REAL_PCT/100, and CARD_REAL_PCT is a ratio of NETS applied to GROSS amounts. A card whose large debits and credits offset gets 100% and every one of its rows is estimated at its full face value: Mart's VENDA000001 sums to Rs 347.86 Cr of 'really open' against a card balance of −Rs 20.93 Cr. Gross-summing it across Mart's shown rows yields Rs 505.88 Cr against a CO_OCRD_NET of −Rs 9.39 Cr, which is nonsense. 233 of 421 oil cards, 17 of 50 mart, 43 of 306 bev overstate this way. SUM(SGN × ITEM_REAL_EST) per card = sign(net) × min(|net|,|balance|) — verified on all 265 fully-contained cards — and that is the only defensible total. Recommendation: do NOT publish a company-level 'really open' KPI from this column; expose it per row and per card only.

OPEN_AMT_FC IS NOT RUPEES AND ITS COLUMN IS NOT ADDABLE. OPEN_AMT is always local INR; OPEN_AMT_FC is the same item in its own currency, so totalling the column adds USD to EUR to zero. 107 oil rows are non-INR and they are Rs 2,103.78 Cr of the Rs 2,519.74 Cr shown — 83% of the book is exchange-rate exposed. Worse, rows with a rotten DocRate are INVISIBLE: Oil OVPM 26317 books USD 44.34 L as Rs 443.40 (~87,000x too small) and sinks below the Rs 10,000 floor entirely. One such row was found; no systematic sweep was run.

OITR_RECON_AMT CAN EXCEED THE DOCUMENT'S OWN TOTAL AND THAT IS NOT A BUG. SAP writes account-level system reconciliations that stamp the reconciliation's whole total onto each participant line, so 87 oil / 14 mart / 1 bev documents legitimately carry more reconciliation than value. It is a DIAGNOSTIC, never a settlement figure, and it is never used to compute OPEN_AMT. It is also easy to break: the naive SUM over ITR1's signed lines double-counted settlements written on both IsCredit sides and fired FULL_PER_OITR on documents SAP had not reconciled (128 impossible rows and Rs 18.24 Cr of phantom excess in Oil before defect D2 was fixed). If the impossible-row count jumps back toward 128, the GREATEST(D,C) guard has been removed.

MART'S SHOWN LIST IS 67.2% INTERCOMPANY BY VALUE (Rs 356.62 Cr of Rs 530.98 Cr), 68.2% once its BRANCH cards are added (Rs 362.29 Cr = the IS_GROUP=1 figure) — and VENDA000001 'JIVO WELLNESS PVT LTD' alone is Rs 347.86 Cr across 1,070 documents. Any Mart headline read without ACCT_KIND in front of it is mostly JIVO trading with itself (C-0005). Oil is 6.8% group (BRANCH 5.1% + INTERCO 1.7%), Bev 11.6% (BRANCH 11.1% + INTERCO 0.5%). Group parties are flagged and kept here, never dropped — the board must let the reader subtract them consciously.

BPL_NAME IS INCONSISTENTLY CASED IN SAP. Oil carries both 'FACTORY' and 'Factory' and both 'DELHI' and 'Delhi'; Bev carries 'FACTORY'/'Factory', 'DELHI'/'Delhi' and 'Punjab'. Grouping without UPPER() splits one branch into two bars and understates the larger one.

EXT_REF IS NULL ON EVERY PAYMENT ROW and on many invoices — 1,344 of 2,168 oil rows, 909 of 2,188 mart, 883 of 1,096 bev. It is the ONLY nullable column in the 51. A naive String(v) prints the literal 'None'.

OBJ_TYPE AND DOC_ENTRY ARRIVE WITH MIXED JSON TYPES. The SQL declares OBJ_TYPE as a string but data.json holds it as an INTEGER (13, 14, 18, 19, 24, 46), while DOC_ENTRY — a numeric key in SAP — arrives as a STRING. Cast both before building a document URL or the link silently 404s.

AS_OF FILTERS DocDate ONLY. PaidToDate, OpenBal and OCRD.Balance are live values with no history in these tables, so a back-dated run gives 'documents that existed on that date, with today's settlement state' — not the open position as it stood. Measured on Oil: --as-of 2026-03-31 reports Rs 80.34 Cr adjusted receivable against Rs 108.86 Cr today. Never label a back-dated run as a closing position.

STAFF IS A GROUP-NAME TEST ONLY, so employee imprest cards filed under a geography group (ORGC000031 'ARVINDER SINGH IMPREST JWPL0115', group DELHI) come out as TRADE. Measured cost: 11 items / Rs 1.27 L (oil), 2 / Rs 1,957 (mart), 6 / Rs 11,562 (bev). Immaterial, deliberately left — but do not present the TRADE figure as 'purely external' without this footnote.

NEGATIVE OpenBal ROWS ARE SILENTLY DROPPED by the > 0 filter: 2 oil rows (−Rs 0.91), 2 mart (−Rs 1,025), 0 bev. Total Rs 1,025.91 across all three books. Immaterial, but it is why the ORCT/OVPM totals here differ by exactly that amount from a raw table scan.

data.json MOVES UNDER YOU. The VPS rebuilds it every 2 minutes. Between 18:58:48 and 19:05:02 on 2026-08-22 Oil's CO_OPEN_ALL moved +Rs 40.32 L on a single new A/R invoice — and CO_OCRD_NET moved by the identical amount, leaving CO_STALE_GAP unchanged, which is exactly the behaviour a correct pipeline should show. Any regression test must compare shape and identities, not frozen paise.

sql.text:
-- Same mirror-image trap: OVPM is "money out", usually to a vendor, but 26
  -- open Oil rows (Rs 25.9 L) and 2 Bev are DocType='C' - a refund PAID TO A
  -- CUSTOMER.  The party is a customer, so the row belongs on the AR side.
  SELECT 'AP_PMT',
         CAST(CASE WHEN "DocType" = 'C' THEN 'AR' WHEN "DocType" = 'S' THEN 'AP'
                   ELSE 'AP' END AS NVARCHAR(2)), 1, '46',
         "DocEntry", "DocNum", CAST('' AS NVARCHAR(100)),
         "CardCode", "BPLId", CAST(IFNULL("BPLName",'') AS NVARCHAR(200)),
         CAST("DocDate" AS DATE), CAST("DocDueDate" AS DATE),
         CAST("DocTotal" AS DOUBLE),
         CAST("DocTotal" - "OpenBal" AS DOUBLE),
         CAST("OpenBal" AS DOUBLE),
         CAST("DocCurr" AS NVARCHAR(3)),
         CAST(IFNULL("OpenBalFc",0) AS DOUBLE)
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.OVPM
  WHERE "Canceled" = 'N'
    AND CAST(IFNULL("OpenBal",0) AS DOUBLE) > 0
    AND CAST("DocDate" AS DATE) <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'

excludes.why: dormant provision heads are published so an unused head is visibly unused (sql line 236) — counting rows overstates activity ~2.6x

prov-accounts-carrying.formula: COUNT(accounts where OUTSTANDING_CR_L > 0). Published rows are 53 / 40 / 39 — most of them are deliberately-listed dormant accounts, so row count is NOT this number.
prov-accounts-carrying.label: Accounts carrying a balance
prov-accounts-carrying.method: row count over the filter (unit is count)
section_traps: CROSSED_YEAREND_L and MIGRATED_OPENING_L are RE-CUTS of the same FIFO residual already inside AGE_0_30_L..AGE_365P_L. Adding them as extra buckets inflates Oil by Rs 3.23 Cr on a Rs 5.99 Cr base. Only the four AGE_* columns are additive, and they sum to OUTSTANDING_CR_L.

The headline is GROSS. OUTSTANDING_CR_L is floored at zero per account, so over-reversal is not netted: Oil's real net register position is Rs 4.62 Cr, not the Rs 5.99 Cr headline. Column: DEBIT_BAL_L (Rs 1.37 Cr Oil / Rs 16.63 L Mart / Rs 5.15 L Bev).

v1 renders the over-reversal KPI as String(dr.length) — a COUNT of 8 — so Rs 1.37 Cr never reaches the page. Column: DEBIT_BAL_L. The single biggest is Oil 2161007 SALARY PAYABLE JUL at a Rs 1.10 Cr DEBIT, which is itself worth an Accounts look.

'Older than a year' reads as neglect and mostly is not. AGE_365P_L on Oil is Rs 1.60 Cr of which Rs 1.52 Cr (95.3%) is the 2024-09-30 SAP go-live opening — balance-sheet carry-forward, not an unreviewed provision. Ex-migration it is Rs 7.49 L. Never render AGE_365P_L without MIGRATED_OPENING_L beside it.

Every money column is LAKHS. CREATED_CR_L, OUTSTANDING_CR_L, PROV_MEMO_CR_L and NET_DR_MINUS_CR_L contain '_CR' but do not END in it, so scale() must take the _L branch. Rename any of them to _CR and the page renders 100x too large.

Sign convention: NET_DR_MINUS_CR_L and OACT_CURRTOTAL_L are Debit-minus-Credit, so NEGATIVE means still provided for. Plotting either raw draws provisions as negative bars and over-reversal as positive.

The ageing is a MODELLING CHOICE, not something SAP says. JDT1.IntrnMatch = 0, ExtrMatch = 0 and Closed = 'N' on 100% of 15,630 register lines in all three books, so SAP cannot say which provision is still open. Debits consume the OLDEST credit first, which deliberately ages the residual as old as possible. Never caption a bucket chart 'per SAP'.

This is a G/L register, not a party or document register — no CardCode, no DocEntry, no DocStatus. C-0019 / C-0021 / C-0005 do not bite here. What does bite: 'total liabilities = payables + provisions' is not a supported sum. Oil 2110008 SUNDRY CREDITORS CLEARING (Rs 55.32 L) and Bev 2110008 (Rs 2.23 L) are fed through five internal clearing VENDOR cards that also appear in vendor-ageing. Measured on today's data the vendor-side ADJ_OPEN on those cards is Rs 29,897 (Oil, VENDA000987 INCENTIVE TA/DA/PAYABLE) and Rs 500 (Bev), so the arithmetic overlap is small — but it is not zero, and the two sections must never be added.

Rounding is coarse: every _L column is ROUND(x/100000, 2), i.e. Rs 1,000 granularity. Per-row the four AGE_* buckets can miss OUTSTANDING_CR_L by Rs 1,000 (live today: Oil 2163025 BLOWING CONVERSION PAYABLE, Mart 2180010 PROVISION FOR CLAIMS PAYABLE -RK). Book-level route deltas run to Rs 2,000. Every check must use a Rs 1,000 x rowcount tolerance; exact equality WILL false-alarm.

Dormant accounts are published on purpose (25 nil rows Oil, 24 Mart, 24 Bev out of 53/40/39). Counting rows as 'provision accounts' overstates activity about 2.6x. Count OUTSTANDING_CR_L > 0 — that is 20 / 9 / 10.
NEVER_REVERSED reads 'N' for an account that has never been posted at all (lifetime credit is 0). It is not a 'has been reversed' flag. Column: NEVER_REVERSED, cross-read with N_LINES.

The C_OTHER_BY_MEMO gate (>= Rs 5 L memo-tagged credit AND >= 25% of the account's total credit) is hard-coded and absolute, not scaled to book size. Mart yields no C_OTHER_BY_MEMO row at all — that is data, not a failure, and the family chart must not draw a zero slice or an error.

OACT_CURRTOTAL_L is a LIFETIME balance and is NOT filtered by as_of. It equals the as-of figure today only because there are zero future-dated JE lines on register accounts. Any historical as-of run will make the OACT cross-check legitimately disagree, and the check dot must report 'not applicable at this as-of', not red.

PROV_MEMO_CR_L is a weak label, not a classification. Its only real job is the C_OTHER_BY_MEMO gate. Book-wide it covers 22.7% of Oil's lifetime credits, 59.5% of Mart's, 30.9% of Bev's — do not present it as 'how much of this is really a provision'.

There is no detail slice. provisions has summary rows only (data.json detail: {}), so no page may offer a drill to individual JDT1 journal lines, a JE memo list, or a posting timeline. gl-account.html for a provision account can show only the 30 summary columns for that one account plus its history.jsonl trend.
N_LINES counts BOTH legs of storno reversals (160 of them touch Oil's register accounts), so it measures posting volume, not the number of provisions raised.

sql.text:
WHERE (
        -- every dedicated PROVISION account is listed, even if never used
        reg.FAMILY = 'A_PROVISIONS'
        -- accrual accounts: only if they actually moved or hold a balance
     OR (reg.FAMILY = 'B_EXPENSES_PAYABLE'
         AND (IFNULL(g.N_LINES,0) > 0 OR ABS(CAST(a."CurrTotal" AS DOUBLE)) > 1))
        -- off-piste accounts: only if provisioning is a MATERIAL part of what
        -- the account does. Without this gate the memo rule drags in the bank
        -- CC account, the vendor control account and every TDS-withholding
        -- account, because a provision JE happened to touch them once.
     OR (reg.FAMILY = 'C_OTHER_BY_MEMO'
         AND IFNULL(g.CR_PMEMO,0) >= 500000
         AND IFNULL(g.CR_PMEMO,0) >= 0.25 * IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0))
      )

prov-aged-365p.label: Standing more than a year
section_traps: CROSSED_YEAREND_L and MIGRATED_OPENING_L are RE-CUTS of the same FIFO residual already inside AGE_0_30_L..AGE_365P_L. Adding them as extra buckets inflates Oil by Rs 3.23 Cr on a Rs 5.99 Cr base. Only the four AGE_* columns are additive, and they sum to OUTSTANDING_CR_L.

The headline is GROSS. OUTSTANDING_CR_L is floored at zero per account, so over-reversal is not netted: Oil's real net register position is Rs 4.62 Cr, not the Rs 5.99 Cr headline. Column: DEBIT_BAL_L (Rs 1.37 Cr Oil / Rs 16.63 L Mart / Rs 5.15 L Bev).

v1 renders the over-reversal KPI as String(dr.length) — a COUNT of 8 — so Rs 1.37 Cr never reaches the page. Column: DEBIT_BAL_L. The single biggest is Oil 2161007 SALARY PAYABLE JUL at a Rs 1.10 Cr DEBIT, which is itself worth an Accounts look.

'Older than a year' reads as neglect and mostly is not. AGE_365P_L on Oil is Rs 1.60 Cr of which Rs 1.52 Cr (95.3%) is the 2024-09-30 SAP go-live opening — balance-sheet carry-forward, not an unreviewed provision. Ex-migration it is Rs 7.49 L. Never render AGE_365P_L without MIGRATED_OPENING_L beside it.

Every money column is LAKHS. CREATED_CR_L, OUTSTANDING_CR_L, PROV_MEMO_CR_L and NET_DR_MINUS_CR_L contain '_CR' but do not END in it, so scale() must take the _L branch. Rename any of them to _CR and the page renders 100x too large.

The ageing is a MODELLING CHOICE, not something SAP says. JDT1.IntrnMatch = 0, ExtrMatch = 0 and Closed = 'N' on 100% of 15,630 register lines in all three books, so SAP cannot say which provision is still open. Debits consume the OLDEST credit first, which deliberately ages the residual as old as possible. Never caption a bucket chart 'per SAP'.

What does bite: 'total liabilities = payables + provisions' is not a supported sum. Oil 2110008 SUNDRY CREDITORS CLEARING (Rs 55.32 L) and Bev 2110008 (Rs 2.23 L) are fed through five internal clearing VENDOR cards that also appear in vendor-ageing. Measured on today's data the vendor-side ADJ_OPEN on those cards is Rs 29,897 (Oil, VENDA000987 INCENTIVE TA/DA/PAYABLE) and Rs 500 (Bev), so the arithmetic overlap is small — but it is not zero, and the two sections must never be added.

Rounding is coarse: every _L column is ROUND(x/100000, 2), i.e. Rs 1,000 granularity. Per-row the four AGE_* buckets can miss OUTSTANDING_CR_L by Rs 1,000 (live today: Oil 2163025 BLOWING CONVERSION PAYABLE, Mart 2180010 PROVISION FOR CLAIMS PAYABLE -RK). sql.text:
credits AS (
  SELECT l.ACCT, l.RD, l.NET_CR AS CR,
         SUM(l.NET_CR) OVER (PARTITION BY l.ACCT
                         ORDER BY l.RD, l.TID, l.LID
                         ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS CUM_CR
  FROM lines l WHERE l.NET_CR > 0
),
resid AS (
  -- >= 0.01 tolerance: the running totals are DOUBLE (DECIMAL would overflow on
  -- the 5,800-line COGS PAYABLE account), and a credit line that FIFO consumes
  -- EXACTLY leaves a ~1e-7 float residue. Without the tolerance that residue is
  -- rounded away in the money columns but still counts as "open" for
  -- OLDEST_OPEN_DATE, which then reports a fully-reversed provision as 386 days
  -- old. Seen live on Mart 2180014 PROVISION FOR JULY.
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT c.ACCT, c.RD,
           GREATEST(0, LEAST(c.CR, c.CUM_CR - g.TOT_CONSUME)) AS RESID
    FROM credits c JOIN agg g ON g.ACCT = c.ACCT
  ) WHERE RESID >= 0.01
),
aged AS (
  SELECT r.ACCT,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) <= 30                       THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A0,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) BETWEEN  31 AND  90         THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A1,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) BETWEEN  91 AND 365         THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A2,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) > 365                       THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A3,
         SUM(CASE WHEN r.RD <  pr.FY_START                                     THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A_YE,
         SUM(CASE WHEN r.RD =  pr.GOLIVE                                       THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A_MIG,
         MIN(r.RD) AS OLDEST_OPEN
  FROM resid r CROSS JOIN params pr
  GROUP BY r.ACCT
)
SELECT
  '{{SCHEMA}}'                                             AS COMPANY_SCHEMA,
  pr.ASOF                                                  AS AS_OF,
  reg.FAMILY                                               AS FAMILY,
  reg.ACCT                                                 AS ACCT_CODE,
  a."AcctName"                                             AS ACCT_NAME,
  IFNULL(pa."AcctName",'')                                 AS PARENT_NAME,
  IFNULL(g.N_LINES,0)                                      AS N_LINES,
  g.FIRST_POST                                             AS FIRST_POST,
  g.LAST_POST                                              AS LAST_POST,
  DAYS_BETWEEN(g.LAST_POST, pr.ASOF)                       AS DAYS_SINCE_LAST_POST,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0)/100000, 2)                      AS CREATED_CR_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0)/100000, 2)                      AS REVERSED_DR_L,
  ROUND((IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0)-IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0))/100000, 2) AS NET_DR_MINUS_CR_L,
  ROUND(GREATEST(0, IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0)-IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0))/100000, 2) AS OUTSTANDING_CR_L,
  ROUND(GREATEST(0, IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0)-IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0))/100000, 2) AS DEBIT_BAL_L,
  ROUND(CAST(a."CurrTotal" AS DOUBLE)/100000, 2)           AS OACT_CURRTOTAL_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.CR_FYTD,0)/100000, 2)                     AS CREATED_FYTD_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.DR_FYTD,0)/100000, 2)                     AS REVERSED_FYTD_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A0,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_0_30_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A1,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_31_90_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A2,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_91_365_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A3,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_365P_L,

sql.text:
SUM(CASE WHEN RD >= (SELECT FY_START FROM params) THEN CR ELSE 0 END) AS CR_FYTD,
         SUM(CASE WHEN RD >= (SELECT FY_START FROM params) THEN DR ELSE 0 END) AS DR_FYTD,
         SUM(CASE WHEN PMEMO = 1 THEN CR ELSE 0 END) AS CR_PMEMO,
         SUM(CASE WHEN MANUAL_JE = 1 THEN DR + CR ELSE 0 END) AS MOVE_MANUAL,
         SUM(DR + CR) AS MOVE_ALL,
         -- everything that CONSUMES a provision: real debits plus any line
         -- booked as a negative credit. Guarantees SUM(RESID) == TOT_CR-TOT_DR.
         SUM(CASE WHEN NET_CR < 0 THEN -NET_CR ELSE 0 END) AS TOT_CONSUME
  FROM lines GROUP BY ACCT
),
-- FIFO: oldest credit first; total debits consume them in order
credits AS (
  SELECT l.ACCT, l.RD, l.NET_CR AS CR,
         SUM(l.NET_CR) OVER (PARTITION BY l.ACCT
                         ORDER BY l.RD, l.TID, l.LID
                         ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS CUM_CR
  FROM lines l WHERE l.NET_CR > 0
),
resid AS (
  -- >= 0.01 tolerance: the running totals are DOUBLE (DECIMAL would overflow on
  -- the 5,800-line COGS PAYABLE account), and a credit line that FIFO consumes
  -- EXACTLY leaves a ~1e-7 float residue. Without the tolerance that residue is
  -- rounded away in the money columns but still counts as "open" for
  -- OLDEST_OPEN_DATE, which then reports a fully-reversed provision as 386 days
  -- old. Seen live on Mart 2180014 PROVISION FOR JULY.
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT c.ACCT, c.RD,
           GREATEST(0, LEAST(c.CR, c.CUM_CR - g.TOT_CONSUME)) AS RESID
    FROM credits c JOIN agg g ON g.ACCT = c.ACCT
  ) WHERE RESID >= 0.01
),
aged AS (
  SELECT r.ACCT,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) <= 30                       THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A0,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) BETWEEN  31 AND  90         THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A1,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) BETWEEN  91 AND 365         THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A2,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) > 365                       THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A3,
         SUM(CASE WHEN r.RD <  pr.FY_START                                     THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A_YE,
         SUM(CASE WHEN r.RD =  pr.GOLIVE                                       THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A_MIG,
         MIN(r.RD) AS OLDEST_OPEN
  FROM resid r CROSS JOIN params pr
  GROUP BY r.ACCT
)

  '{{SCHEMA}}'                                             AS COMPANY_SCHEMA,
  pr.ASOF                                                  AS AS_OF,
  reg.FAMILY                                               AS FAMILY,
  reg.ACCT                                                 AS ACCT_CODE,
  a."AcctName"                                             AS ACCT_NAME,

  IFNULL(g.N_LINES,0)                                      AS N_LINES,
  g.FIRST_POST                                             AS FIRST_POST,

  DAYS_BETWEEN(g.LAST_POST, pr.ASOF)                       AS DAYS_SINCE_LAST_POST,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0)/100000, 2)                      AS CREATED_CR_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0)/100000, 2)                      AS REVERSED_DR_L,
  ROUND((IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0)-IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0))/100000, 2) AS NET_DR_MINUS_CR_L,

section_traps: CROSSED_YEAREND_L and MIGRATED_OPENING_L are RE-CUTS of the same FIFO residual already inside AGE_0_30_L..AGE_365P_L. Adding them as extra buckets inflates Oil by Rs 3.23 Cr on a Rs 5.99 Cr base. Only the four AGE_* columns are additive, and they sum to OUTSTANDING_CR_L.

The headline is GROSS. OUTSTANDING_CR_L is floored at zero per account, so over-reversal is not netted: Oil's real net register position is Rs 4.62 Cr, not the Rs 5.99 Cr headline. Column: DEBIT_BAL_L (Rs 1.37 Cr Oil / Rs 16.63 L Mart / Rs 5.15 L Bev).

v1 renders the over-reversal KPI as String(dr.length) — a COUNT of 8 — so Rs 1.37 Cr never reaches the page. Column: DEBIT_BAL_L. The single biggest is Oil 2161007 SALARY PAYABLE JUL at a Rs 1.10 Cr DEBIT, which is itself worth an Accounts look.

'Older than a year' reads as neglect and mostly is not. AGE_365P_L on Oil is Rs 1.60 Cr of which Rs 1.52 Cr (95.3%) is the 2024-09-30 SAP go-live opening — balance-sheet carry-forward, not an unreviewed provision. Ex-migration it is Rs 7.49 L. Never render AGE_365P_L without MIGRATED_OPENING_L beside it.

Every money column is LAKHS. CREATED_CR_L, OUTSTANDING_CR_L, PROV_MEMO_CR_L and NET_DR_MINUS_CR_L contain '_CR' but do not END in it, so scale() must take the _L branch. Rename any of them to _CR and the page renders 100x too large.

Sign convention: NET_DR_MINUS_CR_L and OACT_CURRTOTAL_L are Debit-minus-Credit, so NEGATIVE means still provided for. Plotting either raw draws provisions as negative bars and over-reversal as positive.

The ageing is a MODELLING CHOICE, not something SAP says. JDT1.IntrnMatch = 0, ExtrMatch = 0 and Closed = 'N' on 100% of 15,630 register lines in all three books, so SAP cannot say which provision is still open. Debits consume the OLDEST credit first, which deliberately ages the residual as old as possible. Never caption a bucket chart 'per SAP'.

This is a G/L register, not a party or document register — no CardCode, no DocEntry, no DocStatus. C-0019 / C-0021 / C-0005 do not bite here. What does bite: 'total liabilities = payables + provisions' is not a supported sum. Oil 2110008 SUNDRY CREDITORS CLEARING (Rs 55.32 L) and Bev 2110008 (Rs 2.23 L) are fed through five internal clearing VENDOR cards that also appear in vendor-ageing. Measured on today's data the vendor-side ADJ_OPEN on those cards is Rs 29,897 (Oil, VENDA000987 INCENTIVE TA/DA/PAYABLE) and Rs 500 (Bev), so the arithmetic overlap is small — but it is not zero, and the two sections must never be added.

Rounding is coarse: every _L column is ROUND(x/100000, 2), i.e. Rs 1,000 granularity. Per-row the four AGE_* buckets can miss OUTSTANDING_CR_L by Rs 1,000 (live today: Oil 2163025 BLOWING CONVERSION PAYABLE, Mart 2180010 PROVISION FOR CLAIMS PAYABLE -RK). Book-level route deltas run to Rs 2,000. Every check must use a Rs 1,000 x rowcount tolerance; exact equality WILL false-alarm.

Dormant accounts are published on purpose (25 nil rows Oil, 24 Mart, 24 Bev out of 53/40/39). Counting rows as 'provision accounts' overstates activity about 2.6x. Count OUTSTANDING_CR_L > 0 — that is 20 / 9 / 10.
NEVER_REVERSED reads 'N' for an account that has never been posted at all (lifetime credit is 0). It is not a 'has been reversed' flag. Column: NEVER_REVERSED, cross-read with N_LINES.

The C_OTHER_BY_MEMO gate (>= Rs 5 L memo-tagged credit AND >= 25% of the account's total credit) is hard-coded and absolute, not scaled to book size. Mart yields no C_OTHER_BY_MEMO row at all — that is data, not a failure, and the family chart must not draw a zero slice or an error.

OACT_CURRTOTAL_L is a LIFETIME balance and is NOT filtered by as_of. It equals the as-of figure today only because there are zero future-dated JE lines on register accounts. Any historical as-of run will make the OACT cross-check legitimately disagree, and the check dot must report 'not applicable at this as-of', not red.

PROV_MEMO_CR_L is a weak label, not a classification. Its only real job is the C_OTHER_BY_MEMO gate. Book-wide it covers 22.7% of Oil's lifetime credits, 59.5% of Mart's, 30.9% of Bev's — do not present it as 'how much of this is really a provision'.

There is no detail slice. provisions has summary rows only (data.json detail: {}), so no page may offer a drill to individual JDT1 journal lines, a JE memo list, or a posting timeline. gl-account.html for a provision account can show only the 30 summary columns for that one account plus its history.jsonl trend.
N_LINES counts BOTH legs of storno reversals (160 of them touch Oil's register accounts), so it measures posting volume, not the number of provisions raised.

CREATED_CR_L is literally SUM(Credit), so a line posted as a NEGATIVE credit reduces 'created' instead of appearing as a reversal. Created minus Reversed is therefore not exactly 'raised less released' in accounting terms — it is a net of the two columns as SAP stores them.
Month names in ACCT_NAME (FREIGHT PAYABLE JUN, SALARY PAYABLE JUL) are the month PROVIDED FOR, not the month posted, and the FIFO ages by RefDate. Do not read the account name as a date.

sql.text:
CASE WHEN j."TransType" = '30' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS MANUAL_JE,
         CASE WHEN UPPER(IFNULL(h."Memo",''))     LIKE '%PROVISION%'
                OR UPPER(IFNULL(j."LineMemo",'')) LIKE '%PROVISION%'
              THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS PMEMO
  FROM reg r
  JOIN {{SCHEMA}}.JDT1 j ON j."Account"  = r.ACCT
  JOIN {{SCHEMA}}.OJDT h ON h."TransId"  = j."TransId"
  CROSS JOIN params pr
  WHERE TO_DATE(j."RefDate") <= pr.ASOF
),
agg AS (
  SELECT ACCT,
         COUNT(*)      AS N_LINES,
         MIN(RD)       AS FIRST_POST,
         MAX(RD)       AS LAST_POST,
         SUM(DR)       AS TOT_DR,
         SUM(CR)       AS TOT_CR,
         SUM(CASE WHEN RD >= (SELECT FY_START FROM params) THEN CR ELSE 0 END) AS CR_FYTD,
         SUM(CASE WHEN RD >= (SELECT FY_START FROM params) THEN DR ELSE 0 END) AS DR_FYTD,
         SUM(CASE WHEN PMEMO = 1 THEN CR ELSE 0 END) AS CR_PMEMO,
         SUM(CASE WHEN MANUAL_JE = 1 THEN DR + CR ELSE 0 END) AS MOVE_MANUAL,
         SUM(DR + CR) AS MOVE_ALL,
         -- everything that CONSUMES a provision: real debits plus any line
         -- booked as a negative credit. Guarantees SUM(RESID) == TOT_CR-TOT_DR.
         SUM(CASE WHEN NET_CR < 0 THEN -NET_CR ELSE 0 END) AS TOT_CONSUME
  FROM lines GROUP BY ACCT
),
-- FIFO: oldest credit first; total debits consume them in order
credits AS (
  SELECT l.ACCT, l.RD, l.NET_CR AS CR,
         SUM(l.NET_CR) OVER (PARTITION BY l.ACCT
                         ORDER BY l.RD, l.TID, l.LID
                         ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS CUM_CR
  FROM lines l WHERE l.NET_CR > 0
),
resid AS (
  -- >= 0.01 tolerance: the running totals are DOUBLE (DECIMAL would overflow on
  -- the 5,800-line COGS PAYABLE account), and a credit line that FIFO consumes
  -- EXACTLY leaves a ~1e-7 float residue. Without the tolerance that residue is
  -- rounded away in the money columns but still counts as "open" for
  -- OLDEST_OPEN_DATE, which then reports a fully-reversed provision as 386 days
  -- old. Seen live on Mart 2180014 PROVISION FOR JULY.
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT c.ACCT, c.RD,
           GREATEST(0, LEAST(c.CR, c.CUM_CR - g.TOT_CONSUME)) AS RESID
    FROM credits c JOIN agg g ON g.ACCT = c.ACCT
  ) WHERE RESID >= 0.01
),
aged AS (
  SELECT r.ACCT,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) <= 30                       THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A0,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) BETWEEN  31 AND  90         THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A1,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) BETWEEN  91 AND 365         THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A2,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) > 365                       THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A3,
         SUM(CASE WHEN r.RD <  pr.FY_START                                     THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A_YE,
         SUM(CASE WHEN r.RD =  pr.GOLIVE                                       THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A_MIG,
         MIN(r.RD) AS OLDEST_OPEN
  FROM resid r CROSS JOIN params pr
  GROUP BY r.ACCT
)
SELECT
  '{{SCHEMA}}'                                             AS COMPANY_SCHEMA,
  pr.ASOF                                                  AS AS_OF,
  reg.FAMILY                                               AS FAMILY,
  reg.ACCT                                                 AS ACCT_CODE,
  a."AcctName"                                             AS ACCT_NAME,
  IFNULL(pa."AcctName",'')                                 AS PARENT_NAME,
  IFNULL(g.N_LINES,0)                                      AS N_LINES,
  g.FIRST_POST                                             AS FIRST_POST,
  g.LAST_POST                                              AS LAST_POST,
  DAYS_BETWEEN(g.LAST_POST, pr.ASOF)                       AS DAYS_SINCE_LAST_POST,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0)/100000, 2)                      AS CREATED_CR_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0)/100000, 2)                      AS REVERSED_DR_L,
  ROUND((IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0)-IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0))/100000, 2) AS NET_DR_MINUS_CR_L,
  ROUND(GREATEST(0, IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0)-IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0))/100000, 2) AS OUTSTANDING_CR_L,
  ROUND(GREATEST(0, IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0)-IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0))/100000, 2) AS DEBIT_BAL_L,
  ROUND(CAST(a."CurrTotal" AS DOUBLE)/100000, 2)           AS OACT_CURRTOTAL_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.CR_FYTD,0)/100000, 2)                     AS CREATED_FYTD_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.DR_FYTD,0)/100000, 2)                     AS REVERSED_FYTD_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A0,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_0_30_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A1,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_31_90_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A2,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_91_365_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A3,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_365P_L,
  ag.OLDEST_OPEN                                           AS OLDEST_OPEN_DATE,
  DAYS_BETWEEN(ag.OLDEST_OPEN, pr.ASOF)                    AS OLDEST_OPEN_DAYS,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A_YE,0)/100000, 2)                       AS CROSSED_YEAREND_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A_MIG,0)/100000, 2)                      AS MIGRATED_OPENING_L,
  CASE WHEN IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0) > 0 AND IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0) = 0 THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS NEVER_REVERSED,
  CASE WHEN IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0) - IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0) > 1      THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS DEBIT_BALANCE_FLAG,
  CASE WHEN IFNULL(g.MOVE_ALL,0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(100.0 * g.MOVE_MANUAL / g.MOVE_ALL, 1) END AS MANUAL_JE_PCT,

SUM(CASE WHEN RD >= (SELECT FY_START FROM params) THEN CR ELSE 0 END) AS CR_FYTD,
         SUM(CASE WHEN RD >= (SELECT FY_START FROM params) THEN DR ELSE 0 END) AS DR_FYTD,
         SUM(CASE WHEN PMEMO = 1 THEN CR ELSE 0 END) AS CR_PMEMO,
         SUM(CASE WHEN MANUAL_JE = 1 THEN DR + CR ELSE 0 END) AS MOVE_MANUAL,
         SUM(DR + CR) AS MOVE_ALL,
         -- everything that CONSUMES a provision: real debits plus any line
         -- booked as a negative credit. Guarantees SUM(RESID) == TOT_CR-TOT_DR.
         SUM(CASE WHEN NET_CR < 0 THEN -NET_CR ELSE 0 END) AS TOT_CONSUME
  FROM lines GROUP BY ACCT
),
-- FIFO: oldest credit first; total debits consume them in order
credits AS (
  SELECT l.ACCT, l.RD, l.NET_CR AS CR,
         SUM(l.NET_CR) OVER (PARTITION BY l.ACCT
                         ORDER BY l.RD, l.TID, l.LID
                         ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS CUM_CR
  FROM lines l WHERE l.NET_CR > 0
),
resid AS (
  -- >= 0.01 tolerance: the running totals are DOUBLE (DECIMAL would overflow on
  -- the 5,800-line COGS PAYABLE account), and a credit line that FIFO consumes
  -- EXACTLY leaves a ~1e-7 float residue. Without the tolerance that residue is
  -- rounded away in the money columns but still counts as "open" for
  -- OLDEST_OPEN_DATE, which then reports a fully-reversed provision as 386 days
  -- old. Seen live on Mart 2180014 PROVISION FOR JULY.
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT c.ACCT, c.RD,
           GREATEST(0, LEAST(c.CR, c.CUM_CR - g.TOT_CONSUME)) AS RESID
    FROM credits c JOIN agg g ON g.ACCT = c.ACCT
  ) WHERE RESID >= 0.01
),
aged AS (
  SELECT r.ACCT,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) <= 30                       THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A0,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) BETWEEN  31 AND  90         THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A1,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) BETWEEN  91 AND 365         THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A2,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) > 365                       THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A3,
         SUM(CASE WHEN r.RD <  pr.FY_START                                     THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A_YE,
         SUM(CASE WHEN r.RD =  pr.GOLIVE                                       THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A_MIG,
         MIN(r.RD) AS OLDEST_OPEN
  FROM resid r CROSS JOIN params pr
  GROUP BY r.ACCT
)

section_traps: CROSSED_YEAREND_L and MIGRATED_OPENING_L are RE-CUTS of the same FIFO residual already inside AGE_0_30_L..AGE_365P_L. Adding them as extra buckets inflates Oil by Rs 3.23 Cr on a Rs 5.99 Cr base. Only the four AGE_* columns are additive, and they sum to OUTSTANDING_CR_L.

The headline is GROSS. OUTSTANDING_CR_L is floored at zero per account, so over-reversal is not netted: Oil's real net register position is Rs 4.62 Cr, not the Rs 5.99 Cr headline. Column: DEBIT_BAL_L (Rs 1.37 Cr Oil / Rs 16.63 L Mart / Rs 5.15 L Bev).

v1 renders the over-reversal KPI as String(dr.length) — a COUNT of 8 — so Rs 1.37 Cr never reaches the page. Column: DEBIT_BAL_L. The single biggest is Oil 2161007 SALARY PAYABLE JUL at a Rs 1.10 Cr DEBIT, which is itself worth an Accounts look.

'Older than a year' reads as neglect and mostly is not. AGE_365P_L on Oil is Rs 1.60 Cr of which Rs 1.52 Cr (95.3%) is the 2024-09-30 SAP go-live opening — balance-sheet carry-forward, not an unreviewed provision. Ex-migration it is Rs 7.49 L. Never render AGE_365P_L without MIGRATED_OPENING_L beside it.

Every money column is LAKHS. CREATED_CR_L, OUTSTANDING_CR_L, PROV_MEMO_CR_L and NET_DR_MINUS_CR_L contain '_CR' but do not END in it, so scale() must take the _L branch. Rename any of them to _CR and the page renders 100x too large.

Sign convention: NET_DR_MINUS_CR_L and OACT_CURRTOTAL_L are Debit-minus-Credit, so NEGATIVE means still provided for. Plotting either raw draws provisions as negative bars and over-reversal as positive.

The ageing is a MODELLING CHOICE, not something SAP says. JDT1.IntrnMatch = 0, ExtrMatch = 0 and Closed = 'N' on 100% of 15,630 register lines in all three books, so SAP cannot say which provision is still open. Debits consume the OLDEST credit first, which deliberately ages the residual as old as possible. Never caption a bucket chart 'per SAP'.

This is a G/L register, not a party or document register — no CardCode, no DocEntry, no DocStatus. C-0019 / C-0021 / C-0005 do not bite here. What does bite: 'total liabilities = payables + provisions' is not a supported sum. Oil 2110008 SUNDRY CREDITORS CLEARING (Rs 55.32 L) and Bev 2110008 (Rs 2.23 L) are fed through five internal clearing VENDOR cards that also appear in vendor-ageing. Measured on today's data the vendor-side ADJ_OPEN on those cards is Rs 29,897 (Oil, VENDA000987 INCENTIVE TA/DA/PAYABLE) and Rs 500 (Bev), so the arithmetic overlap is small — but it is not zero, and the two sections must never be added.

Rounding is coarse: every _L column is ROUND(x/100000, 2), i.e. Rs 1,000 granularity. Per-row the four AGE_* buckets can miss OUTSTANDING_CR_L by Rs 1,000 (live today: Oil 2163025 BLOWING CONVERSION PAYABLE, Mart 2180010 PROVISION FOR CLAIMS PAYABLE -RK). Book-level route deltas run to Rs 2,000. Every check must use a Rs 1,000 x rowcount tolerance; exact equality WILL false-alarm.

Dormant accounts are published on purpose (25 nil rows Oil, 24 Mart, 24 Bev out of 53/40/39). Counting rows as 'provision accounts' overstates activity about 2.6x. Count OUTSTANDING_CR_L > 0 — that is 20 / 9 / 10.
NEVER_REVERSED reads 'N' for an account that has never been posted at all (lifetime credit is 0). It is not a 'has been reversed' flag. Column: NEVER_REVERSED, cross-read with N_LINES.

The C_OTHER_BY_MEMO gate (>= Rs 5 L memo-tagged credit AND >= 25% of the account's total credit) is hard-coded and absolute, not scaled to book size. Mart yields no C_OTHER_BY_MEMO row at all — that is data, not a failure, and the family chart must not draw a zero slice or an error.

OACT_CURRTOTAL_L is a LIFETIME balance and is NOT filtered by as_of. It equals the as-of figure today only because there are zero future-dated JE lines on register accounts. Any historical as-of run will make the OACT cross-check legitimately disagree, and the check dot must report 'not applicable at this as-of', not red.

PROV_MEMO_CR_L is a weak label, not a classification. Its only real job is the C_OTHER_BY_MEMO gate. Book-wide it covers 22.7% of Oil's lifetime credits, 59.5% of Mart's, 30.9% of Bev's — do not present it as 'how much of this is really a provision'.

There is no detail slice. provisions has summary rows only (data.json detail: {}), so no page may offer a drill to individual JDT1 journal lines, a JE memo list, or a posting timeline. gl-account.html for a provision account can show only the 30 summary columns for that one account plus its history.jsonl trend.
N_LINES counts BOTH legs of storno reversals (160 of them touch Oil's register accounts), so it measures posting volume, not the number of provisions raised.

CREATED_CR_L is literally SUM(Credit), so a line posted as a NEGATIVE credit reduces 'created' instead of appearing as a reversal. Created minus Reversed is therefore not exactly 'raised less released' in accounting terms — it is a net of the two columns as SAP stores them.
Month names in ACCT_NAME (FREIGHT PAYABLE JUN, SALARY PAYABLE JUL) are the month PROVIDED FOR, not the month posted, and the FIFO ages by RefDate. Do not read the account name as a date.

sql.text:
resid AS (
  -- >= 0.01 tolerance: the running totals are DOUBLE (DECIMAL would overflow on
  -- the 5,800-line COGS PAYABLE account), and a credit line that FIFO consumes
  -- EXACTLY leaves a ~1e-7 float residue. Without the tolerance that residue is
  -- rounded away in the money columns but still counts as "open" for
  -- OLDEST_OPEN_DATE, which then reports a fully-reversed provision as 386 days
  -- old. Seen live on Mart 2180014 PROVISION FOR JULY.
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT c.ACCT, c.RD,
           GREATEST(0, LEAST(c.CR, c.CUM_CR - g.TOT_CONSUME)) AS RESID
    FROM credits c JOIN agg g ON g.ACCT = c.ACCT
  ) WHERE RESID >= 0.01
),
aged AS (
  SELECT r.ACCT,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) <= 30                       THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A0,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) BETWEEN  31 AND  90         THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A1,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) BETWEEN  91 AND 365         THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A2,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DAYS_BETWEEN(r.RD, pr.ASOF) > 365                       THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A3,
         SUM(CASE WHEN r.RD <  pr.FY_START                                     THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A_YE,
         SUM(CASE WHEN r.RD =  pr.GOLIVE                                       THEN r.RESID ELSE 0 END) AS A_MIG,
         MIN(r.RD) AS OLDEST_OPEN
  FROM resid r CROSS JOIN params pr
  GROUP BY r.ACCT
)
SELECT
  '{{SCHEMA}}'                                             AS COMPANY_SCHEMA,
  pr.ASOF                                                  AS AS_OF,
  reg.FAMILY                                               AS FAMILY,
  reg.ACCT                                                 AS ACCT_CODE,
  a."AcctName"                                             AS ACCT_NAME,
  IFNULL(pa."AcctName",'')                                 AS PARENT_NAME,
  IFNULL(g.N_LINES,0)                                      AS N_LINES,
  g.FIRST_POST                                             AS FIRST_POST,
  g.LAST_POST                                              AS LAST_POST,
  DAYS_BETWEEN(g.LAST_POST, pr.ASOF)                       AS DAYS_SINCE_LAST_POST,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0)/100000, 2)                      AS CREATED_CR_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0)/100000, 2)                      AS REVERSED_DR_L,
  ROUND((IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0)-IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0))/100000, 2) AS NET_DR_MINUS_CR_L,
  ROUND(GREATEST(0, IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0)-IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0))/100000, 2) AS OUTSTANDING_CR_L,
  ROUND(GREATEST(0, IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0)-IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0))/100000, 2) AS DEBIT_BAL_L,
  ROUND(CAST(a."CurrTotal" AS DOUBLE)/100000, 2)           AS OACT_CURRTOTAL_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.CR_FYTD,0)/100000, 2)                     AS CREATED_FYTD_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.DR_FYTD,0)/100000, 2)                     AS REVERSED_FYTD_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A0,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_0_30_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A1,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_31_90_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A2,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_91_365_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A3,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_365P_L,
  ag.OLDEST_OPEN                                           AS OLDEST_OPEN_DATE,
  DAYS_BETWEEN(ag.OLDEST_OPEN, pr.ASOF)                    AS OLDEST_OPEN_DAYS,

ROUND((IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0)-IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0))/100000, 2) AS NET_DR_MINUS_CR_L,
  ROUND(GREATEST(0, IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0)-IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0))/100000, 2) AS OUTSTANDING_CR_L,
  ROUND(GREATEST(0, IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0)-IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0))/100000, 2) AS DEBIT_BAL_L,
  ROUND(CAST(a."CurrTotal" AS DOUBLE)/100000, 2)           AS OACT_CURRTOTAL_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.CR_FYTD,0)/100000, 2)                     AS CREATED_FYTD_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(g.DR_FYTD,0)/100000, 2)                     AS REVERSED_FYTD_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A0,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_0_30_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A1,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_31_90_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A2,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_91_365_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A3,0)/100000, 2)                         AS AGE_365P_L,
  ag.OLDEST_OPEN                                           AS OLDEST_OPEN_DATE,
  DAYS_BETWEEN(ag.OLDEST_OPEN, pr.ASOF)                    AS OLDEST_OPEN_DAYS,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A_YE,0)/100000, 2)                       AS CROSSED_YEAREND_L,
  ROUND(IFNULL(ag.A_MIG,0)/100000, 2)                      AS MIGRATED_OPENING_L,
  CASE WHEN IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0) > 0 AND IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0) = 0 THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS NEVER_REVERSED,
  CASE WHEN IFNULL(g.TOT_DR,0) - IFNULL(g.TOT_CR,0) > 1      THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS DEBIT_BALANCE_FLAG,
