section_traps: FACETED: the summary array stacks six populations. The company total is the single row with SCOPE=='TOTAL' (GRP_KEY=='ALL'). Summing all 72 rows counts every return about four times over (TOTAL + CLASS + CREDIT_NOTE + MONTH, plus partial CUSTOMER overlap). Column that causes it: SCOPE.

NO_CN_REASON is a partition of the NO_CREDIT_NOTE row, NOT of TOTAL. Its three RET_DOCS sum to RET_DOCS_NO_CN (421/1370/60), never to RET_DOCS. Adding it to the CLASS rows to 'get the total' double-counts the uncredited population. Column: SCOPE + GRP_KEY.

CN_DOCS IS NOT ADDITIVE. It is COUNT(DISTINCT credit note) computed inside each group. Oil's 23 MONTH rows sum to 2518 against a TOTAL of 2517 — verified live in this snapshot — because one credit note credits returns dated in two different months. Every other measure is additive. Column: CN_DOCS.

RET_GROSS IS NOT THE SIZE OF THE RETURN. 1104 of Oil's 1817, 601 of Mart's 1793 and 134 of Bev's 161 live returns carry DocTotal = 0; the note is a stock-movement document and the money is settled on a separate credit note. Cost/gross runs 2.52x in Oil and 2.93x in Mart. Column: RET_GROSS / RET_DOCS_ZERO_VALUE.

RET_STOCK_COST IS 'WHAT SAP PUT BACK INTO INVENTORY', NEVER 'WHAT THE GOODS WERE WORTH'. Computed live from Bev's complete register: 133 of 161 live returns carrying 148,894 of 170,476 pieces (87.3%) have STOCK_COST = 0, because the item's warehouse moving-average cost is nil. Bev's ₹2.59 L is exact and covers 13% of what came back. Mart has the same problem at roughly 27% by pieces per the notes — NOT recomputable from data.json because Mart's detail is capped. Column: RET_STOCK_COST vs RET_QTY_PCS.

BEV'S RET_STOCK_COST IS 54% ONE JOB-WORKER DOCUMENT. DocNum 1608258003, 2025-08-08, CUSTA001061 BHARTI MACHINERY TOOLS, ₹1,40,113 of ₹2,59,427 — ORDN is occasionally used for RAW MATERIAL returns from job-workers, not customer returns (Oil 3 such documents, Mart 0, Bev 1). It is also why Bev's top CUSTOMER row shows RET_QTY_PCS = 0 and SALES_NET = 0. Verified live in this snapshot. Column: RET_STOCK_COST on the CUSTOMER scope.

NEVER ADD RET_QTY_PCS AND RET_QTY_OTHER_UOM. RDN1 mixes PCS/SET/KGS/NOS/LTR/MTR/DRM/GMS. Bev's RET_QTY_OTHER_UOM is 245,350.5 of which 242,950.5 (99%) is GRAMS on that one raw-material document. Column: RET_QTY_OTHER_UOM.

'NO CREDIT NOTE' MEANS 'NO CREDIT NOTE LINKED IN SAP' — a work list, not a loss. 2723 of Oil's 6147, 975 of Mart's 4384 and 161 of Bev's 399 live credit notes carry no base document on any line, so a credited customer can still land here. A ±30-day proximity probe put roughly half of Oil's and 40% of Mart's billed-uncredited returns as plausibly credited but never linked (INFERRED, deliberately not a column). Structural false positives are separately measured at 4 of Oil's 212 and 3 of Mart's 913. Column: RET_DOCS_NO_CN.

COUNTING ALL OF RET_DOCS_NO_CN AS MISSING CREDITS OVERSTATES THE EXCEPTION ~2x IN OIL (421 against an actionable 212). FROM_DELIVERY_UNBILLED means no credit is due; STANDALONE_NO_LINK is unanswerable from document structure. Only RET_DOCS_NO_CN_BILLED is actionable. Column: RET_DOCS_NO_CN vs RET_DOCS_NO_CN_BILLED.

RET_DOCS_OPEN MEASURES NOTHING (C-0019). DocStatus='O' is unreliable at JIVO; it is published as a labelled diagnostic. Nothing in this section is outstanding — a return note has no balance. Column: RET_DOCS_OPEN.

THE CLASS BRANCH ROW CAN CARRY SALES WITH ZERO RETURNS. Oil's BRANCH row is RET_DOCS = 0 against SALES_NET = ₹73.20 Cr — a FULL OUTER JOIN between the return side and the sales side, not a fault. Rendered as a returns row it is a row of zeros; rendered as '0% return rate' it is correct but reads like good news about a book that simply has no branch returns. Column: SALES_NET on SCOPE='CLASS'.

A MONTH ROW CAN EXIST WITH ZERO RETURNS. Mart's 2024-12 and Bev's 2026-05 have RET_DOCS = 0 and a real SALES_NET, for the same FULL OUTER JOIN reason. A monthly bar chart must draw them as a genuine zero, not drop the month and imply continuity. Column: RET_DOCS on SCOPE='MONTH'.

SALES_NET, CN_PCT_OF_SALES AND RET_COST_PCT_OF_SALES ARE NULL ON EVERY CREDIT_NOTE AND NO_CN_REASON ROW, and NULL on any CUSTOMER row with no invoiced sales (4 in Oil, 2 in Bev in this snapshot). Coercing None to 0 and summing produces a confident ₹0 sales figure. Columns: SALES_NET, CN_PCT_OF_SALES, RET_COST_PCT_OF_SALES.

CN_PCT_OF_SALES IS NOT 'SALES RETURNS AS A % OF SALES'. It counts only credit notes raised against a RETURN NOTE (BaseType=16). All Oil credit notes together are about 5.1% of Oil sales against the 0.91% this column shows — invoice-based (₹21.91 Cr) and standalone (₹16.32 Cr) notes are outside it by definition. Column: CN_PCT_OF_SALES.

RET_COST_PCT_OF_SALES IS COST OVER REVENUE — unlike over unlike. Right for sizing the stock coming back, wrong quoted as 'x% of our sales came back', which is a revenue ratio and larger by the gross margin. It also inherits the zero-valuation blind spot. Column: RET_COST_PCT_OF_SALES.

INTERCOMPANY IS 57.6% OF OIL'S RETURN COST AND A GROUP-NAME TEST ALONE FINDS NONE OF IT. Exactly 0 Oil returns sit in a '%BRANCH%' card group, yet CUSTA000606 JIVO MART PVT LTD — card group 'DELHI' — is 477 of 1817 returns and ₹5.02 Cr at cost. Classification is group-name THEN card-name ('%JIVO%'), never a hard-coded code list, because the same CardCode is a different party in a different book. C-0005 / C-0020. Column: PARTY_CLASS / GRP_KEY on SCOPE='CLASS'.

THE DETAIL ARRAY IS CAPPED AT 500 AND TRUNCATED BY EXC_RANK — any total computed from it is wrong for Oil and Mart. Live shape: Oil 500 rows (ranks 1/2/3 complete at 212/115/94, rank 4 truncated to 79 of ~1396), Mart 500 rows ALL rank 1 (500 of a true 913 — nothing in Mart's register is a complete population), Bev 185 rows (the entire register: 161 live + 12 cancelled + 12 mirrors). Completeness rule: a rank is complete iff a strictly higher rank is present in the array, or len(detail) < 500. Column: EXC_RANK.

CANCELED IS THREE-VALUED (C-0021). The summary counts 'N' only. The detail keeps all three and decodes them into CANCEL_STATUS: filtering "!= 'CANCELLED'" leaves the CANCELLATION_DOC mirrors in and double-counts (Oil 9 mirrors and 8 cancelled originals survive in the capped slice; Bev's complete register has 12 of each). Column: CANCEL_STATUS.

DELIVERY-LINKED AND CREDIT-NOTED ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE AT JIVO. All 306 of Oil's delivery-based returns land in NO_CREDIT_NOTE and the HAS_CREDIT_NOTE row shows RET_DOCS_FROM_DELIVERY = 0. So any chart of 'returns with a base link' is, entirely and only, a chart of uncredited returns. Column: RET_DOCS_FROM_DELIVERY.

RET_STOCK_COST_NO_CN DOES NOT MATCH THE BOARD'S MONEY-COLUMN REGEX (it ends _NO_CN). v1 renders it correctly only because the KPI calls money() explicitly. Put it in a table without an explicit formatter and ₹1.52 Cr prints as the bare integer 15217213. Column: RET_STOCK_COST_NO_CN.

DETAIL MONEY IS ROUNDED PER DOCUMENT, SUMMARY MONEY ONCE AT THE END. Oil's uncredited cost is ₹15,217,213.26 from the detail against ₹15,217,213.18 from the summary — 8 paise over 421 documents. A check must tolerate a sub-rupee delta or it will cry wolf on every build. Column: STOCK_COST vs RET_STOCK_COST_NO_CN.
BRANCH_NAME CASE IS INCONSISTENT IN THE BEV DETAIL ('DELHI' and 'Delhi', 'PUNJAB' and 'Punjab'). Upper-case before grouping or one branch splits into two bars. Column: BRANCH_NAME.

CN_DOCNUMS IS TRUNCATED TO 200 CHARACTERS. Never count its commas to recover CN_COUNT, and never union it across rows to rebuild CN_DOCS — one Oil return is credited by 82 separate notes and the list is cut long before it lists them. Column: CN_DOCNUMS.

DATA.JSON MOVES UNDER YOU. The VPS live-refresh cron rewrites site/data.json every 2 minutes; SALES_NET moved ~0.04% between two reads while this spec was written. Every live figure here is from the frozen 2026-08-22T19:05:02+05:30 build. Any regression test must pin generated_at, not compare against a hard-coded number.

         CASE WHEN s.NET > 0 THEN ROUND(t.CST/s.NET*100,4) ELSE NULL END AS RET_COST_PCT_OF_SALES

caveats.right: In the HANA tables the flag has THREE values: 'N' = live, 'Y' = the cancelled original, and 'C' = the system-generated cancellation mirror SAP posts to reverse it. Y and C always appear as exact matching pairs carrying the same value, so a <>'Y' test keeps every mirror and double-counts. Measured live on Oil 2026-08-21: OINV 30,387 'N' (1045.62 Cr) plus 320 'Y' and 320 'C' at 37.27 Cr each; OPCH 16,101 'N' plus 113+113 at 15.96 Cr each; OPDN 10,640 'N' plus 473+473 at 94.63 Cr each; ORDN 1,817 'N' plus 107+107 at 0.49 Cr each. Same pattern in Mart and Beverages. Always test CANCELED='N' positively. Note the Service Layer differs: it exposes only Cancelled 'tYES'/'tNO', so the documented OData filter Cancelled eq 'tNO' is already correct and is not affected.
caveats.rule: HANA "CANCELED" is three-valued: 'N' live, 'Y' cancelled original, 'C' its system mirror. Always filter CANCELED='N' - a <>'Y' test keeps the mirrors and double-counts (Oil OPDN +94.63 Cr).
caveats.title: HANA CANCELED is three-valued — filter ='N', never <>'Y'
caveats.wrong: Excluded cancelled documents in HANA SQL by writing "CANCELED" <> 'Y' (or omitting the filter), assuming the flag is a two-valued Y/N.

sql.text:
WITH RET AS (
  SELECT h."DocEntry"   AS DOC_ENTRY,
         h."DocDate"    AS DOC_DATE,
         h."DocStatus"  AS DOC_STATUS,
         h."CardCode"   AS CARD_CODE,
         IFNULL(c."CardName", h."CardName") AS CARD_NAME,
         CASE WHEN UPPER(IFNULL(g."GroupName",'')) LIKE '%BRANCH%'        THEN 'BRANCH'
              WHEN UPPER(IFNULL(c."CardName",h."CardName")) LIKE '%JIVO%' THEN 'INTERCOMPANY'
              ELSE 'EXTERNAL' END AS PARTY_CLASS,
         CAST(h."DocTotal" AS DOUBLE) AS GROSS_AMT,
         CAST(h."VatSum"   AS DOUBLE) AS GST_AMT,
         h."TransId"    AS TRANS_ID
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.ORDN h
  LEFT JOIN {{SCHEMA}}.OCRD c ON c."CardCode"  = h."CardCode"
  LEFT JOIN {{SCHEMA}}.OCRG g ON g."GroupCode" = c."GroupCode"
                             AND g."GroupType" = c."CardType"
  WHERE h."CANCELED" = 'N'
    AND h."DocDate" <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'
    AND h."DocDate" <> DATE'2024-09-30'          -- trap 10; no return note lands here anyway
),

R_CLS AS (
  SELECT
         PARTY_CLASS K,
         COUNT(*) D,
         SUM(CASE WHEN GROSS_AMT = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DZERO,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DOC_STATUS = 'O' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DOPEN,
         SUM(FROM_DELIVERY) DDLN,
         SUM(QTY_PCS) QP, SUM(QTY_OTHER) QO,
         SUM(GROSS_AMT - GST_AMT) NET, SUM(GST_AMT) GST, SUM(GROSS_AMT) GRS,
         SUM(STOCK_COST) CST,
         SUM(CASE WHEN HAS_CN = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DNOCN,
         SUM(CASE WHEN HAS_CN = 0 AND DLV_INVOICED = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DNOCNB,
         SUM(CASE WHEN HAS_CN = 0 THEN QTY_PCS ELSE 0 END) QPNOCN,
         SUM(CASE WHEN HAS_CN = 0 THEN STOCK_COST ELSE 0 END) CSTNOCN,
         SUM(CN_NET) CNN
  FROM R
  GROUP BY PARTY_CLASS
),

R_TOT AS (
  SELECT
         COUNT(*) D,

caveats.wrong: Split external vs intercompany by excluding only CUSTA000606 (JIVO MART PVT LTD), per C-0002. Measured live 2026-08-21: Mart VENDA000001 'JIVO WELLNESS PVT LTD' is in group PURCHASE at -20.93 Cr and is Mart's single largest payable; Mart VENDA000004 'JIVO WELLNESS PVT LTD - DL' also in PURCHASE; Oil VENDA000483 'JIVO MART PVT LTD' is in group E-COMMERCE at -2.25 Cr. Correction C-0005 lists 23 intercompany CardCodes but they are all CUSTA* — it covers no vendor codes at all. Test the group AND the CardName (JIVO / AKAL), and flag the rows rather than dropping them.

section_traps: FACETED: the summary array stacks six populations. The company total is the single row with SCOPE=='TOTAL' (GRP_KEY=='ALL'). Summing all 72 rows counts every return about four times over (TOTAL + CLASS + CREDIT_NOTE + MONTH, plus partial CUSTOMER overlap). Column that causes it: SCOPE.

NO_CN_REASON is a partition of the NO_CREDIT_NOTE row, NOT of TOTAL. Its three RET_DOCS sum to RET_DOCS_NO_CN (421/1370/60), never to RET_DOCS. Adding it to the CLASS rows to 'get the total' double-counts the uncredited population. Column: SCOPE + GRP_KEY.

CN_DOCS IS NOT ADDITIVE. It is COUNT(DISTINCT credit note) computed inside each group. Oil's 23 MONTH rows sum to 2518 against a TOTAL of 2517 — verified live in this snapshot — because one credit note credits returns dated in two different months. Every other measure is additive. Column: CN_DOCS.

RET_GROSS IS NOT THE SIZE OF THE RETURN. 1104 of Oil's 1817, 601 of Mart's 1793 and 134 of Bev's 161 live returns carry DocTotal = 0; the note is a stock-movement document and the money is settled on a separate credit note. Cost/gross runs 2.52x in Oil and 2.93x in Mart. Column: RET_GROSS / RET_DOCS_ZERO_VALUE.

RET_STOCK_COST IS 'WHAT SAP PUT BACK INTO INVENTORY', NEVER 'WHAT THE GOODS WERE WORTH'. Computed live from Bev's complete register: 133 of 161 live returns carrying 148,894 of 170,476 pieces (87.3%) have STOCK_COST = 0, because the item's warehouse moving-average cost is nil. Bev's ₹2.59 L is exact and covers 13% of what came back. Mart has the same problem at roughly 27% by pieces per the notes — NOT recomputable from data.json because Mart's detail is capped. Column: RET_STOCK_COST vs RET_QTY_PCS.

BEV'S RET_STOCK_COST IS 54% ONE JOB-WORKER DOCUMENT. DocNum 1608258003, 2025-08-08, CUSTA001061 BHARTI MACHINERY TOOLS, ₹1,40,113 of ₹2,59,427 — ORDN is occasionally used for RAW MATERIAL returns from job-workers, not customer returns (Oil 3 such documents, Mart 0, Bev 1). It is also why Bev's top CUSTOMER row shows RET_QTY_PCS = 0 and SALES_NET = 0. Verified live in this snapshot. Column: RET_STOCK_COST on the CUSTOMER scope.

NEVER ADD RET_QTY_PCS AND RET_QTY_OTHER_UOM. RDN1 mixes PCS/SET/KGS/NOS/LTR/MTR/DRM/GMS. Bev's RET_QTY_OTHER_UOM is 245,350.5 of which 242,950.5 (99%) is GRAMS on that one raw-material document. Column: RET_QTY_OTHER_UOM.

'NO CREDIT NOTE' MEANS 'NO CREDIT NOTE LINKED IN SAP' — a work list, not a loss. 2723 of Oil's 6147, 975 of Mart's 4384 and 161 of Bev's 399 live credit notes carry no base document on any line, so a credited customer can still land here. A ±30-day proximity probe put roughly half of Oil's and 40% of Mart's billed-uncredited returns as plausibly credited but never linked (INFERRED, deliberately not a column). Structural false positives are separately measured at 4 of Oil's 212 and 3 of Mart's 913. Column: RET_DOCS_NO_CN.

COUNTING ALL OF RET_DOCS_NO_CN AS MISSING CREDITS OVERSTATES THE EXCEPTION ~2x IN OIL (421 against an actionable 212). FROM_DELIVERY_UNBILLED means no credit is due; STANDALONE_NO_LINK is unanswerable from document structure. Only RET_DOCS_NO_CN_BILLED is actionable. Column: RET_DOCS_NO_CN vs RET_DOCS_NO_CN_BILLED.

RET_DOCS_OPEN MEASURES NOTHING (C-0019). DocStatus='O' is unreliable at JIVO; it is published as a labelled diagnostic. Nothing in this section is outstanding — a return note has no balance. Column: RET_DOCS_OPEN.

THE CLASS BRANCH ROW CAN CARRY SALES WITH ZERO RETURNS. Oil's BRANCH row is RET_DOCS = 0 against SALES_NET = ₹73.20 Cr — a FULL OUTER JOIN between the return side and the sales side, not a fault. Rendered as a returns row it is a row of zeros; rendered as '0% return rate' it is correct but reads like good news about a book that simply has no branch returns. Column: SALES_NET on SCOPE='CLASS'.

A MONTH ROW CAN EXIST WITH ZERO RETURNS. Mart's 2024-12 and Bev's 2026-05 have RET_DOCS = 0 and a real SALES_NET, for the same FULL OUTER JOIN reason. A monthly bar chart must draw them as a genuine zero, not drop the month and imply continuity. Column: RET_DOCS on SCOPE='MONTH'.

SALES_NET, CN_PCT_OF_SALES AND RET_COST_PCT_OF_SALES ARE NULL ON EVERY CREDIT_NOTE AND NO_CN_REASON ROW, and NULL on any CUSTOMER row with no invoiced sales (4 in Oil, 2 in Bev in this snapshot). Coercing None to 0 and summing produces a confident ₹0 sales figure. Columns: SALES_NET, CN_PCT_OF_SALES, RET_COST_PCT_OF_SALES.

CN_PCT_OF_SALES IS NOT 'SALES RETURNS AS A % OF SALES'. It counts only credit notes raised against a RETURN NOTE (BaseType=16). All Oil credit notes together are about 5.1% of Oil sales against the 0.91% this column shows — invoice-based (₹21.91 Cr) and standalone (₹16.32 Cr) notes are outside it by definition. Column: CN_PCT_OF_SALES.

RET_COST_PCT_OF_SALES IS COST OVER REVENUE — unlike over unlike. Right for sizing the stock coming back, wrong quoted as 'x% of our sales came back', which is a revenue ratio and larger by the gross margin. It also inherits the zero-valuation blind spot. Column: RET_COST_PCT_OF_SALES.

INTERCOMPANY IS 57.6% OF OIL'S RETURN COST AND A GROUP-NAME TEST ALONE FINDS NONE OF IT. Exactly 0 Oil returns sit in a '%BRANCH%' card group, yet CUSTA000606 JIVO MART PVT LTD — card group 'DELHI' — is 477 of 1817 returns and ₹5.02 Cr at cost. Classification is group-name THEN card-name ('%JIVO%'), never a hard-coded code list, because the same CardCode is a different party in a different book. C-0005 / C-0020. Column: PARTY_CLASS / GRP_KEY on SCOPE='CLASS'.

THE DETAIL ARRAY IS CAPPED AT 500 AND TRUNCATED BY EXC_RANK — any total computed from it is wrong for Oil and Mart. Live shape: Oil 500 rows (ranks 1/2/3 complete at 212/115/94, rank 4 truncated to 79 of ~1396), Mart 500 rows ALL rank 1 (500 of a true 913 — nothing in Mart's register is a complete population), Bev 185 rows (the entire register: 161 live + 12 cancelled + 12 mirrors). Completeness rule: a rank is complete iff a strictly higher rank is present in the array, or len(detail) < 500. Column: EXC_RANK.

CANCELED IS THREE-VALUED (C-0021). The summary counts 'N' only. The detail keeps all three and decodes them into CANCEL_STATUS: filtering "!= 'CANCELLED'" leaves the CANCELLATION_DOC mirrors in and double-counts (Oil 9 mirrors and 8 cancelled originals survive in the capped slice; Bev's complete register has 12 of each). Column: CANCEL_STATUS.

DELIVERY-LINKED AND CREDIT-NOTED ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE AT JIVO. All 306 of Oil's delivery-based returns land in NO_CREDIT_NOTE and the HAS_CREDIT_NOTE row shows RET_DOCS_FROM_DELIVERY = 0. So any chart of 'returns with a base link' is, entirely and only, a chart of uncredited returns. Column: RET_DOCS_FROM_DELIVERY.

RET_STOCK_COST_NO_CN DOES NOT MATCH THE BOARD'S MONEY-COLUMN REGEX (it ends _NO_CN). v1 renders it correctly only because the KPI calls money() explicitly. Put it in a table without an explicit formatter and ₹1.52 Cr prints as the bare integer 15217213. Column: RET_STOCK_COST_NO_CN.

DETAIL MONEY IS ROUNDED PER DOCUMENT, SUMMARY MONEY ONCE AT THE END. Oil's uncredited cost is ₹15,217,213.26 from the detail against ₹15,217,213.18 from the summary — 8 paise over 421 documents. A check must tolerate a sub-rupee delta or it will cry wolf on every build. Column: STOCK_COST vs RET_STOCK_COST_NO_CN.
BRANCH_NAME CASE IS INCONSISTENT IN THE BEV DETAIL ('DELHI' and 'Delhi', 'PUNJAB' and 'Punjab'). Upper-case before grouping or one branch splits into two bars. Column: BRANCH_NAME.

CN_DOCNUMS IS TRUNCATED TO 200 CHARACTERS. Never count its commas to recover CN_COUNT, and never union it across rows to rebuild CN_DOCS — one Oil return is credited by 82 separate notes and the list is cut long before it lists them. Column: CN_DOCNUMS.

sql.text:
QTY AS (
  SELECT l."DocEntry" AS DOC_ENTRY,
         SUM(CASE WHEN IFNULL(l."unitMsr",'PCS') = 'PCS'
                  THEN CAST(l."Quantity" AS DOUBLE) ELSE 0 END) AS QTY_PCS,
         SUM(CASE WHEN IFNULL(l."unitMsr",'PCS') = 'PCS'
                  THEN 0 ELSE CAST(l."Quantity" AS DOUBLE) END) AS QTY_OTHER
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.RDN1 l
  GROUP BY l."DocEntry"
),
-- base delivery, and whether that delivery was ever invoiced (traps 8 and 9)

caveats.right: In the HANA tables the flag has THREE values: 'N' = live, 'Y' = the cancelled original, and 'C' = the system-generated cancellation mirror SAP posts to reverse it. Y and C always appear as exact matching pairs carrying the same value, so a <>'Y' test keeps every mirror and double-counts. Measured live on Oil 2026-08-21: OINV 30,387 'N' (1045.62 Cr) plus 320 'Y' and 320 'C' at 37.27 Cr each; OPCH 16,101 'N' plus 113+113 at 15.96 Cr each; OPDN 10,640 'N' plus 473+473 at 94.63 Cr each; ORDN 1,817 'N' plus 107+107 at 0.49 Cr each. Same pattern in Mart and Beverages. Always test CANCELED='N' positively. Note the Service Layer differs: it exposes only Cancelled 'tYES'/'tNO', so the documented OData filter Cancelled eq 'tNO' is already correct and is not affected.
caveats.rule: HANA "CANCELED" is three-valued: 'N' live, 'Y' cancelled original, 'C' its system mirror. Always filter CANCELED='N' - a <>'Y' test keeps the mirrors and double-counts (Oil OPDN +94.63 Cr).
caveats.title: HANA CANCELED is three-valued — filter ='N', never <>'Y'
caveats.wrong: Excluded cancelled documents in HANA SQL by writing "CANCELED" <> 'Y' (or omitting the filter), assuming the flag is a two-valued Y/N.

Summing all 72 rows counts every return about four times over (TOTAL + CLASS + CREDIT_NOTE + MONTH, plus partial CUSTOMER overlap). Column that causes it: SCOPE.

NO_CN_REASON is a partition of the NO_CREDIT_NOTE row, NOT of TOTAL. Its three RET_DOCS sum to RET_DOCS_NO_CN (421/1370/60), never to RET_DOCS. Adding it to the CLASS rows to 'get the total' double-counts the uncredited population. Column: SCOPE + GRP_KEY.

CN_DOCS IS NOT ADDITIVE. It is COUNT(DISTINCT credit note) computed inside each group. Oil's 23 MONTH rows sum to 2518 against a TOTAL of 2517 — verified live in this snapshot — because one credit note credits returns dated in two different months. Every other measure is additive. Column: CN_DOCS.

RET_GROSS IS NOT THE SIZE OF THE RETURN. 1104 of Oil's 1817, 601 of Mart's 1793 and 134 of Bev's 161 live returns carry DocTotal = 0; the note is a stock-movement document and the money is settled on a separate credit note. Cost/gross runs 2.52x in Oil and 2.93x in Mart. Column: RET_GROSS / RET_DOCS_ZERO_VALUE.

RET_STOCK_COST IS 'WHAT SAP PUT BACK INTO INVENTORY', NEVER 'WHAT THE GOODS WERE WORTH'. Computed live from Bev's complete register: 133 of 161 live returns carrying 148,894 of 170,476 pieces (87.3%) have STOCK_COST = 0, because the item's warehouse moving-average cost is nil. Bev's ₹2.59 L is exact and covers 13% of what came back. Mart has the same problem at roughly 27% by pieces per the notes — NOT recomputable from data.json because Mart's detail is capped. Column: RET_STOCK_COST vs RET_QTY_PCS.

BEV'S RET_STOCK_COST IS 54% ONE JOB-WORKER DOCUMENT. DocNum 1608258003, 2025-08-08, CUSTA001061 BHARTI MACHINERY TOOLS, ₹1,40,113 of ₹2,59,427 — ORDN is occasionally used for RAW MATERIAL returns from job-workers, not customer returns (Oil 3 such documents, Mart 0, Bev 1). It is also why Bev's top CUSTOMER row shows RET_QTY_PCS = 0 and SALES_NET = 0. Verified live in this snapshot. Column: RET_STOCK_COST on the CUSTOMER scope.

NEVER ADD RET_QTY_PCS AND RET_QTY_OTHER_UOM. RDN1 mixes PCS/SET/KGS/NOS/LTR/MTR/DRM/GMS. Bev's RET_QTY_OTHER_UOM is 245,350.5 of which 242,950.5 (99%) is GRAMS on that one raw-material document. Column: RET_QTY_OTHER_UOM.

'NO CREDIT NOTE' MEANS 'NO CREDIT NOTE LINKED IN SAP' — a work list, not a loss. 2723 of Oil's 6147, 975 of Mart's 4384 and 161 of Bev's 399 live credit notes carry no base document on any line, so a credited customer can still land here. A ±30-day proximity probe put roughly half of Oil's and 40% of Mart's billed-uncredited returns as plausibly credited but never linked (INFERRED, deliberately not a column). Structural false positives are separately measured at 4 of Oil's 212 and 3 of Mart's 913. Column: RET_DOCS_NO_CN.

COUNTING ALL OF RET_DOCS_NO_CN AS MISSING CREDITS OVERSTATES THE EXCEPTION ~2x IN OIL (421 against an actionable 212). FROM_DELIVERY_UNBILLED means no credit is due; STANDALONE_NO_LINK is unanswerable from document structure. Only RET_DOCS_NO_CN_BILLED is actionable. Column: RET_DOCS_NO_CN vs RET_DOCS_NO_CN_BILLED.

RET_DOCS_OPEN MEASURES NOTHING (C-0019). DocStatus='O' is unreliable at JIVO; it is published as a labelled diagnostic. Nothing in this section is outstanding — a return note has no balance. Column: RET_DOCS_OPEN.

THE CLASS BRANCH ROW CAN CARRY SALES WITH ZERO RETURNS. Oil's BRANCH row is RET_DOCS = 0 against SALES_NET = ₹73.20 Cr — a FULL OUTER JOIN between the return side and the sales side, not a fault. Rendered as a returns row it is a row of zeros; rendered as '0% return rate' it is correct but reads like good news about a book that simply has no branch returns. Column: SALES_NET on SCOPE='CLASS'.

A MONTH ROW CAN EXIST WITH ZERO RETURNS. Mart's 2024-12 and Bev's 2026-05 have RET_DOCS = 0 and a real SALES_NET, for the same FULL OUTER JOIN reason. A monthly bar chart must draw them as a genuine zero, not drop the month and imply continuity. Column: RET_DOCS on SCOPE='MONTH'.

SALES_NET, CN_PCT_OF_SALES AND RET_COST_PCT_OF_SALES ARE NULL ON EVERY CREDIT_NOTE AND NO_CN_REASON ROW, and NULL on any CUSTOMER row with no invoiced sales (4 in Oil, 2 in Bev in this snapshot). Coercing None to 0 and summing produces a confident ₹0 sales figure. Columns: SALES_NET, CN_PCT_OF_SALES, RET_COST_PCT_OF_SALES.

CN_PCT_OF_SALES IS NOT 'SALES RETURNS AS A % OF SALES'. It counts only credit notes raised against a RETURN NOTE (BaseType=16). All Oil credit notes together are about 5.1% of Oil sales against the 0.91% this column shows — invoice-based (₹21.91 Cr) and standalone (₹16.32 Cr) notes are outside it by definition. Column: CN_PCT_OF_SALES.

RET_COST_PCT_OF_SALES IS COST OVER REVENUE — unlike over unlike. Right for sizing the stock coming back, wrong quoted as 'x% of our sales came back', which is a revenue ratio and larger by the gross margin. It also inherits the zero-valuation blind spot. Column: RET_COST_PCT_OF_SALES.

INTERCOMPANY IS 57.6% OF OIL'S RETURN COST AND A GROUP-NAME TEST ALONE FINDS NONE OF IT. Exactly 0 Oil returns sit in a '%BRANCH%' card group, yet CUSTA000606 JIVO MART PVT LTD — card group 'DELHI' — is 477 of 1817 returns and ₹5.02 Cr at cost. Classification is group-name THEN card-name ('%JIVO%'), never a hard-coded code list, because the same CardCode is a different party in a different book. C-0005 / C-0020. Column: PARTY_CLASS / GRP_KEY on SCOPE='CLASS'.

THE DETAIL ARRAY IS CAPPED AT 500 AND TRUNCATED BY EXC_RANK — any total computed from it is wrong for Oil and Mart. Live shape: Oil 500 rows (ranks 1/2/3 complete at 212/115/94, rank 4 truncated to 79 of ~1396), Mart 500 rows ALL rank 1 (500 of a true 913 — nothing in Mart's register is a complete population), Bev 185 rows (the entire register: 161 live + 12 cancelled + 12 mirrors). Completeness rule: a rank is complete iff a strictly higher rank is present in the array, or len(detail) < 500. Column: EXC_RANK.

CANCELED IS THREE-VALUED (C-0021). The summary counts 'N' only. The detail keeps all three and decodes them into CANCEL_STATUS: filtering "!= 'CANCELLED'" leaves the CANCELLATION_DOC mirrors in and double-counts (Oil 9 mirrors and 8 cancelled originals survive in the capped slice; Bev's complete register has 12 of each). Column: CANCEL_STATUS.

DELIVERY-LINKED AND CREDIT-NOTED ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE AT JIVO. All 306 of Oil's delivery-based returns land in NO_CREDIT_NOTE and the HAS_CREDIT_NOTE row shows RET_DOCS_FROM_DELIVERY = 0. So any chart of 'returns with a base link' is, entirely and only, a chart of uncredited returns. Column: RET_DOCS_FROM_DELIVERY.

RET_STOCK_COST_NO_CN DOES NOT MATCH THE BOARD'S MONEY-COLUMN REGEX (it ends _NO_CN). v1 renders it correctly only because the KPI calls money() explicitly. Put it in a table without an explicit formatter and ₹1.52 Cr prints as the bare integer 15217213. Column: RET_STOCK_COST_NO_CN.

DETAIL MONEY IS ROUNDED PER DOCUMENT, SUMMARY MONEY ONCE AT THE END. Oil's uncredited cost is ₹15,217,213.26 from the detail against ₹15,217,213.18 from the summary — 8 paise over 421 documents. A check must tolerate a sub-rupee delta or it will cry wolf on every build. Column: STOCK_COST vs RET_STOCK_COST_NO_CN.
BRANCH_NAME CASE IS INCONSISTENT IN THE BEV DETAIL ('DELHI' and 'Delhi', 'PUNJAB' and 'Punjab'). Upper-case before grouping or one branch splits into two bars. Column: BRANCH_NAME.

CN_DOCNUMS IS TRUNCATED TO 200 CHARACTERS. Never count its commas to recover CN_COUNT, and never union it across rows to rebuild CN_DOCS — one Oil return is credited by 82 separate notes and the list is cut long before it lists them. Column: CN_DOCNUMS.

sql.text:
SAL AS (
  SELECT h."DocDate"  AS DOC_DATE,
         h."CardCode" AS CARD_CODE,
         CASE WHEN UPPER(IFNULL(g."GroupName",'')) LIKE '%BRANCH%'        THEN 'BRANCH'
              WHEN UPPER(IFNULL(c."CardName",h."CardName")) LIKE '%JIVO%' THEN 'INTERCOMPANY'
              ELSE 'EXTERNAL' END AS PARTY_CLASS,
         CAST(h."DocTotal" AS DOUBLE) - CAST(h."VatSum" AS DOUBLE) AS NET_AMT
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.OINV h
  LEFT JOIN {{SCHEMA}}.OCRD c ON c."CardCode"  = h."CardCode"
  LEFT JOIN {{SCHEMA}}.OCRG g ON g."GroupCode" = c."GroupCode"
                             AND g."GroupType" = c."CardType"
  WHERE h."CANCELED" = 'N'
    AND h."DocDate" <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'
    AND h."DocDate" <> DATE'2024-09-30'
),
S_TOT AS (SELECT SUM(NET_AMT) NET FROM SAL),
S_CLS AS (SELECT PARTY_CLASS K, SUM(NET_AMT) NET FROM SAL GROUP BY PARTY_CLASS),
S_MTH AS (SELECT TO_VARCHAR(DOC_DATE,'YYYY-MM') K, SUM(NET_AMT) NET FROM SAL GROUP BY TO_VARCHAR(DOC_DATE,'YYYY-MM')),
S_CUS AS (SELECT CARD_CODE K, SUM(NET_AMT) NET FROM SAL GROUP BY CARD_CODE),

sql.text:
R_WHY AS (
  SELECT
         CASE WHEN FROM_DELIVERY = 0 THEN 'STANDALONE_NO_LINK'
              WHEN DLV_INVOICED = 1 THEN 'FROM_DELIVERY_INVOICED'
              ELSE 'FROM_DELIVERY_UNBILLED' END K,
         COUNT(*) D,
         SUM(CASE WHEN GROSS_AMT = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DZERO,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DOC_STATUS = 'O' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DOPEN,
         SUM(FROM_DELIVERY) DDLN,
         SUM(QTY_PCS) QP, SUM(QTY_OTHER) QO,
         SUM(GROSS_AMT - GST_AMT) NET, SUM(GST_AMT) GST, SUM(GROSS_AMT) GRS,
         SUM(STOCK_COST) CST,
         SUM(CASE WHEN HAS_CN = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DNOCN,
         SUM(CASE WHEN HAS_CN = 0 AND DLV_INVOICED = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DNOCNB,
         SUM(CASE WHEN HAS_CN = 0 THEN QTY_PCS ELSE 0 END) QPNOCN,
         SUM(CASE WHEN HAS_CN = 0 THEN STOCK_COST ELSE 0 END) CSTNOCN,
         SUM(CN_NET) CNN
  FROM R WHERE HAS_CN = 0
  GROUP BY CASE WHEN FROM_DELIVERY = 0 THEN 'STANDALONE_NO_LINK'
              WHEN DLV_INVOICED = 1 THEN 'FROM_DELIVERY_INVOICED'
              ELSE 'FROM_DELIVERY_UNBILLED' END
),

caveats.right: In the HANA tables the flag has THREE values: 'N' = live, 'Y' = the cancelled original, and 'C' = the system-generated cancellation mirror SAP posts to reverse it. Y and C always appear as exact matching pairs carrying the same value, so a <>'Y' test keeps every mirror and double-counts. Measured live on Oil 2026-08-21: OINV 30,387 'N' (1045.62 Cr) plus 320 'Y' and 320 'C' at 37.27 Cr each; OPCH 16,101 'N' plus 113+113 at 15.96 Cr each; OPDN 10,640 'N' plus 473+473 at 94.63 Cr each; ORDN 1,817 'N' plus 107+107 at 0.49 Cr each. Same pattern in Mart and Beverages. Always test CANCELED='N' positively. Note the Service Layer differs: it exposes only Cancelled 'tYES'/'tNO', so the documented OData filter Cancelled eq 'tNO' is already correct and is not affected.
caveats.rule: HANA "CANCELED" is three-valued: 'N' live, 'Y' cancelled original, 'C' its system mirror. Always filter CANCELED='N' - a <>'Y' test keeps the mirrors and double-counts (Oil OPDN +94.63 Cr).
caveats.title: HANA CANCELED is three-valued — filter ='N', never <>'Y'
caveats.wrong: Excluded cancelled documents in HANA SQL by writing "CANCELED" <> 'Y' (or omitting the filter), assuming the flag is a two-valued Y/N.

caveats.right: There are 23 related-party customer cards across the three companies (Oil 9, Mart 8, Beverages 6). All of them are group entities, so all of them are intercompany. Exclude the whole set, not one card, and name which cards were excluded.
caveats.rule: Intercompany is 23 group CardCodes, not just CUSTA000606: Oil CUSTA000001/2/3/4/606/827/906/1099/1113, Mart CUSTA000001/827/874/875/876/877/878/926, Bev CUSTA000001/2/3/4/606/827. Exclude all; name them.
caveats.title: Intercompany is 23 group cards, not just CUSTA000606
caveats.wrong: Split external vs intercompany by excluding only CUSTA000606 (JIVO MART PVT LTD), per C-0002. That leaves every other group card counted as an outside customer — JIVO WELLNESS DL/HR/PB/HP, JIVO MART HR/DL/PB/KR/RJ/UP/ISD, JIVO BEVERAGES-CUST. June-2026 olive: Mart 'external' came out Rs 10.47 Cr excluding only CUSTA000606, against Rs 9.53 Cr excluding all eight of Mart's group cards — a Rs 1.53 Cr overstatement of outside business.

caveats.right: On the vendor side several intercompany accounts sit in ordinary trading groups, so a group-only test silently counts JIVO's own money as external trade payable. Measured live 2026-08-21: Mart VENDA000001 'JIVO WELLNESS PVT LTD' is in group PURCHASE at -20.93 Cr and is Mart's single largest payable; Mart VENDA000004 'JIVO WELLNESS PVT LTD - DL' also in PURCHASE; Oil VENDA000483 'JIVO MART PVT LTD' is in group E-COMMERCE at -2.25 Cr. Together 23.19 Cr is missed. The remaining group entities do sit in BRANCH VENDOR, so the group test is necessary but not sufficient. Correction C-0005 lists 23 intercompany CardCodes but they are all CUSTA* — it covers no vendor codes at all. Test the group AND the CardName (JIVO / AKAL), and flag the rows rather than dropping them.
caveats.rule: Intercompany vendors hide outside BRANCH groups: Mart VENDA000001 'JIVO WELLNESS' is in group PURCHASE (-20.93 Cr), Oil VENDA000483 in E-COMMERCE. Match OCRD.CardName too, never group alone.
caveats.title: Intercompany vendors hide outside the BRANCH groups — match on name too
caveats.wrong: Identified JIVO's own intercompany and branch accounts by joining OCRD to OCRG and testing GroupName LIKE '%BRANCH%', assuming that catches every group entity.

sql.text:
R_WHY AS (
  SELECT
         CASE WHEN FROM_DELIVERY = 0 THEN 'STANDALONE_NO_LINK'
              WHEN DLV_INVOICED = 1 THEN 'FROM_DELIVERY_INVOICED'
              ELSE 'FROM_DELIVERY_UNBILLED' END K,
         COUNT(*) D,
         SUM(CASE WHEN GROSS_AMT = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DZERO,
         SUM(CASE WHEN DOC_STATUS = 'O' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DOPEN,
         SUM(FROM_DELIVERY) DDLN,
         SUM(QTY_PCS) QP, SUM(QTY_OTHER) QO,
         SUM(GROSS_AMT - GST_AMT) NET, SUM(GST_AMT) GST, SUM(GROSS_AMT) GRS,
         SUM(STOCK_COST) CST,
         SUM(CASE WHEN HAS_CN = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DNOCN,
         SUM(CASE WHEN HAS_CN = 0 AND DLV_INVOICED = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DNOCNB,
         SUM(CASE WHEN HAS_CN = 0 THEN QTY_PCS ELSE 0 END) QPNOCN,
         SUM(CASE WHEN HAS_CN = 0 THEN STOCK_COST ELSE 0 END) CSTNOCN,
         SUM(CN_NET) CNN
  FROM R WHERE HAS_CN = 0
  GROUP BY CASE WHEN FROM_DELIVERY = 0 THEN 'STANDALONE_NO_LINK'
              WHEN DLV_INVOICED = 1 THEN 'FROM_DELIVERY_INVOICED'
              ELSE 'FROM_DELIVERY_UNBILLED' END
),

trn-bilty-coverage.closure_note: Terms describe how the query built this figure; they are not addends over a row set, so no arithmetic closure is asserted.
trn-bilty-coverage.formula: 100 x FILLED / DISP_DOCS on the synthetic FIELD row 'OINV.LR_NUMBER (bilty)'. The underlying column is per-book: U_BilltyNumber in Oil and Mart, U_BiltyNumber in Beverages (respelled), resolved by the UDFX shim. It is NOT U_LRNUmber, whose SAP caption is 'Bill Of Entry No.'.
trn-bilty-coverage.label: Dispatches carrying a lorry receipt (bilty) number
section_traps: THE FACET TRAP, and it is the big one. SCOPE stacks seven different aggregations into one array. Summing DISP_VAL_L over every row gives Oil Rs 4,293.43 Cr against a true Rs 925.60 Cr (4.64x), Mart 4.16x, Bev 4.83x. Summing FRT_SPEND_L gives 3.78x / 3.30x / 3.99x, because the same freight rupee is counted once on its MONTH row, once on its carrier's TRANSPORTER row and once on its vendor's FREIGHT_VENDOR row. Summing DISP_DOCS is worst of all at 14.08x / 13.38x / 14.64x. The company figure is the SINGLE row SCOPE=='TOTAL' and GRP_KEY=='ALL'.

DISP_DOCS ON A FIELD ROW IS NOT A DISPATCH COUNT - it is that field's own table's row count. Nine of the eleven FIELD rows read OINV and carry 19,332 (Oil), but ODLN.U_TransporterName carries 2,792 deliveries and OPDN.U_TransporterName carries 10,662 GRPOs. The eleven FIELD rows alone contribute 187,442 of the 272,264 you get by summing the column in Oil. A renderer that averages FILL_PCT across all eleven rows is averaging three different populations.

FILLED MEANS TWO UNRELATED THINGS. On a FIELD row it is a document count (Oil bilty: 9,393 documents). On a TRANSPORTER row it is KEYS_IN_FAM - how many distinct squashed spellings merged into that carrier family (Oil RKTANKER: 7). Charting FILLED without splitting by scope puts '9,393 documents' and '7 spellings' on the same axis. FILL_PCT, confusingly, is populated on FIELD rows only and is NULL on the TRANSPORTER rows where FILLED is populated.

TRANSPORTER (top 40) AND FREIGHT_VENDOR (top 25) ARE TOP-N SUBSETS AND NEVER FOOT. The build's own audit.json already files them as 'partial-coverage': Oil TRANSPORTER DISP_VAL_L is -36.1% against the TOTAL rollup, FREIGHT_VENDOR FRT_SPEND_L -5.4%, Mart TRANSPORTER -83.5%. Coverage of what they are actually subsets of is much better and is the number to quote: TRANSPORTER covers 98.1% / 100% / 99.3% of THIRD_PARTY dispatch value, and FREIGHT_VENDOR covers 94.6% / 97.2% / 99.6% of freight. NAMECLASS, PARTY and MONTH DO foot exactly and may be summed.

THE FREIGHT-VENDOR UNIVERSE IS NOT THE TRANSPORTER SUPPLIER GROUP, and defining it that way was the one material defect this section has had. R K TANKER SERVICE (Oil VENDA000671) bills Rs 9.45 Cr of pure road freight - every line 'TPT FREIGHT FROM SHEMLA TO SONIPAT' - and is filed under supplier group 110 PURCHASE OIL. On a group-only test that entire Rs 9.45 Cr vanished, which was MORE THAN THE WHOLE FREIGHT FIGURE the section then reported (Rs 5.20 Cr), and the page printed 'NO FREIGHT VENDOR CARD MATCHED' next to Oil's 4th-largest carrier. A card now qualifies on the group OR a road-carrier token in VENDOR_NAME; every FREIGHT_VENDOR row says which, in its NOTE. Read the group-only figure as roughly a THIRD of the truth in Oil. Do not 'clean this up' back to a group test.

FRT_SPEND_L IS FREIGHT BILLED, NOT FREIGHT COST. Freight accrued straight to the ledger by journal entry never reaches this section: Oil's twelve 2165xxx FREIGHT PAYABLE accounts created Rs 7.09 Cr of credits, 100% by manual JE, with Rs 1.00 Cr still outstanding (visible in the provisions section, not here), and account 5670001 FREIGHT AND CARTAGE OUTWARD carries far more debit than arrives through carrier A/P. The two are NOT additive - a provision is reversed when its bill lands - so never present 'A/P freight plus freight provisions' as total freight. Mart is the one book where the A/P route is close to complete on the accrual side (Rs 0.18 L of freight provision in total).

DISP_VAL_L IS DISPATCH VALUE, NOT TURNOVER. Sales returns (ORIN) are not netted off - a return does not un-dispatch a truck - and service invoices (DocType='S') are counted in: Oil Rs 5.56 Cr / 0.6%, Mart Rs 15.67 Cr / 4.9%, Bev none. None of the service invoices carries a transporter name, so they only dilute the coverage percentages; they never invent a carrier. This figure will not tie to any turnover figure elsewhere on the board and is not meant to.

'U_LRNUmber' IS NOT THE LR NUMBER. Its SAP caption in CUFD.Descr is 'Bill Of Entry No.', a customs field: filled on 39 of Oil's 19,332 dispatches, 1 of Mart's 25,186, and THE COLUMN DOES NOT EXIST AT ALL IN BEVERAGES (its row's NOTE says '(no such column in this book)', which is why its 0 must never be read as bad data entry). The real lorry receipt is the bilty, and LR_PCT is built on it. Rebuilding LR coverage on the field whose name says LR would report 0.2% instead of 48.6%.

THE UDF NAMES DIFFER BETWEEN BOOKS and are resolved by a three-branch shim: Oil and Mart spell them U_BilltyNumber / U_VehicleNoM, Beverages U_BiltyNumber / U_VechileNom. Only those two columns are shimmed. FIELDSTAT and DISP name six more UDFs literally (U_TransporterName, U_TransporterInvoice, U_DriverName, U_BiltyDate, U_BiltAmt, U_Ship_From), so a FOURTH company book missing any of them would fail at HANA compile time, not degrade gracefully. If LR_PCT and VEH_PCT ever come back 0 with a NOTE reading 'UDF SHIM MISS', the shim has missed the book - that is a broken build, not a book with no bilty numbers.

U_TransporterName IS UNVALIDATED FREE TEXT - CUFD.EditType is blank and UFD1 holds zero valid values in all three books. Oil holds 234 raw spellings, Bev 147, and among them are vehicle registration numbers and mobile numbers typed into the carrier field: Mart's THIRD_PARTY list contains '9896437186' (Rs 0.18 Cr), 'HR55Ak6402', '9958007610' and '6006399745'; Beverages' contains 'DL01LY5728', 'UP85CT2177', 'DL01LT9351', '9718858411', a bare 'A' and the literal string 'Transport Name'; Oil has a bare 'd' worth Rs 0.88 Cr. They are all scored THIRD_PARTY and all appear in the TRANSPORTER scope as carriers. This is also why GRP_LABEL is sometimes a JSON integer.

NAME_CLASS LEAKS OWN-FLEET DISPATCHES INTO THIRD_PARTY. The own-fleet test catches keys ENDING in VEHICLE or VEHICAL, so 'AMAZON VEHICLE' and 'BARU SAHIB VEHICLE' are caught - but Mart's 'Amazon vehicle pickup' (Rs 3.26 Cr on 41 invoices, its 6th largest 'carrier' by value) ends in PICKUP and is scored THIRD_PARTY, as is Beverages' plain 'BARU SAHIB'. trn-ownfleet-value is therefore a LOWER BOUND, understated by at least Rs 3.26 Cr in Mart, and Mart's carrier ranking has a customer's own truck sitting in it.

THE FAMILY COLLAPSE UNDER-MERGES, AND IT SPLITS CARRIERS AWAY FROM THEIR VENDOR CARD. Families are built by a two-sided prefix test with a 6-character floor, so spellings that are not prefixes of one another stay apart: 'Bombey Sri Nagar' (Rs 13.56 Cr) and 'Bombe Sri Nagar' (Rs 1.90 Cr) are separate families from carded BOMBAYSRINAGAR; 'Mahaveer Transport' (Rs 8.12 Cr) is separate from carded MAHAVIRTRANSPORT; 'SONIPAT GOODS' (Rs 2.51 Cr) from carded SONEPATGOODS. Rs 26.99 Cr of Oil's Rs 34.62 Cr of 'no vendor card matched' is this - a spelling problem, not a missing vendor. Under-merging never inflates a carrier, but it does make the page tell an operator that a carrier is unbilled when the same carrier is billed one row away.

'NO FREIGHT VENDOR CARD MATCHED' AND 'NEVER BILLED' ARE DIFFERENT FACTS and the SQL keeps them as different NOTE strings on purpose. The first means the name never matched a supplier card. The second means the card exists and carries no A/P at all - Oil has exactly one, BABA MIRCHI NATH TRANSPORT CO (VENDA000745), which moved Rs 11.33 Cr of goods and has never been billed. Conflating them turns a genuine unbilled-carrier finding into a name-matching complaint.

VARIANTS IS ADDITIVE ACROSS NAMECLASS AND NOT ACROSS MONTH. The four NAMECLASS rows partition the spellings and sum exactly to the TOTAL (Oil 196+32+6+0 = 234). Months share spellings, so Oil's 23 MONTH rows sum to 821, Mart's to 65 and Bev's to 416. A 'transporters used' figure built by totalling the month column overstates Oil 3.5x.

FRT_DOCS COUNTS A/P INVOICES ONLY. A/P credit notes contribute 0 to the count while still subtracting from FRT_SPEND_L (sql line 228), so a period with heavy freight credit notes shows fewer documents than the money implies, and average-bill-value computed as FRT_SPEND_L / FRT_DOCS is biased low. Bev's 2026-08 MONTH row has FRT_DOCS 1 and FRT_SPEND_L 0.00 - a real zero, not a missing value.

THE MONTH ROW'S FREIGHT IS DRIVEN OFF DISPATCH MONTHS. MONTH rows come from grouping the dispatch population, and freight is attached by a correlated subquery on the same YM - so a freight bill booked in a month with NO dispatches has no cell to land in and silently disappears from the month series. It happens to reconcile today (Oil 1,802.06 L both ways, Mart 325.72 vs 325.73, Bev 203.03 vs 203.04), and Mart's 2024-12 row already shows the shape of the failure with a NULL freight cell. The TOTAL row, not the month series, is the authority on freight.

THE TWO SIDES OF FRT_PCT_OF_DISP ARE DATED INDEPENDENTLY. A freight bill is dated when it is booked, not when the truck ran, so the monthly ratio swings hard on small books - Beverages moves between 1.7% and 28.6% in adjacent months. Read it as a trend; never quote a month's figure as a per-consignment rate or use it to price a lane.

caveats.right: In SAP B1 a blank is usually a value living somewhere else, not a missing value. Before reporting any blank, absence or exception as a defect, run the disconfirming query first: does the value legitimately sit in a paired column (HSN vs SAC), in another company book (Oil vs Mart vs Beverages), or at a different level (invoice vs customer master, as with GSTIN)? And before quoting a count, confirm the unit - add-on and error tables write multiple rows per document, so COUNT(*) is not an invoice count. Verifying that a total adds up says nothing about whether the right rows were included.
caveats.rule: A blank in SAP usually means the value lives elsewhere. Before calling it a defect check the paired column, the other company books, and the document vs master level - and confirm COUNT(*) counts documents, not add-on rows.
caveats.title: A blank field is not a defect until you check where the value legitimately lives
caveats.wrong: Three wrong figures were reported to a senior operator in one week, all from the same habit: form a hypothesis, run the query that confirms it, never run the query that would kill it. (1) 157 lines / Rs 4.94 Cr called 'missing HSN' - the HSN column was checked, the paired SAC column was not; real defect was 3 lines / Rs 1.07 Cr, wrong by 50x. (2) A HoReCa segment total that silently omitted Rs 1.20 Cr because the same customer is tagged differently in the Oil and Mart books. (3) 2,122 'problem invoices' that were raw add-on error rows, not invoices; real figure 32. In every case the arithmetic was re-verified and reported as 'all figures verify' - which was true and irrelevant, because the sum was right and the population was wrong. Checking the maths created false confidence.

caveats.right: In the HANA tables the flag has THREE values: 'N' = live, 'Y' = the cancelled original, and 'C' = the system-generated cancellation mirror SAP posts to reverse it. Y and C always appear as exact matching pairs carrying the same value, so a <>'Y' test keeps every mirror and double-counts. Measured live on Oil 2026-08-21: OINV 30,387 'N' (1045.62 Cr) plus 320 'Y' and 320 'C' at 37.27 Cr each; OPCH 16,101 'N' plus 113+113 at 15.96 Cr each; OPDN 10,640 'N' plus 473+473 at 94.63 Cr each; ORDN 1,817 'N' plus 107+107 at 0.49 Cr each. Same pattern in Mart and Beverages. Always test CANCELED='N' positively. Note the Service Layer differs: it exposes only Cancelled 'tYES'/'tNO', so the documented OData filter Cancelled eq 'tNO' is already correct and is not affected.
caveats.rule: HANA "CANCELED" is three-valued: 'N' live, 'Y' cancelled original, 'C' its system mirror. Always filter CANCELED='N' - a <>'Y' test keeps the mirrors and double-counts (Oil OPDN +94.63 Cr).
caveats.title: HANA CANCELED is three-valued — filter ='N', never <>'Y'
caveats.wrong: Excluded cancelled documents in HANA SQL by writing "CANCELED" <> 'Y' (or omitting the filter), assuming the flag is a two-valued Y/N.

GRP_LABEL IS NOT ALWAYS A STRING. On the rows where a phone number was typed into the transporter field, JSON serialises GRP_LABEL as an integer - 3 rows in Mart, 1 in Bev. sql.text:
BASE AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS DOCS, SUM(NET_VAL) AS VAL,
         SUM(IS_EXT) AS EXT_DOCS, SUM(IS_EXT*NET_VAL) AS EXT_VAL,
         SUM(CASE WHEN NAME_CLASS='THIRD_PARTY' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS TP_DOCS,
         SUM(HAS_LR) AS LRN, SUM(HAS_VEH) AS VEHN, SUM(HAS_DRV) AS DRVN, SUM(HAS_BOE) AS BOEN,
         COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN TN_RAW<>'' THEN TN_RAW END) AS RAWVAR,
         COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN NAME_CLASS='THIRD_PARTY' THEN TN_RAW END) AS TPVAR
  FROM D
),

terms.label: Live A/R invoices, ex-migration
terms.note: Oil 19,332 of 30,410 uncancelled invoices - the other 11,078 are the 2024-09-30 go-live load. Mart 25,186, Bev 5,331, neither of which has any row on that date.

caveats.right: In the HANA tables the flag has THREE values: 'N' = live, 'Y' = the cancelled original, and 'C' = the system-generated cancellation mirror SAP posts to reverse it. Y and C always appear as exact matching pairs carrying the same value, so a <>'Y' test keeps every mirror and double-counts. Measured live on Oil 2026-08-21: OINV 30,387 'N' (1045.62 Cr) plus 320 'Y' and 320 'C' at 37.27 Cr each; OPCH 16,101 'N' plus 113+113 at 15.96 Cr each; OPDN 10,640 'N' plus 473+473 at 94.63 Cr each; ORDN 1,817 'N' plus 107+107 at 0.49 Cr each. Same pattern in Mart and Beverages. Always test CANCELED='N' positively. Note the Service Layer differs: it exposes only Cancelled 'tYES'/'tNO', so the documented OData filter Cancelled eq 'tNO' is already correct and is not affected.
caveats.rule: HANA "CANCELED" is three-valued: 'N' live, 'Y' cancelled original, 'C' its system mirror. Always filter CANCELED='N' - a <>'Y' test keeps the mirrors and double-counts (Oil OPDN +94.63 Cr).
caveats.title: HANA CANCELED is three-valued — filter ='N', never <>'Y'
caveats.wrong: Excluded cancelled documents in HANA SQL by writing "CANCELED" <> 'Y' (or omitting the filter), assuming the flag is a two-valued Y/N.

caveats.right: There are 23 related-party customer cards across the three companies (Oil 9, Mart 8, Beverages 6). All of them are group entities, so all of them are intercompany. Exclude the whole set, not one card, and name which cards were excluded.
caveats.rule: Intercompany is 23 group CardCodes, not just CUSTA000606: Oil CUSTA000001/2/3/4/606/827/906/1099/1113, Mart CUSTA000001/827/874/875/876/877/878/926, Bev CUSTA000001/2/3/4/606/827. Exclude all; name them.
caveats.title: Intercompany is 23 group cards, not just CUSTA000606
caveats.wrong: Split external vs intercompany by excluding only CUSTA000606 (JIVO MART PVT LTD), per C-0002. That leaves every other group card counted as an outside customer — JIVO WELLNESS DL/HR/PB/HP, JIVO MART HR/DL/PB/KR/RJ/UP/ISD, JIVO BEVERAGES-CUST. June-2026 olive: Mart 'external' came out Rs 10.47 Cr excluding only CUSTA000606, against Rs 9.53 Cr excluding all eight of Mart's group cards — a Rs 1.53 Cr overstatement of outside business.

check.method: reproduces the figure measured independently from the SQL when the section was catalogued

trn-dispatch-value.closure_note: Terms describe how the query built this figure; they are not addends over a row set, so no arithmetic closure is asserted.

excludes.label: Cancelled invoices and their system mirrors
excludes.note: This exclusion is described in the section spec but not expressed as a filter over the published rows, so its amount cannot be computed here: 'n/a - excluded in SQL, no row survives'
excludes.why: C-0021 - CANCELED is three-valued N/Y/C; the SQL filters ='N', which correctly drops both halves of a cancellation pair. Oil OINV carries 320 'Y' and 320 'C'.

excludes.label: Go-live opening invoices dated exactly 2024-09-30
excludes.note: This exclusion is described in the section spec but not expressed as a filter over the published rows, so its amount cannot be computed here: 'n/a - excluded in SQL'
excludes.why: TRN-MIGRATION - 11,078 Oil invoices worth Rs 74.74 Cr, none carrying a transporter; leaving them in dilutes every coverage percentage by about a third. That date exists only in the Oil book.

trn-dispatch-value.formula: DISP_VAL_L x 1e5 read off the single TOTAL/ALL row. DISP_VAL_L is INR LAKHS (the _L suffix), = SUM(OINV.DocTotal - OINV.VatSum) over CANCELED='N', DocDate <= as-of, DocDate <> 2024-09-30. This is DISPATCH VALUE, not turnover: sales returns are not netted off and branch + intercompany movements are inside it.
trn-dispatch-value.label: Goods dispatched (net of GST, all parties)
section_traps: THE FACET TRAP, and it is the big one. SCOPE stacks seven different aggregations into one array. Summing DISP_VAL_L over every row gives Oil Rs 4,293.43 Cr against a true Rs 925.60 Cr (4.64x), Mart 4.16x, Bev 4.83x. Summing FRT_SPEND_L gives 3.78x / 3.30x / 3.99x, because the same freight rupee is counted once on its MONTH row, once on its carrier's TRANSPORTER row and once on its vendor's FREIGHT_VENDOR row. Summing DISP_DOCS is worst of all at 14.08x / 13.38x / 14.64x. The company figure is the SINGLE row SCOPE=='TOTAL' and GRP_KEY=='ALL'.

DISP_DOCS ON A FIELD ROW IS NOT A DISPATCH COUNT - it is that field's own table's row count. Nine of the eleven FIELD rows read OINV and carry 19,332 (Oil), but ODLN.U_TransporterName carries 2,792 deliveries and OPDN.U_TransporterName carries 10,662 GRPOs. The eleven FIELD rows alone contribute 187,442 of the 272,264 you get by summing the column in Oil. A renderer that averages FILL_PCT across all eleven rows is averaging three different populations.

FILLED MEANS TWO UNRELATED THINGS. On a FIELD row it is a document count (Oil bilty: 9,393 documents). On a TRANSPORTER row it is KEYS_IN_FAM - how many distinct squashed spellings merged into that carrier family (Oil RKTANKER: 7). Charting FILLED without splitting by scope puts '9,393 documents' and '7 spellings' on the same axis. FILL_PCT, confusingly, is populated on FIELD rows only and is NULL on the TRANSPORTER rows where FILLED is populated.

TRANSPORTER (top 40) AND FREIGHT_VENDOR (top 25) ARE TOP-N SUBSETS AND NEVER FOOT. The build's own audit.json already files them as 'partial-coverage': Oil TRANSPORTER DISP_VAL_L is -36.1% against the TOTAL rollup, FREIGHT_VENDOR FRT_SPEND_L -5.4%, Mart TRANSPORTER -83.5%. Coverage of what they are actually subsets of is much better and is the number to quote: TRANSPORTER covers 98.1% / 100% / 99.3% of THIRD_PARTY dispatch value, and FREIGHT_VENDOR covers 94.6% / 97.2% / 99.6% of freight. NAMECLASS, PARTY and MONTH DO foot exactly and may be summed.

sql.text:
DISP AS (
  SELECT h."DocEntry" AS DOC_ENTRY,
         TO_VARCHAR(h."DocDate",'YYYY-MM') AS YM,
         TRIM(IFNULL(h."U_TransporterName",'')) AS TN_RAW,
         REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(
           UPPER(TRIM(IFNULL(h."U_TransporterName",''))),
           ' ',''),'.',''),',',''),'-',''),'&',''),'(',''),')',''),'/',''),'''',''),'_',''),'%','') AS TN_KEY,
         CASE WHEN IFNULL(TRIM(h."U_DriverName"),'')          <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS HAS_DRV,
         CAST(h."DocTotal" AS DOUBLE) - CAST(h."VatSum" AS DOUBLE) AS NET_VAL,
         CASE WHEN UPPER(IFNULL(g."GroupName",'')) LIKE '%BRANCH%'            THEN 'BRANCH'
              WHEN UPPER(IFNULL(c."CardName",h."CardName")) LIKE '%JIVO%'     THEN 'INTERCOMPANY'
              ELSE 'EXTERNAL' END AS PARTY_CLASS
  FROM {{SCHEMA}}.OINV h
  LEFT JOIN {{SCHEMA}}.OCRD c ON c."CardCode"  = h."CardCode"
  LEFT JOIN {{SCHEMA}}.OCRG g ON g."GroupCode" = c."GroupCode" AND g."GroupType" = c."CardType"
  WHERE h."CANCELED" = 'N'
    AND h."DocDate" <= DATE'{{ASOF}}'
    AND h."DocDate" <> DATE'2024-09-30'
),

section_traps: THE FACET TRAP, and it is the big one. SCOPE stacks seven different aggregations into one array. Summing DISP_VAL_L over every row gives Oil Rs 4,293.43 Cr against a true Rs 925.60 Cr (4.64x), Mart 4.16x, Bev 4.83x. Summing FRT_SPEND_L gives 3.78x / 3.30x / 3.99x, because the same freight rupee is counted once on its MONTH row, once on its carrier's TRANSPORTER row and once on its vendor's FREIGHT_VENDOR row. Summing DISP_DOCS is worst of all at 14.08x / 13.38x / 14.64x. The company figure is the SINGLE row SCOPE=='TOTAL' and GRP_KEY=='ALL'.

DISP_DOCS ON A FIELD ROW IS NOT A DISPATCH COUNT - it is that field's own table's row count. Nine of the eleven FIELD rows read OINV and carry 19,332 (Oil), but ODLN.U_TransporterName carries 2,792 deliveries and OPDN.U_TransporterName carries 10,662 GRPOs. The eleven FIELD rows alone contribute 187,442 of the 272,264 you get by summing the column in Oil. A renderer that averages FILL_PCT across all eleven rows is averaging three different populations.

FILLED MEANS TWO UNRELATED THINGS. On a FIELD row it is a document count (Oil bilty: 9,393 documents). On a TRANSPORTER row it is KEYS_IN_FAM - how many distinct squashed spellings merged into that carrier family (Oil RKTANKER: 7). Charting FILLED without splitting by scope puts '9,393 documents' and '7 spellings' on the same axis. FILL_PCT, confusingly, is populated on FIELD rows only and is NULL on the TRANSPORTER rows where FILLED is populated.

TRANSPORTER (top 40) AND FREIGHT_VENDOR (top 25) ARE TOP-N SUBSETS AND NEVER FOOT. The build's own audit.json already files them as 'partial-coverage': Oil TRANSPORTER DISP_VAL_L is -36.1% against the TOTAL rollup, FREIGHT_VENDOR FRT_SPEND_L -5.4%, Mart TRANSPORTER -83.5%. Coverage of what they are actually subsets of is much better and is the number to quote: TRANSPORTER covers 98.1% / 100% / 99.3% of THIRD_PARTY dispatch value, and FREIGHT_VENDOR covers 94.6% / 97.2% / 99.6% of freight. NAMECLASS, PARTY and MONTH DO foot exactly and may be summed.

THE FREIGHT-VENDOR UNIVERSE IS NOT THE TRANSPORTER SUPPLIER GROUP, and defining it that way was the one material defect this section has had. R K TANKER SERVICE (Oil VENDA000671) bills Rs 9.45 Cr of pure road freight - every line 'TPT FREIGHT FROM SHEMLA TO SONIPAT' - and is filed under supplier group 110 PURCHASE OIL. On a group-only test that entire Rs 9.45 Cr vanished, which was MORE THAN THE WHOLE FREIGHT FIGURE the section then reported (Rs 5.20 Cr), and the page printed 'NO FREIGHT VENDOR CARD MATCHED' next to Oil's 4th-largest carrier. A card now qualifies on the group OR a road-carrier token in VENDOR_NAME; every FREIGHT_VENDOR row says which, in its NOTE. Read the group-only figure as roughly a THIRD of the truth in Oil. Do not 'clean this up' back to a group test.

FRT_SPEND_L IS FREIGHT BILLED, NOT FREIGHT COST. Freight accrued straight to the ledger by journal entry never reaches this section: Oil's twelve 2165xxx FREIGHT PAYABLE accounts created Rs 7.09 Cr of credits, 100% by manual JE, with Rs 1.00 Cr still outstanding (visible in the provisions section, not here), and account 5670001 FREIGHT AND CARTAGE OUTWARD carries far more debit than arrives through carrier A/P. The two are NOT additive - a provision is reversed when its bill lands - so never present 'A/P freight plus freight provisions' as total freight. Mart is the one book where the A/P route is close to complete on the accrual side (Rs 0.18 L of freight provision in total).

DISP_VAL_L IS DISPATCH VALUE, NOT TURNOVER. Sales returns (ORIN) are not netted off - a return does not un-dispatch a truck - and service invoices (DocType='S') are counted in: Oil Rs 5.56 Cr / 0.6%, Mart Rs 15.67 Cr / 4.9%, Bev none. None of the service invoices carries a transporter name, so they only dilute the coverage percentages; they never invent a carrier. This figure will not tie to any turnover figure elsewhere on the board and is not meant to.

'U_LRNUmber' IS NOT THE LR NUMBER. Its SAP caption in CUFD.Descr is 'Bill Of Entry No.', a customs field: filled on 39 of Oil's 19,332 dispatches, 1 of Mart's 25,186, and THE COLUMN DOES NOT EXIST AT ALL IN BEVERAGES (its row's NOTE says '(no such column in this book)', which is why its 0 must never be read as bad data entry). The real lorry receipt is the bilty, and LR_PCT is built on it. Rebuilding LR coverage on the field whose name says LR would report 0.2% instead of 48.6%.

THE UDF NAMES DIFFER BETWEEN BOOKS and are resolved by a three-branch shim: Oil and Mart spell them U_BilltyNumber / U_VehicleNoM, Beverages U_BiltyNumber / U_VechileNom. Only those two columns are shimmed. FIELDSTAT and DISP name six more UDFs literally (U_TransporterName, U_TransporterInvoice, U_DriverName, U_BiltyDate, U_BiltAmt, U_Ship_From), so a FOURTH company book missing any of them would fail at HANA compile time, not degrade gracefully. If LR_PCT and VEH_PCT ever come back 0 with a NOTE reading 'UDF SHIM MISS', the shim has missed the book - that is a broken build, not a book with no bilty numbers.

U_TransporterName IS UNVALIDATED FREE TEXT - CUFD.EditType is blank and UFD1 holds zero valid values in all three books. Oil holds 234 raw spellings, Bev 147, and among them are vehicle registration numbers and mobile numbers typed into the carrier field: Mart's THIRD_PARTY list contains '9896437186' (Rs 0.18 Cr), 'HR55Ak6402', '9958007610' and '6006399745'; Beverages' contains 'DL01LY5728', 'UP85CT2177', 'DL01LT9351', '9718858411', a bare 'A' and the literal string 'Transport Name'; Oil has a bare 'd' worth Rs 0.88 Cr. They are all scored THIRD_PARTY and all appear in the TRANSPORTER scope as carriers. This is also why GRP_LABEL is sometimes a JSON integer.

NAME_CLASS LEAKS OWN-FLEET DISPATCHES INTO THIRD_PARTY. The own-fleet test catches keys ENDING in VEHICLE or VEHICAL, so 'AMAZON VEHICLE' and 'BARU SAHIB VEHICLE' are caught - but Mart's 'Amazon vehicle pickup' (Rs 3.26 Cr on 41 invoices, its 6th largest 'carrier' by value) ends in PICKUP and is scored THIRD_PARTY, as is Beverages' plain 'BARU SAHIB'. trn-ownfleet-value is therefore a LOWER BOUND, understated by at least Rs 3.26 Cr in Mart, and Mart's carrier ranking has a customer's own truck sitting in it.

THE FAMILY COLLAPSE UNDER-MERGES, AND IT SPLITS CARRIERS AWAY FROM THEIR VENDOR CARD. Families are built by a two-sided prefix test with a 6-character floor, so spellings that are not prefixes of one another stay apart: 'Bombey Sri Nagar' (Rs 13.56 Cr) and 'Bombe Sri Nagar' (Rs 1.90 Cr) are separate families from carded BOMBAYSRINAGAR; 'Mahaveer Transport' (Rs 8.12 Cr) is separate from carded MAHAVIRTRANSPORT; 'SONIPAT GOODS' (Rs 2.51 Cr) from carded SONEPATGOODS. Rs 26.99 Cr of Oil's Rs 34.62 Cr of 'no vendor card matched' is this - a spelling problem, not a missing vendor. Under-merging never inflates a carrier, but it does make the page tell an operator that a carrier is unbilled when the same carrier is billed one row away.

'NO FREIGHT VENDOR CARD MATCHED' AND 'NEVER BILLED' ARE DIFFERENT FACTS and the SQL keeps them as different NOTE strings on purpose. The first means the name never matched a supplier card. The second means the card exists and carries no A/P at all - Oil has exactly one, BABA MIRCHI NATH TRANSPORT CO (VENDA000745), which moved Rs 11.33 Cr of goods and has never been billed. Conflating them turns a genuine unbilled-carrier finding into a name-matching complaint.

VARIANTS IS ADDITIVE ACROSS NAMECLASS AND NOT ACROSS MONTH. The four NAMECLASS rows partition the spellings and sum exactly to the TOTAL (Oil 196+32+6+0 = 234). Months share spellings, so Oil's 23 MONTH rows sum to 821, Mart's to 65 and Bev's to 416. A 'transporters used' figure built by totalling the month column overstates Oil 3.5x.

FRT_DOCS COUNTS A/P INVOICES ONLY. A/P credit notes contribute 0 to the count while still subtracting from FRT_SPEND_L (sql line 228), so a period with heavy freight credit notes shows fewer documents than the money implies, and average-bill-value computed as FRT_SPEND_L / FRT_DOCS is biased low. Bev's 2026-08 MONTH row has FRT_DOCS 1 and FRT_SPEND_L 0.00 - a real zero, not a missing value.

THE MONTH ROW'S FREIGHT IS DRIVEN OFF DISPATCH MONTHS. MONTH rows come from grouping the dispatch population, and freight is attached by a correlated subquery on the same YM - so a freight bill booked in a month with NO dispatches has no cell to land in and silently disappears from the month series. It happens to reconcile today (Oil 1,802.06 L both ways, Mart 325.72 vs 325.73, Bev 203.03 vs 203.04), and Mart's 2024-12 row already shows the shape of the failure with a NULL freight cell. The TOTAL row, not the month series, is the authority on freight.

THE TWO SIDES OF FRT_PCT_OF_DISP ARE DATED INDEPENDENTLY. A freight bill is dated when it is booked, not when the truck ran, so the monthly ratio swings hard on small books - Beverages moves between 1.7% and 28.6% in adjacent months. Read it as a trend; never quote a month's figure as a per-consignment rate or use it to price a lane.

FRT_PCT_OF_DISP IS ROUNDED TO 1 DECIMAL AND HAS ALREADY MOVED. Oil's TOTAL row currently prints 1.9 where pipeline/notes/transporter.md and README.md both quote 2.0% - the true ratio slipped from 1.9507 to 1.9469 on one extra day of dispatches. Compute the percentage from FRT_SPEND_L and DISP_VAL_L rather than reading the rounded column, and never quote the notes' figure as live.

THE PIPELINE NOTES ARE A BUILD BEHIND. pipeline/notes/transporter.md records as-of 2026-08-21 (Oil 19,309 docs / 92,379.73 L / freight 2.0% of dispatch); the live slice is as-of 2026-08-22 (19,332 docs / 92,560.36 L / 1.9%). Every figure in that file is a lead, not a live number - re-derive from the slice before publishing anything.

EVERY MONEY COLUMN ENDS _L AND IS LAKHS, rounded to 2 decimals. So the finest resolution the section can express is Rs 100, and any cross-check tolerance must be at least Rs 500 (Oil's headline reads Rs 9,256,036,000 against return-note's Rs 9,256,036,260.99). Multiply by 1e5 for rupees, and multiply exactly once - the *_PCT columns are already 0-100 and DISP_DOCS / FRT_DOCS / FILLED / VARIANTS are counts.

THE 2024-09-30 EXCLUSION IS OIL-ONLY AND IS NOT APPLIED CONSISTENTLY. Oil has 11,078 live invoices dated exactly that day (Rs 74.74 Cr of go-live openings, none carrying a transporter); Mart and Bev have zero rows on that date in OINV, OPCH, ORPC and ODLN, so the filter is a no-op for them. But the ODLN branch of FIELDSTAT (sql line 324) omits the date exclusion that every other branch carries. The effect is almost certainly nil - I did not measure ODLN rows on 2024-09-30 - and it means the ODLN fill rate is computed on a marginally different population from the OINV ones.

GROUP TOTALS ARE NOT ELIMINATED. Adding oil + mart + bev double counts JIVO's inter-book movement - Oil's Rs 305.64 Cr of dispatches to CUSTA000606 JIVO MART is the mirror of Mart's own inward stock. Per-company is the figure that means something, and the PARTY scope exists so the reader can see exactly how much would be double counted (Oil 40.9% of its headline).

THE PARTY CLASSIFIER IS A HEURISTIC, NOT A REGISTER: group name contains BRANCH, or card name contains JIVO. It catches all 23 of C-0005's settled intercompany CardCodes today - nine by group, the rest only by name, including CUSTA000606 JIVO MART which sits in card group 'DELHI' - but a new group entity named otherwise would score EXTERNAL and inflate the trade figure silently. Unlike the vendor side of the board there is no STAFF class here at all.

DO NOT TOTAL THE DETAIL GRID'S FREIGHT COLUMN. transporter-detail.sql discloses it in its own header and the live numbers confirm it: the grid carries Oil Rs 10.12 Cr against the Rs 18.02 Cr this section reports, Mart Rs 0.66 Cr against Rs 3.26 Cr, Bev Rs 1.85 Cr against Rs 2.03 Cr. Two structural causes, both inherent to the (family, month) grain: families outside the top 20 fold into ZZ_OTHER, whose freight is NULL by design, and a bill booked in a month that carrier did not dispatch in has no cell. The grid's DISPATCH columns, by contrast, foot exactly to the THIRD_PARTY row and are safe.

ZZ_OTHER IS IN THE DETAIL AND NOT IN THE SUMMARY. The detail grid carries a synthetic ZZ_OTHER family (Oil 23 rows / Rs 56.24 Cr, Bev 23 rows / Rs 0.44 Cr, Mart none) so its months still foot to the third-party total. It is not a carrier, it has no vendor card and its freight is deliberately NULL. Joining detail rows to summary TRANSPORTER rows on FAM_KEY silently drops it, which is correct for a carrier list and wrong for a total.

GRP_LABEL IS NOT ALWAYS A STRING. On the rows where a phone number was typed into the transporter field, JSON serialises GRP_LABEL as an integer - 3 rows in Mart, 1 in Bev. Any .upper(), .startswith() or string slice on it will raise. Coerce with str() first. SORT_KEY, by contrast, is always a string even though it holds 1..7.

The real lorry receipt is the bilty, and LR_PCT is built on it. Rebuilding LR coverage on the field whose name says LR would report 0.2% instead of 48.6%.

THE MONTH ROW'S FREIGHT IS DRIVEN OFF DISPATCH MONTHS. THE PIPELINE NOTES ARE A BUILD BEHIND. pipeline/notes/transporter.md records as-of 2026-08-21 (Oil 19,309 docs / 92,379.73 L / freight 2.0% of dispatch); the live slice is as-of 2026-08-22 (19,332 docs / 92,560.36 L / 1.9%). Every figure in that file is a lead, not a live number - re-derive from the slice before publishing anything.

EVERY MONEY COLUMN ENDS _L AND IS LAKHS, rounded to 2 decimals. So the finest resolution the section can express is Rs 100, and any cross-check tolerance must be at least Rs 500 (Oil's headline reads Rs 9,256,036,000 against return-note's Rs 9,256,036,260.99). Multiply by 1e5 for rupees, and multiply exactly once - the *_PCT columns are already 0-100 and DISP_DOCS / FRT_DOCS / FILLED / VARIANTS are counts.

THE 2024-09-30 EXCLUSION IS OIL-ONLY AND IS NOT APPLIED CONSISTENTLY. GROUP TOTALS ARE NOT ELIMINATED. Adding oil + mart + bev double counts JIVO's inter-book movement - Oil's Rs 305.64 Cr of dispatches to CUSTA000606 JIVO MART is the mirror of Mart's own inward stock. GRP_LABEL IS NOT ALWAYS A STRING. On the rows where a phone number was typed into the transporter field, JSON serialises GRP_LABEL as an integer - 3 rows in Mart, 1 in Bev. section_traps: THE FACET TRAP, and it is the big one. SCOPE stacks seven different aggregations into one array. Summing DISP_VAL_L over every row gives Oil Rs 4,293.43 Cr against a true Rs 925.60 Cr (4.64x), Mart 4.16x, Bev 4.83x. Summing FRT_SPEND_L gives 3.78x / 3.30x / 3.99x, because the same freight rupee is counted once on its MONTH row, once on its carrier's TRANSPORTER row and once on its vendor's FREIGHT_VENDOR row. Summing DISP_DOCS is worst of all at 14.08x / 13.38x / 14.64x. The company figure is the SINGLE row SCOPE=='TOTAL' and GRP_KEY=='ALL'.

DISP_DOCS ON A FIELD ROW IS NOT A DISPATCH COUNT - it is that field's own table's row count. Nine of the eleven FIELD rows read OINV and carry 19,332 (Oil), but ODLN.U_TransporterName carries 2,792 deliveries and OPDN.U_TransporterName carries 10,662 GRPOs. The eleven FIELD rows alone contribute 187,442 of the 272,264 you get by summing the column in Oil. A renderer that averages FILL_PCT across all eleven rows is averaging three different populations.

FILLED MEANS TWO UNRELATED THINGS. On a FIELD row it is a document count (Oil bilty: 9,393 documents). On a TRANSPORTER row it is KEYS_IN_FAM - how many distinct squashed spellings merged into that carrier family (Oil RKTANKER: 7). Charting FILLED without splitting by scope puts '9,393 documents' and '7 spellings' on the same axis. FILL_PCT, confusingly, is populated on FIELD rows only and is NULL on the TRANSPORTER rows where FILLED is populated.

NAMECLASS, PARTY and MONTH DO foot exactly and may be summed.

The two are NOT additive - a provision is reversed when its bill lands - so never present 'A/P freight plus freight provisions' as total freight. Mart is the one book where the A/P route is close to complete on the accrual side (Rs 0.18 L of freight provision in total).

sql.text:
SELECT 'FREIGHT_VENDOR', v.CARD_CODE, v.CARD_NAME, 7,
         NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL,
         v.CARD_CODE, v.CARD_NAME, v.FDOCS, v.FAMT, NULL,
         CASE WHEN v.IN_GRP = 1 THEN '' ELSE
              'OUTSIDE the transporter group -- filed under "' || v.GRP_NAME
              || '", pulled in on the carrier token in its name; ' END
         || CASE WHEN v.FAM_KEY IS NULL THEN 'PAID BUT NEVER NAMED ON A DISPATCH'
                 ELSE 'ships under transporter family "' || v.FAM_KEY || '"' END
  FROM (SELECT f.CARD_CODE, ve.CARD_NAME, ve.GRP_NAME, ve.IN_GRP, f.FDOCS, f.FAMT, m.FAM_KEY,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY f.FAMT DESC, f.CARD_CODE) AS RN
        FROM FRTV f
        JOIN VEND ve ON ve.CARD_CODE = f.CARD_CODE
        LEFT JOIN VMAP m ON m.CARD_CODE = f.CARD_CODE) v
  WHERE v.RN <= 25

terms.note: Mart is the finding: 17 of its 25 shown freight vendors have never been typed onto a dispatch, worth Rs 2.12 Cr of its Rs 3.17 Cr shown freight (67%). Its two largest carriers by spend - OM LOGISTICS SUPPLY CHAIN Rs 0.76 Cr and OM LOGISTICS LTD Rs 0.51 Cr - appear nowhere in its dispatch data. Oil is Rs 1.48 Cr on 7 cards, Bev Rs 0.02 Cr on 2.

THIS IS THE SHOWN-SET FIGURE (top 25 vendors only); the uncapped total is stated in the TOTAL row's NOTE: Oil 32 carriers worth Rs 12.82 Cr, Mart 14 worth Rs 0.36 Cr, Bev 12 worth Rs 0.35 Cr.
